headline: West Bengal government to appoint coordinators for all 209 wards in Kolkata: Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar
content: Kolkata Union Minister of State and Bharatiya Janata Party MP Sukanta Majumdar on Saturday (November 21) said that they are preparing to appoint coordinators for all 209 wards in Kolkata. Also read | Feuds, factions and allegations of extortion: BJP’s problem of plenty in West Bengal | Explained https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/west-bengal/feuds-factions-and-allegations-of-extortion-bjps-problem-of-plenty-in-west-bengal-explained/article71710758.ece The announcement by the senior BJP leader from West Bengal, who has been entrusted with responsibility for the civic polls by the party, comes as elections to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) remain suspended after a stay by the Calcutta High Court. “We are preparing for all 209 wards. If needed, we will appoint coordinators in 209 wards. Appointing a coordinator is a temporary matter, so there should be no legal issue in it,” Mr. Majumdar said. Only a day before. Mr. Majumdar had said that they would appoint coordinators in the 144 wards, which was the number of wards before delimitation. Calcutta High Court had granted a stay on the announcement of dates of civic polls on a petition challenging that delimitation was not done as per established norms. Opposition raises alarm Meanwhile, the Opposition have raised alarm over the BJP appointing its own people as civic body coordinators instead of legally appointing elected representatives. “BJP people becoming coordinators is unacceptable. If BJP people want to come to power, get elected and take the seats or increase the tenure of the previously elected representatives, or appoint government representatives,” Mamata-Trinamool Congress MLA Kunal Ghosh said. Communist Party of India (Marxist) leader Sujan Chakraborty said that this is the BJP using backdoor methods to get BJP people at the top of the civic bodies as coordinators and control the Corporation. “This is the backdoor policy to control the KMC, and it is a forceful acquisition of the civic body without a free and fair election,” Congress State general secretary Ashutosh Chatterjee told The Hindu on Saturday (November 21, 2026). Civic polls chaos On August 22, KMC published a draft list of 209 wards, increasing it from 144 wards. The Calcutta High Court on November 6 had restrained the West Bengal State Election Commission from issuing any notification for the KMC elections based on newly redrawn wards until a pending petition challenging the delimitation exercise is decided. The State government has filed a petition with the Supreme Court to ask it to lift the ban on holding the civic polls. The top court is likely to hear the matter of the KMC ward delimitation and civic poll petition on Monday (November 23). The last KMC election was held in 2021, in which the Trinamool Congress won 134 seats out of 144. The Trinamool Congress board at KMC was dissolved weeks after the BJP came to power in West Bengal on May 4, 2026. KMC Mayor Firhad Hakim resigned from his post, stating that he wanted a dignified exit from the post as the civic body has become “practically defunct” after the regime change in the State.

headline: TVK is seeking help of Centre, Congress to remain in power, says former Minister
content: DHARMAPURI Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has squandered an opportunity to persuade Congress leader Sonia Gandhi to intervene in the Mekedatu dam issue, said AIADMK leader R.B. Udhayakumar here on Saturday. He was speaking on the sidelines of the Jayalalithaa Peravai meeting. The former Minister is the front’s State secretary. “Mr. Vijay was accorded the significance that was denied even to Congress Chief Ministers at Ms. Gandhi’s book launch. Yet, he went there and returned without so much as broaching the topic of Mekedatu with Ms. Gandhi,” Mr. Udhayakumar said. He also pointed out that the TVK did not have the 118 seats required to secure a majority and alleged that the relationship between the allies had soured. Mr. Vijay was seeking the help of the Union government and the Congress to stay in power, he alleged. Criticising the State’s law and order situation over the past six months, Mr. Udhayakumar recalled Mr. Vijay’s remarks targeting DMK leader and former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin over law and order during the latter’s tenure. The AIADMK leader said the State had been pushed backward by six years, thanks to the inefficiency of the Chief Minister and his Ministers, who lacked experience. The rise in crimes against women and children and circulation of drugs, as well as the custodial deaths were indicators of the failure of the government, which was still trying to get a foothold in administration, Mr. Udhayakumar alleged.

headline: Karnataka Cabinet clears 15 lakh free sites, one lakh houses
content: Bengaluru The Karnataka Cabinet has approved the distribution of 15 lakh free residential sites to landless families and construction of one lakh houses during 2026-27 at an estimated cost of ₹2,241 crore. The decisions were taken at the Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on November 19. The initiatives aim to provide housing security to families without residential sites and those unable to afford house construction. Karnataka to build 30,000 houses for industrial workers under ‘Shramik Nivas’ scheme Karnataka to build 30,000 houses for industrial workers under ‘Shramik Nivas’ scheme Karnataka to build 30,000 houses for industrial workers under ‘Shramik Nivas’ scheme storyline 1 Under the proposed Bhooguarantee scheme of the Karnataka government, the first phase will cover five lakh sites at an estimated cost of ₹1,000 crore. The government plans to develop nine lakh sites in rural areas, requiring around 45,000 acres, while five lakh urban beneficiaries will be accommodated through a G+3 housing model, according to a press release. The government has identified 23,500 acres of government land across 31 districts, sufficient for about 4.70 lakh sites. District administrations have been asked to identify additional land. The first-phase development cost is estimated at ₹20,000 per site. Priority for vulnerable groups The proposed Niveshana Yojane will provide sites to eligible landless families, including ex-servicemen, with a 3% reservation for former defence personnel. Priority will also be given to senior citizens, widows, divorced persons, single mothers, persons with disabilities and transgender persons. DSS to hold rallies on June 16 seeking Karnataka Cabinet berth for H.C. Mahadevappa DSS to hold rallies on June 16 seeking Karnataka Cabinet berth for H.C. Mahadevappa Karnataka State Dalit Sangharsha Samiti has announced a Statewide rally on June 16, demanding a Cabinet berth for senior Congress leader and former Minister H.C. Mahadevappa in the proposed expansion of the State Cabinet DSS to hold rallies on June 16 seeking Karnataka Cabinet berth for H.C. Mahadevappa storyline 1 The proposed reservation includes 19.5% for Scheduled Castes and 7.5% for Scheduled Tribes. The Chief Minister has also directed officials to provide for reservation for Backward Classes. Eligible families must hold a Priority Household or Antyodaya Anna Yojana ration card. Annual family income should not exceed ₹1.20 lakh in rural areas and ₹2 lakh in urban areas. Applications will be invited online through Nadakacheri, Grama One and other government service centres, with Aadhaar-based verification to prevent duplication. The government has also decided to waive stamp duty and registration charges for beneficiaries. Digital ownership documents will be issued through the respective Tahsildars. Housing assistance increased Separately, the Cabinet approved one lakh houses under various schemes, including Basava Vasati Yojane, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Nivas Yojane and Vajpayee Urban Housing Scheme. Karnataka Cabinet hikes quota for minorities in housing schemes from 10% to 15% Karnataka Cabinet hikes quota for minorities in housing schemes from 10% to 15% Minister H.K. Patil said the decision was based on the disproportionately high number of homeless individuals among minority communities in both urban and rural areas Karnataka Cabinet hikes quota for minorities in housing schemes from 10% to 15% storyline 1 Under the Beneficiary-Led Construction model, assistance for general category beneficiaries has been increased from ₹1.20 lakh to ₹2 lakh, while SC/ST beneficiaries will receive ₹3 lakh against the earlier ₹2 lakh.

headline: Rahul Gandhi breaks from Sonia, Priyanka on Israel. Left allies hit out
content: Senior Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s support for strong ties with Israel due to “strategic interests”, while condemning both the October 7, 2023, attacks by Hamas on civilians in Israel, and Israel’s war on Gaza since, is a moderation from the party’s stand and has drawn condemnation from its allies. While both Sonia Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra have used the word “genocide” while describing Israel’s actions in Gaza, Gandhi’s remarks – during an interaction at University of Chicago this week – are, in fact, closer to the position maintained by the Indian government led by Narendra Modi, which has sought to balance ties between Israel and the Arab world. In a sharp reaction on Saturday, former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan, whose party CPI(M) is a close ally of the Congress at the Centre, said Gandhi’s remarks “expose the Congress party’s glaring hypocrisy on Palestine”. “His pro-imperialist position undermines the legacy of Nehru, whose foreign policy stood firmly against imperialism and in solidarity with the Palestinian struggle,” Vijayan posted on X. Another ally, the CPI(ML) Liberation, called for an end to India’s relationship with Israel. Describing it as a "genocidal regime", CPI (ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya said there could be no strategic relationship with a State that continued to perpetrate genocide against "children, women and common people despite global condemnation". Gandhi’s call for strong ties with Israel is also striking because the Modi government has been criticised for its perceived closeness to Israel PM Benjamin Netanyahu, whose hawkish policy has driven the war on Gaza. Modi visited Israel just days before the US and Israel launched their attacks on Iran on February 28 this year. Gandhi shared his remarks on Israel, during a conversation with Professor Robert Pape at the University of Chicago, on X. The Congress leader said: “India’s foreign policy must be guided by what is good for India… I support a strong relationship with Israel. We have strategic interests, including buying the best weapons for our armed forces.” At the same time, this “cannot mean silence on Gaza”, Gandhi said. “I condemn the October 7th attacks and the killing of innocent people. I also condemn what Israel has done in Gaza. One wrong cannot justify another… We are a nation of 1.5 billion people. No country – Israel, USA, Russia or China – should hold us back from playing our rightful role on the global stage. India must stand for what it believes in.” Gandhi’s sister and senior Congress leader Vadra has been among the most critical voices in the party when it comes to Israel. On August 12, 2025, she accused the Israeli government of committing “genocide” and said it is “shameful” that the Indian government is standing “silent” on this. She has also worn Palestine tote bags as a symbol of her support. In June, in an op-ed in The Indian Express, Sonia Gandhi wrote: “The calculus of national interest demands that we respond to the global public opinion against the Israeli regime’s genocidal actions in Gaza and its brutal displacement and dispossession of lakhs of Palestinian families in the occupied West Bank. The Modi government’s continued silence simply cannot be explained rationally or morally.” In a response to Vadra’s remarks, Israeli Ambassador to India Reuven Azar had said: “What is shameful is your deceit. Israel killed 25,000 Hamas terrorists. The terrible cost in human lives derives from Hamas’s heinous tactics of hiding behind civilians, their shooting of people trying to evacuate or receive assistance and their rocket fire… Israel facilitated 2 million tonnes of food into Gaza while Hamas tries to sequester them, thereby creating hunger. Gaza population has grown 450 per cent in the last 50 years, no genocide there. Don’t buy Hamas numbers.” The Congress itself has treaded more carefully, with its historic support for Palestine requiring a modulation after the October 7, 2023, attacks by Hamas. The Congress initially refrained from naming Hamas and using the word “terror” to describe the attacks. But party leaders like Shashi Tharoor questioned this, seeking at a meeting of the Congress Working Committee (CWC) on October 9, 2023, that a resolution be passed condemning the attacks, naming the outfit and using the word terror. While the CWC ignored the suggestion, soon afterwards, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge condemned “the brutal attacks by Hamas on the people of Israel”, adding that “the indiscriminate actions by Israel’s military forces in civilian areas, that includes a siege of the Gaza Strip and bombings in it” were also “unacceptable”. Later, the Congress joined Left parties in slamming the Modi government after India abstained from voting at the UN General Assembly on a resolution drafted by Arab states calling for an immediate truce between Israel and Hamas and demanding aid access to the Gaza Strip. In his post Saturday criticising Rahul Gandhi, Vijayan said: “At a time when Gaza is witnessing one of the most devastating genocides of our time, with thousands of innocent children among its victims, he openly advocates stronger ties with Israel and arms purchases from a state responsible for their slaughter. His attempt to strike a diplomatic balancing act in the face of this catastrophe is indefensible… There can be no balancing act when humanity is on trial.” In a Facebook post, sharing a report on Gandhi's comments, CPI (ML) Liberation leader Bhattacharya said: “Just as there could be no strategic relationship with Nazi Germany or the apartheid state of South Africa, there can be no normalising, condoning or downplaying of the genocide in Gaza or the cruel colonial occupation of Palestine by Israel.” He added: “India's existing strategic relationship with Israel, the growing Adani-led corporate trade including arms supply, and sinister use of Israel’s surveillance technology and security model has already done enough damage to India's international image, foreign policy credibility and above all the health of our own internal democracy and governance. We must end it sooner rather than later and must not rationalise it in the name of India's defence or ‘national security’ needs.”

headline: Inside BJP’s worst Zila Parishad loss in Rajasthan in three decades
content: As the ruling BJP in Rajasthan goes back to the drawing board after its rout in the Panchayati Raj polls, data shows that the party has suffered its worst performance in Zila Parishad elections in at least three decades, and its worst showing in Panchayat Samiti polls in 16 years. According to the state rural poll results declared Friday, the Congress’s vote share in the Zila Parishad polls was 5.63 percentage points higher than the BJP’s 37.77%. Prior to this the BJP’s worst performance came in 2010, when the Congress secured 5.51% more votes. (See box). Similarly, for Panchayat Samiti polls, the difference between the two parties is 5.37 percentage points, which is the third highest in the last three decades. In 2000 and 2010, the Congress vote share was higher than the BJP’s by 5.85 and 5.71 percentage points, respectively (See box). As per data with the State Election Commission (SEC), which was constituted in July 1994, the BJP has had a higher vote share in the Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad polls than the Congress only in 2015. The BJP had handed a crushing defeat to the Congress in the 2013 Assembly polls, reducing the party to its worst performance till date. Led by Vasundhara Raje, the BJP had then swept the polls, bagging 163 of the state's 200 seats as against the Congress's 21. In 2014, the Modi wave had helped the BJP storm to power at the Centre. As a result, the BJP’s vote share was 3.93 percentage points higher in the Zila Parishad polls and 2.94 percentage points higher in the Panchayat Samiti polls in 2015. However, a higher vote share does not necessarily translate into a proportionate number of zila pramukh or pradhan posts, as this depends on actual number of wins in the local seat/ward, as well as other factors. In 2020-21 for example, the Congress had a slightly higher vote share of 0.17 percentage points in the zila parishad polls but the BJP, then led by Satish Poonia as its state chief, had managed to elect 17 zila pramukhs against the Congress’s 13, while Independents were elected in three other places, out of a total of 33 districts. Following Friday's panchayat poll outcome, Congress state chief Govind Singh Dotasra said that it showed a difference of over 5 percentage points between the two parties. “You were ahead by about 2.5 percentage points in the (2023) Assembly polls. So, this means you are behind by about 7.5 percentage points now. And once the counting for the remaining four districts is done (by December), the Congress will be ahead of the BJP in terms of the vote share by 9-10 percentage points,” Dotasra said. Emphasising the contrast, he said the BJP managed to form a government in 2023 with a vote share difference of 2.5 percentage points “and now you are falling behind by 8-10 percentage points.” While the BJP has been active in Rajasthan since its formation in 1980 – the party won 32 Assembly seats that year – the panchayat polls in the state were earlier held by the Election Department and the Panchayat Department before that. Elections to Panchayati Raj institutions have been held in Rajasthan since 1960. “The first election was conducted in 1960 by the Panchayat Department. Thereafter, the 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th elections in the years 1965, 1978, 1981 and 1988 respectively were conducted by the Election Department,” as per the SEC.

headline: ‘Bihar, which once counted scams and crimes, now counts investments’: PM Modi on state’s turnaround
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Saturday that Bihar, which used to count scams and crime incidents earlier, is now counting data on investments and action taken against criminals. Speaking on the occasion of the NDA government completing one year in office, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who reached the stage in an open jeep through a central path amid the crowds, inaugurated 27 development schemes worth Rs 34,000 crore. One of these was the 9.7-km Nitish Setu, connecting Patna to North Bihar. “The new bridge is named after Nitish Kumar as a mark of respect to the former CM for his service and dedication to Bihar for the last 20 years,” Modi said in his speech. The prime minister said Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary had been carrying forward the good work of his predecessor Nitish Kumar, adding that naming the new Ganga bridge after Nitish Kumar was an acknowledgement of the former CM's service and dedication towards Bihar. "Bihar saw a ray of hope after Nitish Kumar implemented the agenda of good governance and took Bihar on the path of progress. New CM Samrat Choudhary and his team have been carrying forward the good work done by Nitish Kumar,” he said. Also referring to the just-concluded Chhath Puja, Modi said: “After having observed Chhath Puja, Bihar is observing 'vikas parv' (festival of development) with the blessings of Chhathi Maiya." Taking a dig at the RJD regime without naming anyone, Modi said: “People would recall those times when the number of scams was counted. Now, data on investments is discussed. Earlier, the number of crime incidents was counted, but now, the number of actions taken against criminals is being counted”. He said those wishing to see Bihar's progress should visit the state. The prime minister also highlighted the NDA government's achievements in Bihar over the past year. "The state government has signed MoUs for investments worth Rs 2 lakh crore. Closed sugar mills of Motihari are being reopened,” he said. He also welcomed the state government's approval for the establishment of Maa Sita Mahila Vishwavidyalaya. Modi said Vaishali, the seat of the ancient republic, was the most appropriate place to organise the event. He acknowledged the contributions of NDA allies and recalled the late Ram Vilas Paswan. NDA leaders JD(U)'s Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh and Sanjay Kumar Jha, LJP (RV) chief Chirag Paswan, RLM head Upendra Kushwaha and HAM(S) patron Jitan Ram Manjhi were present. The PM was also seen embracing Health Minister and Nitish Kumar's son Nishant Kumar. Though local Raghopur MLA Tejashwi Prasad Yadav was invited, he did not attend. Talking about the NDA government's achievements at the Centre, Modi said: "Congress only gave the slogan of Garibi Hatao; it is the NDA government that took about 50 crore people out of BPL in the last 12 years." He added that the Centre had provided houses to 42 lakh people in Bihar. Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary acknowledged his predecessor Nitish Kumar's contributions, saying: "Those who complained that there is no photograph of Nitish Kumar near the new bridge should know the bridge itself is called Nitish Setu and hence, is full of Nitish." Thanking the PM for attending the event, Choudhary said: "We started Sahyog (a grievance redressal portal) which has received 10.5 lakh applications. If an application is not disposed of within 30 days, the officers responsible face action directly from the CM's office." Of the 27 projects worth over Rs 34,000 crore inaugurated or launched by the PM on Saturday, the 9.7-km Nitish Setu, built parallel to the existing Mahatma Gandhi Setu, was the centrepiece. It is aimed at easing traffic congestion and boosting trade between Patna and North Bihar. The other projects span road connectivity, railway expansion, energy infrastructure and rural development across the state.

headline: A funeral, homecoming and a silent MP: Amritpal’s return turns into political spectacle
content: For nearly three hours on Saturday, Jallupur Khera was more than a village preparing to bid farewell to an elderly woman. It became the centre of an extraordinary public gathering, where grief, political symbolism and anticipation surrounding the return of a jailed parliamentarian converged. When Khadoor Sahib MP and Akali Dal (Waris Punjab de) chief Amritpal Singh arrived at his ancestral residence around noon to attend the cremation of his grandmother, Charan Kaur, the village was already teeming with supporters. Heavy police deployment, barricades and designated parking zones had transformed the otherwise quiet rural landscape into a heavily guarded zone. The real spectacle, however, unfolded when Amritpal boarded the tractor-trolley carrying mortal remains of his grandmother, who had passed away on November 8, to the cremation ground, around three kilometres away. As the trolley moved slowly along the village link road, supporters rushed through adjoining fields to catch a glimpse of the MP, while hundreds followed the procession on foot and in vehicles. What was meant to be a solemn funeral journey gradually acquired the appearance of a massive political procession. The 15-minute journey became a closely watched passage through a sea of people. Police personnel struggled to manage the swelling crowd as temporary barricades gave way, although the inner iron fencing at the cremation ground remained intact. To escort Amritpal safely over the final 100 metres to the cremation site, police created a special security enclosure. Once he climbed the raised cremation platform, slogans in his support rang out across the ground. Dressed in traditional attire, Amritpal acknowledged the gathering but refrained from addressing the crowd or making any overt political gesture. It was a striking contrast: a gathering resembling a political rally, presided over by a man who remained publicly silent. The visit marked Amritpal's first return to Punjab in more than three-and-a-half years. He has been lodged in Dibrugarh Central Jail in Assam since April 2023, following his arrest in connection with the Ajnala police station attack case. An Amritsar court permitted him to attend his grandmother's cremation under three-hour custodial parole, from noon to 3 pm on November 21. His participation in subsequent ceremonies was allowed through video conferencing. Charan Kaur, 84, died on November 8 following a prolonged illness. The family had deferred her cremation to enable Amritpal to attend the last rites. The appearance was significant for another reason — Amritpal was seen in public without handcuffs and was accompanied by his wife, Kirandeep Kaur. His uncle, Harjit Singh, was also permitted to attend, though he remained handcuffed throughout. Security restrictions inside the ancestral residence were particularly stringent, with visitors prohibited from carrying mobile phones or recording videos. Outside, however, there was little to contain the excitement. The gathering had a distinctly statewide character, with supporters travelling from different districts. Women and men stood along the route, many carrying flags and placards bearing Amritpal's photographs. Attendees maintained that the turnout was voluntary, with very few buses being used and most people travelling in their own vehicles at their expense. Kashmir Kaur, who travelled from Barnala district, said “the gathering reflected people's affection for Singh, whom she described as being unjustly incarcerated”. Hardev Singh from Fatehgarh Sahib said he had “never attended a political rally but felt compelled to visit Jallupur Khera simply to see the MP in person”. The massive turnout also created logistical challenges. Authorities had established multiple parking zones and attempted to regulate traffic along the four-kilometre approach stretch. Mobile internet connectivity reportedly became erratic as thousands converged on the village. Interestingly, even some police personnel on duty were seen recording videos of Amritpal on their mobile phones. The cremation also brought together several political figures, adding to the occasion's political significance. Among those present were Shiromani Akali Dal MLA Manpreet Singh Ayali, who is now with the Akali Dal (WPD), and Shiromani Akali Dal (Punar Surjit) leaders Sucha Singh Chhotepur and Santa Singh Umaidpuri. Ayali was seen travelling alongside Amritpal on the tractor-trolley. Another figure attracting attention was Punjab government Chief Engineer Jitender Singh Bhangu, who stood alongside Amritpal and his family on the main cremation platform. His presence was particularly significant given earlier allegations by the Shiromani Akali Dal that he had been working for the MP while holding a government position. Despite the charged atmosphere and the overwhelming crowd, the cremation concluded peacefully, without any reported major law-and-order incident. After the last rites, Amritpal was escorted to a local gurdwara for final prayers before being taken away in an official vehicle as his permitted time came to an end. A party leader, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the peaceful conduct of thousands of attendees demonstrated that Amritpal's presence did not pose a threat to Punjab's law and order. The leader urged authorities to take note of the public response and allow the MP to return to state to campaign in the 2027 Assembly elections.

headline: Another fissure in Mahayuti? Sena looks to expand footprint in BJP bastion of Vidarbha
content: Vidarbha, traditionally regarded as a stronghold of the BJP and RSS, is witnessing a sustained organisational push by the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena. Although part of the ruling Mahayuti alliance alongside the BJP and the Sunetra Pawar-led NCP, the Sena's recent activities across the region indicate an attempt to build an independent organisational base. For Sena workers, who share the BJP's ideological outlook but see limited opportunities for advancement within its established structure, the Sena could offer a political alternative to the BJP. As a senior Sena leader in Nagpur put it, “If you are out shopping, which billing counter will you choose? One that has ten people or the other that has 25 people?" In November, the party appointed six city unit heads to oversee Nagpur's six Assembly segments under the leadership of Sanjay Nirupam, indicating an attempt to decentralise the organisation. The induction of former Maharashtra minister and Prahar Janshakti Party chief Bachchu Kadu in April was another significant development. Kadu, who has built his political identity around farmers' issues and rural concerns, brings an established support base in the Amravati region. Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde also toured Vidarbha extensively in November. In South Nagpur, a recent induction programme saw around 250 workers from different political parties and local organisations join the Sena, according to organisers. These reportedly included workers associated with the Congress, BJP, NCP (Ajit Pawar faction) and the Aam Aadmi Party. Workers see leadership opportunity For younger workers, the attraction appears to be as much about political opportunity as ideology. The BJP's entrenched organisational network and established leadership in Vidarbha mean aspiring workers face considerable competition for prominent positions. The Sena, which is still building its structure, offers opportunities to take on responsibilities at the constituency, district and regional levels. A senior Sena leader in Nagpur said Eknath Shinde's visibility as Chief Minister and now as Deputy Chief Minister had contributed to the party's growing appeal. His public outreach and welfare initiatives, including the Ladki Bahin Yojana, had helped him connect with a wider section of people. “The Sena had repeatedly been compelled to compromise within the alliance, particularly in East Vidarbha, where the BJP has a stronger presence. Despite being part of the ruling alliance, the Sena had to adjust its political ambitions and organisational demands on several occasions,” the leader said. However, he felt East Vidarbha had not received adequate attention and that the Sena was now attempting to address this gap. The party's increased focus on Nagpur, Amravati and Gadchiroli, including visits and organisational meetings by senior leaders such as MLAs Uday Samant and Yogesh Kadam, was part of this exercise, he said. Speaking to The Indian Express, Kiran Pandav, Sena leader and Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde’s close aide, said: “Who would not want their party to grow? We welcome anyone who wants to come join us and work with the party.” Pandav was appointed the party's East Vidarbha organiser in 2023 and has been instrumental in expanding its organisational network across the region. The Sena's relatively smaller organisational footprint in the region also creates greater opportunities for aspiring workers to become office-bearers and seek electoral nominations. The party is looking to attract workers from the Congress, NCP and other parties, besides sections of the Shiv Sena (UBT), while maintaining that Hindutva should continue to guide its politics. “The focus is on acquiring leaders from the Sena (UBT) as many of their leaders feel there is no Hindutva left in it,” a leader said. The BJP, meanwhile, dismissed the development. “We are not aware of any workers joining the Sena,” a BJP leader from Nagpur said. Can expansion translate into votes? The Sena's expansion in Vidarbha has its roots in the June 2022 split in the undivided Shiv Sena. Several leaders from the region, including then MPs Krupal Tumane (Ramtek), Prataprao Jadhav (Buldhana) and Bhavana Gawali (Yavatmal-Washim), aligned with Shinde. The Election Commission (EC) subsequently recognised the Shinde faction as the official Shiv Sena in February 2023. Since then, the party has appointed office-bearers across Nagpur, Amravati, Wardha, Bhandara, Gondia, Chandrapur and Gadchiroli. However, organisational expansion comes with its own challenges. Workers joining from rival parties bring their individual ambitions and loyalties, which could create competing claims within the organisation. There is also the question of how the Sena will negotiate its ambitions with the BJP, its principal alliance partner. The 2024 Assembly results underline the imbalance between the two alliance partners. The BJP won 38 of Vidarbha's 62 seats, consolidating its position as the region's dominant political force. The Mahayuti alliance won 48 seats, while the Opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) secured 13. In Nagpur city alone, the BJP won four of the six Assembly seats, with the Congress winning the remaining two. Nagpur remains an important political centre for the BJP, with Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and Union Minister Nitin Gadkari having considerable influence. Any attempt by the Sena to consolidate independently could eventually lead to negotiations over electoral constituencies and political influence within the Mahayuti. For now, the Sena's approach appears to be one of gradual expansion rather than direct confrontation with its alliance partner. By creating organisational positions, inducting established leaders such as Bachchu Kadu and attracting younger workers, it is attempting to build a political network of its own. The real test will be whether this organisational space translates into electoral influence — and whether the Sena can offer its new entrants not just positions, but a genuine opportunity to climb the political ladder.

headline: GTA 6, Modi and the BJP’s bid to crack the Gen Z audience
content: The release of the long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI video game on November 19 is being viewed as an important global cultural moment. While gamers in India, like in the rest of the world, immerse themselves in the lives of Jason and Lucia — the game’s protagonists — in the fictional world of Leonida, in real life the game has triggered a political slugfest between the BJP and the Congress. As the game was released after being in development for 13 years, triggering an online frenzy, Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s X handle uploaded a post containing several slides, created using the game’s characteristic fonts and imagery, to sell his government’s development message and the progress the country had made in the years between GTA V and GTA VI. “Between GTA V and VI, here’s how India upgraded,” read the November 19 post, followed by images of how the country had levelled up in various aspects, from the economy and poverty alleviation to ramping up solar power generation and building the start-up ecosystem. India is playing a whole new game! — Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) November 19, 2026 Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal wrote in a post, “No cheat codes used,” taking a dig at the previous Congress government. The BJP’s official X handle also posted an animated clip inspired by the game, captioning it, “New India’s transformation dropped way before #GTAVI!” The video simulated a GTA-style character running through a city as captions appear highlighting how things had changed post-2014, including Metro expansion, Vande Bharat, PM Surya Ghar, and the widespread use of UPI. New India’s transformation dropped way before #GTAVI! 🇮🇳 — BJP (@BJP4India) November 20, 2026 Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma, whose team is quick to latch on to the latest social media trends and pop-cultural moments to push a message, uploaded a GTA-inspired image and captioned it, “GTA VI may be launching today, but Guwahati is busy unlocking its own upgrades and bonus levels. And trust us it's going to be epic.” GTA VI may be launching today, but Guwahati is busy unlocking its own upgrades and bonus levels. And trust us it's going to be epic. — Himanta Biswa Sarma (@himantabiswa) November 19, 2026 Apart from the senior BJP leaders, several state accounts of the ruling party, such as BJP Goa and BJP Uttarakhand, also joined the trend. Targeting the PM, Congress’s communications head Jairam Ramesh wrote on X, “The PM in a desperate bid to reach out to the youth has resorted to GTA V and GTA VI imagery on social media. Recall that this video game follows a criminal duo. How very appropriate.” The PM in a desperate bid to reach out to the youth has resorted to GTA V and GTA VI imagery on social media. Recall that this video game follows a criminal duo. How very appropriate. — Jairam Ramesh (@Jairam_Ramesh) November 19, 2026 In a video posted on the Congress’s X handle, the party called GTA “the perfect game for a criminal mindset” and said the PM had “found his game as he makes yet another desperate attempt to woo Gen Z by projecting himself as a GTA 6 enthusiast”. “For those unfamiliar with the game, GTA is all about theft, violence and crime, giving players the free will to break rules, commit crimes and climb the criminal ranks. But why is Narendra Modi so keen to associate himself with a game that celebrates crime and lawlessness?” asked the party. From Vote Chori To GTA: Modi's Perfect Match — Congress (@INCIndia) November 20, 2026 BJP responds Hitting back at Ramesh, BJP’s social media co-convener Priti Gandhi said the PM’s post was “about exposing Congress-era failures & showcasing India's progress” since 2014. “You were unable to counter a single figure, so you chose to moralise about video-game characters. “Desperate bid” to hide Congress's failures is yours,” she said. BJP’s national media co-in-charge Pradeep Bhandari accused Ramesh of “FOMO (a popular Gen Z slang that stands for fear of missing out)”, saying, “Mr Jairam Ramesh, Crime & Congress are synonyms. Congress committed an economic crime by Keeping People of India poor for 70 years! Congress committed an economic crime by making India a fragile five economy! During GTA V India a fragile five economy During GTA VI India fastest growing economy I understand your FOMO seeing PM Narendra Modi's connect with Youth of India!” BJP sources said that while the members of the party’s social media team identified the trend before the launch of the game, the decision was finalised following Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi’s recent interaction with students at US universities. Following the Cockroach Janta Party’s July protests, which forced Dharmendra Pradhan to resign as Union Education Minister, the BJP stepped up its youth outreach, with PM Modi taking to Instagram to reach out to the youth for whom the video platform is the preferred social media platform of choice. Unlike the text-heavy platforms such as WhatsApp and Twitter, where reach is determined by follower count, Instagram’s interest-graph algorithm has proved difficult for the BJP to crack. In short, someone's post may go viral on Instagram or reach more viewers if they generate interest and is determined to be relevant for other users. Reach is thus dependent on relevance rathern than personal connections. And that possibly is one of the reasons why the party is trying hard to get onto social media trends to amplify its political message.

headline: In Gujarat, how BJP, Opposition vie to claim Birsa Munda legacy for tribal outreach
content: In Pipardi village in Gujarat's Dahod district, Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel walks into an anganwadi and switches on his mobile phone light to navigate the dark room. The videos released by the BJP government show the CM meeting the village's tribal families, interacting with children, and drinking water from a hand pump. The village is part of the Ratanmahal forest, which is home to sloth bear. A tiger, extinct from Gujarat 30 years ago, strayed in the forest late last year, prompting the government to launch an eco corridor project. Patel's visit to the village was part of his plan to spend 72 hours in Dahod's Garbada belt that began on Wednesday. He spent his first day in Bhindol village with a Tadvi family. He donned a wide turban, tried his hand at a bow and arrow, sat on the floor for a meal in leaf plates, and joined the local tribals at a spiritual music event. In the run-up to the state Assembly elections due in December 2027, the BJP has intensified its bid to reach out to the tribal community, which is concentrated in 14 of the state's 34 districts, accounting for about 14% of its voters. The tribal icon and freedom fighter Birsa Munda's 151st birth anniversary on November 15, was commemorated in the state as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas, which saw the BJP and the Opposition parties vying to stake claims over his legacy. While the BJP made a development pitch to tribals in Chhota Udepur district, the Congress held an Ulgulan Sabha in Naswadi, even as the Congress and the AAP together joined a Birsa Munda event in Panchmahal district. Birsa Munda, whose rebellion against the British rule was rooted in the tribal rights over "jal, jungle and zameen", seems to have become a rallying point for the Gujarat parties over tribal issues centred on identity, land rights and development. The BJP organised Janjatiya Gaurav Saptah from November 12 to 18, covering 55 Assembly constituencies across 14 tribal districts, during which the CM announced projects worth Rs 2,283 crore, distributed forest rights certificates to 18,828 beneficiaries, announced Johar Cafes to promote tribal cuisine, and proposed the installation of Birsa Munda statues. BJP's game plan With the Assembly polls a year away, the BJP is seeking to consolidate its position in tribals belts, where the Opposition has made inroads, particularly in Narmada, Bharuch, Tapi and Dang districts. The AAP's good showing in the Narmada district in the local body elections earlier this year has alarmed the BJP, which is now trying to take its development pitch directly to tribal villages. Adding to the BJP's concern, its tribal MP Mansukh Vasava has questioned the government's distribution of the forest rights certificates, warning that tribal farmers in Narmada and Bharuch districts could be left out of it again. Ahead of the November 15 programme, Vasava took to social media to point to over 800 pending applications in Narmada in this regard. He alleged that forest officials, armed with “flawed satellite surveys”, have denied land rights to tribal families who had cultivated their land for 20-25 years. He also met farmers from the villages in Sagbara taluka just three days before the state event to urge them to fight "through legal and democratic means". On November 15, 900 farmers from Narmada and Bharuch were given title deeds by the administration in what was seen as the BJP's bid to “silence” its outspoken MP. As part of the BJP's bid to connect with the Scheduled Tribes (STs), ministers, party MPs and MLAs were recently asked to camp overnight in villages in 27 ST-reserved Assembly constituencies, interact with tribals for feedback on various amenities and government schemes, hold hold gram sabhas and visit schools and anganwadis. "The BJP's tribal outreach is an organisational exercise, not merely a commemorative programme. The party is seeking to interact, hear out and identify local grievances, assess gaps in the implementation of government schemes and counter the Opposition's claims before the election campaign gathers pace," a senior BJP leader said. Opposition's play The absence of the AAP's tribal face Chaitar Vasava, who has been in jail since June this year after his conviction in a case of alleged assault on government officials, seems to have brought the party and the Congress together in some tribal areas. Chaitar had won from the Dediapada seat in Narmada by a landslide on his electoral debut in 2022. On November 15, at a Birsa Munda event organised by local tribals at Morva Hadaf in Panchmahal, the AAP and Congress leaders were together in attendance. Former CM Shankersinh Vaghela, who has been considering his return to the Congress, also attended the event, praising the leadership of the AAP leaders like Chaitar and Gopal Italia. However, there are currently no signs of the Congress and the AAP making any moves to forge an alliance for the 2027 elections. They had tied up for the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, but the BJP had then swept the polls, winning 25 of the state's 26 seats with the Congress getting the remaining one seat. At the Congress-held Ulgulan Sabha on November 15, state party president Amit Chavda alleged that tribal villages have continued to reel from “inadequate” drinking water and irrigation facilities, while the non-existence of industries in the tribal belts have been forcing youths to migrate to Saurashtra to work as labourers. He also accused the BJP government of taking over tribal land in the name of hydroelectric projects, displacing the community and leaving it burdened with debts. "The Congress needs to recover political ground in the tribal belts as the BJP has increasingly expanded its presence there, also inducting several tribal Congress leaders into its fold. The Birsa Munda anniversary is an opportunity to take the message directly to the tribal voters rather than leave the occasion for the ruling party to leverage on, which is why we also decided to have such events,” a senior Congress leader said. In the 2022 Assembly elections, the BJP had bagged 156 of the state's 182 seats as against the Congress's 17 and the AAP's 5. Of the 27 tribal seats, the BJP had won 23 – up from nine in 2017 – with the Congress winning three and the AAP one seat. For the AAP now, Chaitar's incarceration has created a leadership vacuum at a time when the BJP and the Congress are intensifying their engagement with the STs. The BJP is looking to regain ground in areas where Chaitar's campaign over land and forest rights has created a resonance. For the Congress, the challenge is to turn its campaign to connect with tribals into a sustained exercise for organisational revival in tribal regions, where it has traditionally had an edge.

headline: BJP vs BJP in Bengal: Six months into government, what is plaguing the party?
content: Fissures seem to have surfaced in the West Bengal BJP barely six months after the party stormed to power in the state by routing the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress (TMC). This has been attributed to various factors including the induction of a section of TMC activists into the BJP fold, law and order issues, and allegations of extortion. “The BJP’s victory was largely driven by public resentment against the previous TMC government but its subsequent attempts to expand our organisational base has created friction between the new and old party workers, especially those veteran workers close to the Sangh Parivar,” a senior state BJP leader said. Admitting that party workers were “uncomfortable” with sharing the same platform now with their rivals who had targeted them in the past, the leader said the BJP leadership had repeatedly cautioned the grassroots-level party functionaries against such inductions but “its directives were not being strictly followed in several areas”. ‘Must stop extortion’ The issue of alleged extortion has emerged as a major embarrassment for the BJP. State Finance Minister Swapan Dasgupta recently admitted that the menace had not been completely eliminated in the state, warning that public confidence would remain fragile until it was eradicated. “It is true that extortion is still going on here. Until that is stopped, people's trust will not be fully restored,” he said. Dasgupta acknowledged that he had not been able to eliminate extortion even in his own Assembly constituency, Rashbehari, in Kolkata. “Personally, I have tried but I cannot say I have been able to stop it fully. It has become a habit among people,” he said. The Minister also said that ending extortion, cut money and syndicate rule was essential to attract large-scale investments and industrial projects to the state. Strengthening law and order, he said, would have to go hand in hand with dismantling these practices. He also said the BJP has issued show-cause notices to more than 20 party leaders over allegations of extortion and other acts of indiscipline. State BJP president Shamik Bhattacharya has also issued repeated warnings to party workers against using the party's name to extort money. “If anybody with a BJP flag asks for money at your factory gate, do inform us. His place will be in jail,” Bhattacharya has said. On Friday, addressing BJP workers, Bhattacharya warned against the entry of people accused of allegedly looting the state under the previous regime. “Those who looted the state earlier are now trying to come to the BJP. They must be identified. This anarchy cannot be allowed to continue," he said, urging workers to file police complaints against anyone attempting to tarnish the party's image. Bhattacharya said several people had been attempting to join the BJP following the change in government, with some allegedly moving around their localities carrying the party flag and claiming to be its leaders. He also cautioned party workers against confusing organisational authority with administrative power. “In some places, some mandal presidents think that the police will act according to their instructions. Everyone must remember that we have won due to the people's votes. The people have the final say. If there is any deviation among us, the people will see it. Everyone must remain restrained and humble," he said. The concerns over internal rifts are not limited to the party's state leadership. Union Minister Santanu Thakur, referring to the internal party clashes, said: “The BJP is beating BJP.” Questioning the administration's silence, he alleged that some people within the party were seeking to use their new-found power against their own colleagues. A BJP insider said, "In the government, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has the greatest influence. He has co-ordination with state party president Samik Bhattacharya. However, some party groups are not happy with the government's work. Some Cabinet ministers are also not happy with some organisational decisions. Sometimes those leaders are coming out openly and expressing their voices which is not desirable, but you can't control everybody." He also said, "Even before assuming power, the Bengal BJP had various factions. Even after the party came to power, those groups still operate – and all of them have their own agendas. So, some friction is inevitable." Party worker's murder The recent murder of a BJP worker in Panihati in North 24 Parganas, allegedly by members of a rival party faction, has highlighted the tensions within the party. Reacting to the incident, Panihati MLA Ratna Debnath of the BJP, mother of the RG Kar case victim, purportedly made a remark that triggered a controversy. “It would have been better if the BJP had not won,” she said while expressing her condolences to the family of the deceased party worker. Debnath also questioned the administration’s role, claiming that repeated complaints had been made about law and order in the area, but the situation had not improved. She said several clashes had taken place across different wards of Panihati, alleging that the erstwhile TMC activists who switched to the BJP were creating unrest there. The Opposition seized on her remarks to target the BJP and question the Adhikari government's handling of law and order situation. Debnath subsequently issued a clarification on social media, alleging that a portion of her statement had been taken out of context. “A part of my statement has been presented in a way that has detached it from its original context, resulting in a misleading message,” she stated. She said she had neither intended nor suggested that it would have been better if the BJP had not come to power, describing the interpretation of her remarks as a distortion of their intended meaning.

headline: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary at Year 1: Tackling crime, corruption, and the Prashant Kishor test
content: With the BJP-led NDA government in Bihar having completed a year in office on Friday, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary speaks to The Indian Express about his administration’s achievements, challenges, the debate on the Nitish versus Samrat model, funds crunch, alleged corruption in the tendering process, how the government is tackling the mafia, and Prashant Kishor. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to visit the state on Saturday to inaugurate and lay foundation stones of projects worth around Rs. 34,470 crore in Vaishali. The PM will also unveil the Nitish Setu, a six-lane cable-stayed bridge across the Ganga, near Patna. Excerpts: * After a year in power, what are your government’s achievements and challenges? We went into the 2025 Assembly elections with 25 promises on all-round development, including women's safety and empowerment, quality education, and industrial growth. We started the Sahyog programme (an online and offline forum to receive people's grievances) and received 10 lakh applications in the first 30 days. We disposed of 96% of the cases and took action against negligent officials. In education, we earlier had only a few models such as Navodaya, Netarhat, Ramakrishna Mission, and Simultala schools. It is a matter of pride for us that we have now started 700 model schools (Classes 9 to 12) across the state that provide smart classes and online classes to reach out to the maximum number of students, even during the night. We also simultaneously started 211 degree colleges across the state and provided loans of over Rs 18,000 crore under the Student Credit Card scheme. In terms of new policies, we are starting e-cabinet from December, during which I will review and clear proposals worth over Rs 100 crore relating to green energy, MSME, biofuels, and GCC (Global Capability Centre). We are starting an IT park in the Gardanibagh area of Patna and developing a centre of excellence at IIT Patna to attract youth willing to work in the IT sector in Bihar. * What about law-and-order challenges? There was the Bharat Bhushan Tiwari encounter and the Jamui incident. The state has 93 policemen per one lakh population. We need reforms at the police station level. We have issued directions for speedy trials. The mafia who have become rich all of a sudden are under our scanner. Over 700 applications seeking permission to take action against them are pending before the courts; we have got permission in only seven cases. We have already started the 'Police Didi' initiative for the safety of college and school girls. We have focused on effective ways to deal with cybercrime. The media must not look at a few isolated cases and instead look at it broadly. Our data suggests that about 70% of crime, including murder, is land-related. A land survey is being conducted to streamline land ownership and deal with land disputes. We have major land-related issues. There are areas such as Darbhanga, Saharsa, Khagaria, and Naugachia that have not seen a land survey since the days of Raja Todarmal (during the reign of Mughal Emperor Akbar). We have deployed an IPS officer and a secretary since August 15 to monitor land mutation and other land-related cases. * The tendering process in the state has come under heavy scrutiny lately, especially after the Rishu Shree case. The ED is questioning six IAS officers. Doesn't it impact the image of the bureaucracy in the state? We have been continuously working to make tendering transparent, with the Special Vigilance Unit and Economic Offences Unit carrying out crackdowns. Some cases are already in court. Those found giving tenders to a favoured few will face dire consequences. There will be no compromise on our stated 'triple C' policy against crime, corruption, and communalism. There is no government-sponsored crime in the state, unlike before. * Your dream project to develop 12 satellite towns is facing resistance. How are you dealing with issues of land acquisition, especially when several farmers are not willing to part with their land? If Bihar has to be economically well-off, we have to develop 12 urban townships with the potential to realise investment worth Rs 50 lakh crore in five years. These towns will have education, industry, hospitality, medical, and tourism hubs. There is a transparent system of land pooling. Suppose a person has 100 katha of land; we will use 45 katha (1 katha equals 0.312 acres approximately) and return the remaining 55 katha after developing it — providing roads, electricity, water, and sewerage. This will increase the value of a farmer's land by up to 10 times, and this land can be used for commercial purposes. Second, if a landowner gives us land willingly, we will pay four times the circle rate in rural areas and two times the circle rate in urban areas, plus an additional 10% of the total value of the land. In the third category, we will acquire land from those unwilling to give it to us by applying the same rate, minus the extra 10%. We are trying to clear people's misconceptions. We will start realising township projects from March 2027. * You had promised investment worth Rs 5 lakh crore by this month. How close are you to achieving it? I will make an announcement at the right time, but we hope to exceed the Rs 5 lakh crore mark. We now have five cement factories and ethanol factories in the state. We have received investments in logistics, food processing, and pharma sectors. As we give subsidies worth Rs 23,000 crore in the power sector, we are vetting big investments in this sector as well. We have one dry port at Bihta, for which we are working out ways to get hassle-free customs clearance. We will open more dry ports. * What are the government’s plans to take medical services to the grassroots? We have now equipped district and sub-divisional hospitals with ICU facilities. Doctors can no longer routinely refer cases to Patna; they will have to deal with the maximum number of cases locally and give sound reasons for referring a patient to a Patna hospital. We have given Ayushman Bharat cards to about 9.5 crore BPL people in the state. A paucity of doctors is a concern at some hospitals, but this is because several doctors go on leave to pursue higher studies after joining, and we cannot create new vacancies against those on leave. As for private practice, the Health Minister (Nishant Kumar) can review the situation. * What are the government’s plans to deal with the funds crunch? There is no major funds crunch. We are giving Rs 1,100 monthly social security pension to 1.09 crore families. We face a funds crunch mainly because we have additional schemes. The state revenue is hovering around Rs 65,000 crore, but we expect to take it to Rs 75,000 crore by next year and Rs 2 lakh crore by 2030. * Is Bihar following the Nitish model or the Samrat model, as you once said that Nitish has set a high bar for others to follow? Bihar has been following the NDA model, which combines the Nitish model and the Samrat model under the leadership of PM Narendra Modi. Nitish Kumar has become a point of reference and an ideal for development politics now. After Dr Srikrishna Singh and Karpoori Thakur, it is Nitish Kumar who worked so hard for social justice and development. We have named the new Ganga bridge after Nitish Kumar to acknowledge his contribution to building the state. If Lalu Prasad's family is sore over it, we cannot do anything about it. * There is a clamour to name Nishant Kumar Deputy CM. How do you see it? The JD(U) alone can take a call on it. They alone can decide who will head the party or become Deputy CM. The BJP will not interfere in its internal affairs. * Do you consider Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor a challenger? And can he replace the RJD as the principal Opposition in the near future? So long as Lalu Prasad ji is there, the RJD will continue to be the principal Opposition. Eventually, people will decide these things. I have nothing personal against him (PK). He is free to criticise me as a political opponent.

headline: ‘We got this before GTA 6’: Why the BJP and Congress are invoking a viral meme in their political battle
content: The launch of Grand Theft Auto VI has given India’s political parties a new reference point in their social media messaging, with the BJP and Congress drawing on the video game's popularity to trade political barbs. The exchange centres on a popular internet joke about the 13-year gap between GTA V, released in 2013, and its successor, which launched worldwide on Thursday (November 19). The BJP, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, used the comparison to highlight what it describes as India’s progress over this period. The Congress has questioned the ruling party’s decision to associate itself with a game built around criminal activity and violence. India is playing a whole new game! — Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) November 19, 2026 First, what is GTA? First released in 1997, Grand Theft Auto is an open-world video game franchise in which players explore fictional American cities, undertake missions and engage in activities ranging from driving and exploration to theft and violent crime. Developed by Rockstar Games, the series has become known for its sprawling virtual worlds, satirical portrayal of American society and the freedom it gives players to interact with their surroundings. Its best-known instalments include GTA III, Vice City, San Andreas, GTA IV and GTA V. Players can move freely through these virtual worlds, travelling on foot or by vehicle, and undertake missions involving everything from petty theft to organised crime. The games also recreate aspects of everyday life, including phone calls and messages, while using fictional characters and businesses to satirise American society. GTA VI follows Jason and Lucia, a couple involved in criminal activity in a fictionalised version of Florida. Like its predecessors, the game features violence and criminal missions alongside an expansive world that players can explore. And what is the meme? The political exchange draws on a meme that became popular during the long wait for GTA VI: “We got [something] before GTA VI.” Internet users inserted major political events, technological developments and other milestones into the phrase to joke about how much had changed since the previous instalment. The 13-year gap made the joke particularly adaptable to political messaging. For the BJP, it offered a way to present its account of changes in India since 2013 using a reference familiar to younger audiences. For the Congress, the game’s criminal themes provided an opportunity to ridicule the Prime Minister's choice of imagery. The franchise’s popularity added to the attention surrounding the exchange. Rockstar Games, the game’s publisher, said GTA VI generated $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, describing it as the biggest entertainment launch in history. How has the BJP used GTA VI? As anticipation surrounding the game’s release grew, the Prime Minister’s X and Instagram accounts published a series of slides borrowing the franchise's distinctive typography and imagery. “Between GTA V and VI, here’s how India upgraded”, the post stated, followed by images of ‘Level Up’ across various sectors from the economy and poverty alleviation to ramping up its solar power generation capacity and start-up ecosystem. The campaign used the period between the two releases to showcase the government’s claims about India’s economic growth, infrastructure development and other achievements. According to BJP sources, the party’s social media workers had identified the trend before the game’s launch. However, the decision to capitalise on it was made following Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi’s recent interaction with students at US universities. On Saturday (November 21), Minister of Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari’s social media account used similar imagery to highlight highway construction and reductions in travel time across the country. Several BJP state units and accounts associated with senior leaders, including Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, also amplified the trend. Why has the Congress objected? The Congress attacked the Prime Minister’s choice of imagery, pointing to the game’s central themes of crime and violence. Congress communications in-charge Jairam Ramesh criticised the Prime Minister’s post, referring to GTA VI’s protagonists, Jason and Lucia, who are involved in criminal activity. He said in a post, “The PM in a desperate bid to reach out to the youth has resorted to GTA V and GTA VI imagery on social media. Recall that this video game follows a criminal duo. How very appropriate.” The BJP responded by accusing the Congress of focusing on the video game's storyline rather than engaging with the figures presented in Modi's post. BJP social media co-convenor Priti Gandhi said the post was “about exposing Congress-era failures & showcasing India's progress” since 2014. “You were unable to counter a single figure, so you chose to moralise about video-game characters…” she alleged. The Congress also circulated a minute-long video highlighting the game's violent themes, captioned “From Vote Chori To GTA: Modi’s Perfect Match”.

headline: Dhami meets PM Modi, seeks relief for Uttarakhand from Centre’s borrowing cap
content: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami has sought an exemption for the state from the Centre’s cap on Externally Aided Projects (EAP), citing the state’s mountainous terrain and limited financial resources. During a meeting on Friday with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi, Dhami also pressed for central support for a series of proposed infrastructure projects including the Delhi-Haldwani Expressway, Tanakpur-Bageshwar and Bageshwar-Karnaprayag railway lines, and the doubling of the Haridwar-Dehradun railway line. He also sought assistance for expansion and modernisation of the Chinyalisaur airstrip. Dhami sought exemption from the Centre’s cap on loans and grants the state can get for Externally Aided Projects. EAPs are government projects financed through loans and grants, routed through the Department of Economic Affairs. Under the Centre’s fiscal framework, there is an annual net borrowing ceiling for each state. As per a Uttarakhand government statement, among other proposals put forward was the establishment of an All India Institute of Ayurveda at Kichha. Dhami also sought support for the Dehradun Ring Road, the Dehradun-Mussoorie Ropeway and an extension of the Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) from Dehradun to Haridwar. Traffic management initiatives in Rishikesh also figured in the discussions. The meeting comes as Uttarakhand prepares for the 2027 Kumbh in Haridwar. The Centre provided financial assistance of Rs 500 crore for the event, which is likely to draw large numbers of pilgrims.

headline: PM Modi’s remark on jobs & wages a confession: Congress
content: NEW DELHI: Congress ­claimed vindication over PM’s speech to Ficci lamenting stagnant wages and jobs and growing ­disparity, with Rahul Gandhi calling Narendra Modi’s taunt to the industry a “confession”.Rahul accused PM Modi of creating monopolies and asked him how many jobs have been created by the groups whom he “handed over ports, airports, coal, roads, power, mines and jungles”.“Small traders and MSMEs that create jobs — you destroyed them with demonetisation and flawed GST. And for large companies that competed honestly, you wiped out the playing field altogether. Monopolies don’t create jobs. They drive up prices and eliminate competition,” he said.Also Read| 'Apologise for 1962 humiliation': Rijiju fires 4 questions at Rahul over 'compromised PM' jibeCongress spokesperson Jairam Ramesh said Congress 2024 Lok Sabha manifesto – nyay patra – stated exactly what Modi told Ficci, but the PM then dubbed Congress as driven by “urban naxal mindset against wealth creators”.Ramesh said Modi’s policies are squarely responsible for the lack of private investment, without which there cannot be wage and job growth.He also said that imports from China this year will touch a record $150 billion, up from $112 billion, which is responsible for decimating MSMEs.He said PM Modi has also spread fear in the industry by misusing enforcement agencies for benefitting select corporates. “GDP growth is only in the headlines,” he said. “By the way he spoke at Ficci, it was clear the PM is rattled... For the first time in 12 years, the PM launched such an attack on wealth creators...”Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: 'Grand Theft India': AAP mocks PM, Amit Shah in AI-generated GTA 6 spoof featuring Raghav Chadha
content: NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on X shared an AI-generated video featuring Rajya Sabha member Raghav Chadha in a version of the popular video game Grand Theft Auto (GTA), reimagined as ‘Grand Theft India’. The edited clip also features characters resembling Prime Minister Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah.Sharing the video, the AAP's social media handle wrote: “Wait! Raghav Chadha Just Unlocked a Secret Character in GTA VI!”The video appears to be an edited version of a clip Chadha had shared on his social media account around the game's India launch. In the original video, the BJP MP was seen waiting for the game to unlock, with a controller in his hand and his eyes fixed on the television screen.The AI-generated version reworks that footage into a fictional Indian-themed game, with Modi and Shah also appearing as characters. Titled ‘Grand Theft India’, the clip also uses political imagery, including an electoral ballot and an electronic voting machine (EVM). Other visuals appear to show voters' names being struck off electoral rolls, an apparent reference to the controversy surrounding the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.Chadha had earlier shared the countdown video as he waited for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) on Thursday. The MP was seen sitting in front of his television, watching the timer approach midnight.As the countdown ended, Chadha turned towards the camera and smiled. Sharing the clip, he wrote: “11:59 PM has never felt this long. #GTA6 A little glimpse of life beyond Parliament.”The post offered a glimpse of the Rajya Sabha MP away from his parliamentary engagements and drew attention from gaming enthusiasts on social media.The clip comes amid the continued online buzz around GTA 6, one of the most anticipated video game releases in recent years.Political parties tap GTA 6 buzzPolitical parties are increasingly using the global buzz around GTA 6 to push their political messaging and take aim at rivals.PM Narendra Modi used GTA-themed posters to highlight India's progress since 2013, comparing the country's economic and infrastructure milestones with the period when GTA 5 was released. The post also took a swipe at the previous Congress-led United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government.In Tamil Nadu, the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) invoked the game's fictional crime-ridden Vice City to target the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government. Reacting to a major narcotics seizure in Chennai, DMK president MK Stalin wrote on X: “Tamil Nadu is turning into a 'Vice City' under the TVK regime!”Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Stung by PM Modi's criticism, India Inc fears government may turn cold on tax concessions
content: NEW DELHI: A day after PM Modi shellacked India Inc for not translating tax cuts into more jobs and higher salaries, stunned corporate honchos were still trying to process the rebuke, with many worrying the govt may shut the door on any requests for tax concessions.The "insatiable hunger for concessions" remark by the PM hit members of the industry and businesses at the Ficci event hard. Many sitting in the room only realised the weight of Modi's comment later. Some executives are also seeing it as a signal that govt is in no mood to offer concessions. "It's a signal to back off before the budget," said an industry veteran.In coming weeks, the industry will be readying data to argue how jobs have increased and wages have gone up.Executives pointed to the pressure faced by the industry due to increase in fuel and input costs and the impact of a weak rupee that companies had to grapple with until a few weeks ago. However, sources in govt acknowledged the problems but maintained that the industry could have done much more to reciprocate the help govt extended to help them grow and compete internationally. Frustration with the industry's response had been building up.Officials have argued that from reduction in tax rates, direct as well as GST, to making life easier for businesses, govt had created conditions for the industry to grow at a rapid pace.Modi's statement is seen as a push to lift real incomes, a key worry for employees and workers since Covid. The 2025 Economic Survey had noted that corporate profitability had soared to a 15-year high in 2024 but growth in employee expense moderated.In 2023-24, job growth was estimated at 5.6%, while emoluments rose 11.8% with profits rising 10%, according to the Annual Survey of Industries. The latest report showed that persons engaged was up 7.2% to 2.1 crore in 2024-25, and emoluments were up 12.1% to Rs 8 lakh crore. Profits were up 7.7% to 11.6 lakh crore.Over the past few years, govt and industry have sparred over the pace of investment, with the private sector seen as lagging. In recent months, there has been a pick-up as the impact of lower GST has helped keep consumption strong amid global headwinds.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

headline: Evening newswrap: BJP targets Rahul as Trump hails India's GDP growth; PM Modi recreates 'gamcha' wave in
content: Donald Trump praised India's 7 per cent GDP growth, prompting the BJP to target Rahul Gandhi, accusing him of ignoring the country's economic achievements.PM Narendra Modi inaugurated the Nitish Setu in Bihar's Vaishali district and recreated his viral 'gamcha' wave from the NDA's 2025 Assembly election victory celebrations.Mexico arrested FBI's most-wanted fugitive Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores in a military operation that triggered gun battles, explosions and roadblocks in Sinaloa, forcing a baseball match to be abandoned.India's space journey began on November 21, 1963, with the launch of the US-made Nike-Apache sounding rocket from Thumba, Kerala, laying the foundation for its space programme.Shubman Gill and Rishabh Pant became the first two Indian batters to cross 3,000 runs in the World Test Championship, achieving the milestone against New Zealand in Wellington.Here are top news stories of the day'Turns a blind eye': BJP takes swipe at Rahul Gandhi as Trump hails India's 7% GDP growthUS President Donald Trump praised India's 7 per cent GDP growth while arguing that lower interest rates could help the US economy grow by 15 to 20 per cent. BJP leader Ashish Sood seized on the remarks to target Rahul Gandhi, saying the world was recognising India's progress while the Congress leader was turning a blind eye to its achievements. Trump's praise comes after his 2025 criticism of India's trade policies, when he called the country a "dead economy".Read full storyPM Modi inaugurates Nitish Setu in Bihar, recreates 'poll victory' moment with 'gamcha' wavePrime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday waved a gamcha while inaugurating the Nitish Setu in Vaishali, recreating his viral gesture from the 2025 Bihar Assembly election celebrations. The moment had gained popularity after the NDA won 202 of the 243 Assembly seats. The inauguration was attended by Bihar Governor Syed Ata Hasnain, Union minister Chirag Paswan and chief minister Samrat Choudhary, among other dignitaries. Read full storyBullets rain from helicopter, explosions on ground: How Mexico hunted down FBI's most-wanted drug lordMexican security forces arrested alleged cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, also known as 'El Chapo Isidro', in an operation involving elite military units and US assistance. Militants reportedly retaliated with gunfire, explosives and roadblocks across Sinaloa. Helicopters were seen firing towards the ground as violence spread to Guasave, where a baseball match was suspended and spectators fled for safety. Meza-Flores, who heads the Los Mazatlecos criminal organisation, was among the FBI's 10 most-wanted fugitives, with a $5 million reward announced for information leading to his arrest. Read full storyBefore Chandrayaan and Mangalyaan, there was Nike-Apache: India's first sounding rocket launchIndia launched its first sounding rocket, the two-stage Nike-Apache, from Thumba on November 21, 1963, to study the upper atmosphere. The launch was organised by the Indian National Committee for Space Research, established under Dr Vikram Sarabhai in 1962. It marked the beginning of India's space programme. The first indigenous sounding rocket, RH-75, followed in 1967, while ISRO was established in 1969. Rishabh Pant followed him later in the day, becoming the first wicketkeeper in the world to reach the milestone. India ended Day 3 at 486/4, leading New Zealand by 118 runs after KL Rahul scored 136, while Yashasvi Jaiswal and Devdutt Padikkal contributed 85 and 80 respectively.
