headline: 'Modi ji should apologise': Congress alleges PM's Lucknow event led to cancellation of four weddings
content: NEW DELHI: Former Uttar Pradesh Congress chief Ajay Rai on Saturday demanded an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, alleging that his event in Lucknow led to the cancellation of four weddings scheduled at Indira Gandhi Pratishthan.Speaking to ANI, Rai said the venue had been booked months in advance by four families for their children's weddings, but the arrangements were disrupted after the Prime Minister's programme was scheduled at the same location."Modi ji should apologise to the families whose four weddings have been cancelled. They should ask for it and certainly offer an apology," Rai said.Rai said the day was considered auspicious for weddings and pointed out that the families had already distributed invitation cards mentioning Indira Gandhi Pratishthan as the venue. He also displayed a wedding invitation card which, according to him, had been reprinted with a different venue following the cancellation."I received a wedding card. It clearly says here that in place of Indira Gandhi Pratishthan, the new wedding venue is Royal Grand Lawn by Royal Cafe. Look at this in front, and properly, the most important thing in it is that the venue's Gate Number 1 is clearly mentioned here," he said."The Prime Minister's programme could have been held somewhere else, but the Prime Minister requires VIP protocol. The best hall is needed, the most beautiful hall there; that is what they want. Instead of weddings for children, isn't it?" he said.Rai further alleged that the cancellation had caused distress to the families, particularly as wedding preparations had been made well in advance and invitation cards had already been distributed."Their weddings will be ruined. The weddings will happen with their permission. These are the protectors of democracy, the people who protect democracy; they are for the public. So the public is being troubled today; people are being troubled," he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: PM Modi inaugurates Nitish Setu in Bihar, recreates 'poll victory' moment with 'gamcha' wave
content: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday recreated his viral 'gamcha' moment from the 2025 Bihar assembly election celebrations while inaugurating the Nitish Setu in Vaishali district.PM Modi was seen waving his gamcha during the event, recalling his celebratory appearance at the BJP office in Patna after the National Democratic Alliance's (NDA) sweeping victory in the November 2025 Assembly elections.The gesture had become one of the most widely shared visuals of the election aftermath. Videos of Modi waving a light-coloured gamcha and wearing a Madhubani-print stole had gone viral on social media, with the phrase 'Modi Ka Gamcha' trending soon after.Also read - Modi’s ‘gamcha’ moment steals show after NDA sweepThe phrase 'Modi Ka Gamcha' had also gained traction online, with supporters associating the moment with the NDA's electoral performance in the state. The alliance had won 202 of the 243 Assembly seats.The moment was widely shared as a symbol of the NDA's electoral triumph, with supporters also circulating the phrase "Bihar ke logo ne garda uda diya". The alliance had won 202 of the 243 Assembly seats.During the 2025 celebrations, Modi's entry into the BJP office, waving the gamcha and wearing the Madhubani-print stole, drew widespread attention. A video of the moment, set to the Bollywood track 'Jiya Ho Bihar Ke Lala' from Gangs of Wasseypur, further fuelled its popularity online.The inauguration of Nitish Setu was attended by Bihar governor Lt Gen Syed Ata Hasnain (retd), Union minister Chirag Paswan, chief minister Samrat Choudhary and other dignitaries.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: PM Modi launches projects worth Rs 34,000cr in Bihar; says state now known for development, not scams
content: NEW DELHI: PM Modi on Saturday launched a sharp attack on the RJD-Congress alliance in Bihar, saying the state, under the NDA government, was now making headlines for development and investment proposals instead of scams and crime.Addressing a rally in Jafarpatti in Vaishali district, PM Modi inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 228 infrastructure and development projects worth Rs 34,000 crore, including the 'Nitish Setu' over the Ganga river.The Prime Minister said the bridge had been named after JD(U) president Nitish Kumar, who stepped down as chief minister in April to make way for a BJP-led government, as a mark of respect for his contributions to the state."The state has come a long way since the NDA took over. Earlier, only scams and crimes were talked about. Now Bihar makes news for investment proposals and action taken against those who indulge in any type of wrongdoing," he said.Taking a swipe at the Congress over its 'Garibi Hatao' campaign, PM Modi said his government's political resolve and welfare schemes had helped transform the lives of millions across the country."In a country where the Congress party spent decades chanting the slogan 'Garibi Hatao' - we have managed to lift 50 crore people out of poverty in just 12 years. This is the result of the government's willpower and its welfare schemes for the poor," he said."The nation is winning this battle against poverty because we have prioritised making life easier for millions of poor people and providing them with essential amenities. We have provided free food grains to 80 crore people. By providing permanent houses to millions of families, we have given them a sense of security. By guaranteeing free medical treatment, we have relieved them from the burden of expensive healthcare costs," he added.Earlier, PM Modi flagged off 100 PM-eBuses in Vaishali, giving a boost to cleaner public transport in the state. He described the large public turnout as a "festival of development", celebrated with the blessings of Chhathi Maiya following the conclusion of the Chhath festival."Today, 100 modern PM-eBuses have been flagged off to make urban transport more convenient. Under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, the keys to permanent homes have been handed over to thousands of poor families. I congratulate the people of Bihar on all these development initiatives," he said.Among the projects for which the PM laid foundation stones were the four-laning of the Sahebganj-Areraj-Bettiah section of NH-139W, to be developed at a cost of over Rs 3,800 crore, and the power evacuation initiative for the Pirpainti Super Thermal Power Project (3x800 MW), estimated at around Rs 3,350 crore.Among the major road projects inaugurated were the six-laning of the Aurangabad-Chardaha section of NH-19, the Chorma-Bairgania section of NH-227F and the Umagaon-Saharsa section of NH-327.The PM also inaugurated the second 660 MW unit of the 1,320 MW Buxar Thermal Power Project, along with electricity distribution and transmission infrastructure projects under the Energy Department.Other projects included the restoration and strengthening of canals and embankments, a floating solar project at Phulwaria Dam in Nawada, and sewerage infrastructure at Kahalgaon.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday recreated his viral ‘gamcha’ moment from the 2025 Bihar assembly election celebrations while inaugurating the Nitish Setu in Vaishali district.PM Modi was seen waving his gamcha during the event, recalling his celebratory appearance at the BJP office in Patna after the National Democratic Alliance’s (NDA) sweeping victory in the November 2025 Assembly elections.

headline: Not insisting on 4th term as CM, high command should decide: Ashok Gehlot
content: JAIPUR: Amid speculation over Congress leadership in Rajasthan ahead of the 2028 assembly elections, former chief minister Ashok Gehlot Saturday said he was not insisting on becoming CM for a fourth term, asserting that the final decision should rest with the party high command.His remarks come a day after Congress’s strong performance in Rajasthan’s panchayat elections, which has strengthened the position of PCC chief Govind Singh Dotasra and Leader of Opposition Tikaram Jully in the state unit.“I am very happy and satisfied with what Congress leadership has given me. Sonia Gandhi gave me opportunities, Indira Gandhi made me a minister, Rajiv Gandhi promoted me, and I also served in Union govt under PV Narasimha Rao. I have been Rajasthan CM three times. Is that a small achievement?” Gehlot said in an interview with PTI.He said he did not believe that becoming CM again was a personal necessity. “Should I necessarily become CM for a fourth time? It is not that I must become CM every time. I am satisfied with what I have received from the party,” Gehlot said.The ex-CM maintained that leadership decisions should be taken keeping the party’s interests and public expectations in mind. “The (Congress) high command has to decide what is in the party’s interest and what the people of Rajasthan want. Whether the decision goes in my favour or not is a separate matter,” he said.The former CM also said that such decisions were not ordinarily made by individuals, indicating that he would accept the party leadership’s decision.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Jaipur | Silver Rate in Jaipur | Bank Holidays in Jaipur | Public Holidays in Jaipur | Jaipur AQI | Weather in Jaipur | Petrol Price in Jaipur | Diesel Price in Jaipur | CNG Price in Jaipur | LPG Price in JaipurStay updated with the latest Jaipur news. headline: Yuzvendra Chahal joins BJP as OBC Morcha member, thanks PM Modi, other leaders for a ‘place in the family’ | India News
content: Cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Saturday after being named a special invitee to its OBC (Other Backward Classes) Morcha's national working committee.The BJP on Saturday released its list of national office-bearers, national executive members and other appointments in the party's OBC Morcha, which also included the name of Chahal.Chahal thanked PM Narendra Modi and several other BJP leaders after joining the party. “I sincerely thank respected Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji, respected Home Minister Shri Amit Shah ji, BJP National President Shri Nitin Naveen ji, and OBC Morcha National President Shri Amarpal Maurya ji for giving me a place and respect within the BJP family,” he posted on X.According to the official communication issued by the party's central office, the list includes seven national vice-presidents, three national general secretaries and seven national secretaries representing various states across the country. Chahal has been named as a special invitee to the OBC Morcha's national working committee, representing Delhi. The other two special invitees are Advait Charan Gananayak from Odisha and advocate Seema Samriddhi Kushwaha from Uttar Pradesh.Chahal has played 72 ODIs, and 80 T20Is for India so far, picking up 121 and 96 wickets in two formats respectively. He also has 233 IPL wickets across 188 matches he has played for different teams in the T20 league.A look at key appointmentsThe seven newly appointed national vice-presidents of the BJP OBC Morcha are Jogen Mohan (Assam), Mamata Mohanta (Odisha), Sangam Lal Gupta (Uttar Pradesh), Babanrao Ravji Choudhary (Maharashtra), Sat Prakash Rana (Delhi), Arjun Sahani (Bihar) and Sangeeta Balwant Bind (Uttar Pradesh).Gajendra Yadav (Delhi), Pramod Madhwaraj (Karnataka), and Lalit Chandrakar (Chhattisgarh) have been named as national general secretaries.The party also appointed seven national secretaries: Dashrathji Thakor (Gujarat), T Varatharajan (Tamil Nadu), Sanjeev Kumar alias Bablu Bhagat (Jharkhand), Sarita Jangid (Haryana), Kadaganchi Ramesh (Telangana), Vaibhav Panwar (Madhya Pradesh), and Bhim Kumar Sahu (Bihar).As part of the organisational appointments, Radheshyam Yadav from Uttar Pradesh has been appointed national treasurer.Sanjay Kumar Gurjar and Dr Arun Yadav, both from Delhi, have been named national office secretary and co-office secretary, respectively. Meanwhile, Ajay Gupta from Bihar has been appointed media coordinator of the Morcha.

headline: PMR to face 100 TMC water demand by 2047, state explores Mulshi diversion, river link | Hindustan Times
content: PUNE:As Maharashtra grapples with severe drought and water scarcity, chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has directed officials to prepare an integrated, time-bound and financially viable long-term water supply plan for the for the Pune Metropolitan Region (PMR) up to 2047 and Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) which will remain valid till 2051.He also sought a feasibility report on the demand for eight TMC (thousand million cubic feet) water for Pune city and other areas of PMR from Mulshi and Khadakwasla dams to resolve the current deficit.In a review meeting on Friday in Mumbai, Fadnavis emphasised that both regions must also focus on reusing treated wastewater, controlling leakages, employing rainwater harvesting, and alternative water sources to ensure future water security.The Pune Metropolitan Region Development Authority (PMRDA) presented its long-term water demand projections, highlighting the widening gap between available water and requirements. The region, with an estimated current population of 1.80 crore, is expected to have 4.12 crore residents by 2047.PMRDA metropolitan commissioner Abhijit Chaudhary said that the region currently has water reservations of 36.90 TMC against an estimated demand of 41.65 TMC. “By 2047, the annual requirement is projected to rise to around 100 TMC, equivalent to 7,816 million litres per day (MLD),” he said during the presentation.Fadnavis directed officials to examine the technical and financial feasibility of bringing around eight TMC of water from the Mulshi dam through a pipeline to the Khadakwasla area. He also asked them to explore river-basin linking and groundwater recharge as part of the long-term water security plan.“Another proposal involves diverting water from the Savitri river basin in the central Konkan towards the Kukadi, Bhima, Indrayani, Mula-Mutha and Nira river basins. The chief minister directed officials to prepare a preliminary project report for the proposed Konkan-to-Bhima river-linking scheme,” a statement from CMO stated.The chief minister also called for greater use of treated sewage to reduce dependence on fresh water. He asked the authorities to plan tertiary treatment of sewage for supply to industries, power plants and data centres, while secondary-treated water should be used for irrigation.Fadnavis said leakage control, smart metering, repair of ageing pipelines and expansion of 24-hour water supply schemes should be prioritised. These measures could save around 350 MLD of water, he said.He also asked civic bodies to conduct water audits and maintain an accurate account of water supplied, distributed and billed. Smart meters should be increasingly introduced for commercial and industrial consumers, while non-revenue water should be reduced in a phased manner.The chief minister stressed that ongoing water projects should be completed on schedule and that clearances, land acquisition and rehabilitation for proposed projects should be pursued simultaneously.The chief minister also proposed the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC) establish a wholly owned subsidiary to manage industrial water supply by sourcing fresh water as well as treated wastewater from municipal sewage treatment plants.Pune Municipal Commissioner Naval Kishore Ram, Pune divisional commissioner Sheetal Teli-Ugale, Pune district collector Jitendra Dudi also attended the meeting.

headline: PM Modi inaugurates ‘Nitish Setu’ in Bihar: What we know about six-lane, cable-stayed bridge | India News
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated a six-lane bridge across the Ganga in Bihar's Vaishali district on Saturday, opening up another major road link between north and south Bihar.Named 'Nitish Setu' after former chief minister Nitish Kumar, the 9.76-km-long structure has been built at a cost of around ₹4,280 crore and will connect Bidupur in Vaishali with Kachchi Dargah in outskirts of Patna, a statement from the Prime Minister's Office read. What we know about the ‘Nitish Setu’The bridge is the main component of a 19.7-km connectivity project linking Kachchi Dargah on NH-22 in Patna district to Bidupur on NH-322 in Vaishali.Built as an extradosed cable-stayed structure, the new crossing is expected to take some of the traffic load off the Mahatma Gandhi Setu and JP Setu. It will also shorten journeys between the two parts of Bihar, particularly for people living in areas that have limited road connectivity with Patna.One of the key beneficiaries is expected to be Raghopur Diara in Vaishali district, which is surrounded by the Ganga and has limited connectivity. The new bridge will give residents easier access to Patna, including hospitals, educational institutions and other essential services, the government release said.The benefits are expected to extend beyond passenger movement. The bridge will provide farmers and businesses in north Bihar with a faster route to markets, improving the transportation of agricultural produce and industrial goods, the release added.The state government also sees the project as an opportunity to strengthen the agricultural economy of north Bihar, a densely populated region with fertile farmland. Easier access to markets could particularly benefit producers of litchis, bananas, maize and vegetables, whose transportation currently faces connectivity-related challenges.Officials also expect the Bidupur-Kachchi Dargah corridor to draw investment by developing into a centre for tourism and logistics, news agency PTI reported.A political fight over nameThe naming of the bridge has triggered a political slugfest between the ruling BJP-JD(U) alliance and the opposition RJD, with both sides disputing who deserves credit for the project. Questioning the decision to name the bridge after the JD(U) chief, RJD working president Yadav alleged that the BJP was attempting to signal that Nitish Kumar's political career was over. “It is well known that when a person is alive, his statues are not erected nor are bridges named after him. So, maybe, they are trying to send across the message that Nitish Kumar is politically finished,” PTI quoted Yadav as saying.RJD leader further claimed that his party had earlier proposed naming the bridge after Akshayvat Rai, a freedom fighter and close associate of former Bihar chief minister Karpoori Thakur."When the project was in its initial stages, Lalu ji and I had requested Nitish Ji to name the bridge after Akshayvat Rai, a freedom fighter who was also a close aide of Karpoori Thakur. I had also written a letter to this effect," Yadav said. The BJP hit back at the RJD leader over his remarks. State party spokesperson Kuntal Krishna called him "an irresponsible leader who chooses to travel abroad while the assembly session is on", and accused his family of corruption."You and your family have only been involved in loot. The bridge is testimony to the development under the leadership of Nitish Kumar and the same is being acknowledged".Bihar deputy chief minister Vijay Kumar Chaudhary also rejected the RJD's attempt to claim a share of credit for the project. The JD(U) leader questioned why the opposition's demand was being given importance and dismissed the argument that Yadav's tenure as deputy chief minister, when he held the road construction portfolio, entitled him to recognition."I am baffled at such a demand and even more baffling is the fact that it is being considered worth discussing," Chaudhary said.The project was first commissioned by Nitish Kumar in 2012, when he was the chief minister of Bihar. However, construction got underway only in 2015.(With PTI inputs)

headline: Ask BJP, JD(S) leaders to show Kadugolla ST certificate, CM Shivakumar tells voters
content: <p>Hiriyur: <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/dk-shivakumar">Chief Minister D K Shivakumar</a> asked voters to boycott leaders of BJP and JD(S) when they visit their households seeking votes for the bypolls and ask them to come to their villages by showing Kadugolla ST certificate. </p><p>Speaking at the Praja Seve event in the town on Saturday, he said JD(S) leaders had claimed that they had a copy of a letter recommending that the Centre accord ST status to the Kadugolla community in their pockets. "Now, you should question them," he said.</p><p>He also claimed that the Congress would demonstrate its commitment in this regard and that the government would once again recommend to the Centre that the Kadugolla community be included in the list of STs.</p>.Karnataka govt to double festival advance for employees to Rs 50,000: CM Shivakumar.<p>Reacting to State BJP president B Y Vijayendra's allegation that Rs 100 crore had been spent on the renovation of Ganga residence in Bengaluru, he said, "If it is true, let Vijayendra conduct a probe and I will form a panel headed by him. Let the BJP leader appoint anyone to the panel and present a report on the expenses incurred on the renovation of the Chief Minister's official residence in the next Assembly session. Let the people of the state know the truth," he added.</p><p>On the demand for the repeal of the Karnataka Prevention of Slaughter and Preservation of Cattle Act, 2020, and the Karnataka Protection of Right to Freedom of Religion Act, 2022, he said, "We have our own policies in this regard and we too protect cows. Why did they (BJP) implement a law that led to the creation of hatred towards the other community? The companies that export meat are still functioning in Uttar Pradesh, and what is the reason for it?" he questioned.</p>

headline: Rijiju hits back at Rahul's 'compromised PM' jibe, asks Congress questions on 1962 war, poverty
content: <p>New Delhi:  Slamming the Congress over <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/rahul-gandhi">Rahul Gandhi</a>'s "compromised PM" remark against Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju on Saturday asked the opposition party to answer four questions, including whether it would apologise for the "1962 humiliation" and why it kept India a "poor nation".</p>.<p>In a post on X, Rijiju said, "Congress must answer 4 questions: My village was occupied by China in 1962. Will Congress apologise for the 1962 humiliation? 2. Congress kept India a poor nation. Why? 3. Why was India called the land of snake charmers? 4. Why was India's economy insulted as Hindu rate of growth?"</p>.<p>Rijiju's remarks came after Gandhi took a swipe at Modi over a trilateral meeting involving US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China on Thursday.</p>.<p>"If Congress were in power, India's Prime Minister would be sitting at this table. A compromised PM can never sit at this table," Gandhi had said in a post on X, sharing a photograph of the three leaders at the meeting.</p>.<p>Talking to reporters here on Friday, <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/kiren-rijiju">Rijiju </a>also said Gandhi should not make statements against India, whether at home or abroad.</p>.'A compromised PM can never sit at this table': Rahul Gandhi takes dig at PM Modi over Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meet.<p>The Congress leader's remarks triggered a war of words between the BJP and the opposition party, with several BJP leaders accusing Gandhi of being "clueless" about global geopolitics.</p>.<p>The ruling party mocked Gandhi's remarks by sharing an AI-generated image showing the Congress leader serving drinks to the <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/donald-trump">US president</a> at the trilateral meeting in China.</p>.<p>Sharing the image on X, Bharatiya Janata Party's national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia took a dig at Gandhi with the caption, "Kuch aise (Something like this)", accompanied by laughing and fire emojis. </p>

headline: Minister Raghumurthy seeks 2 tmc of Bhadra water to avert drinking water crisis
content: <p>Hiriyur (Chitradurga district): District In-charge Minister T Raghumurthy on Saturday urged Chief Minister D K Shivakumar to release two tmc of water from the Bhadra Reservoir immediately, to protect the interests of farmers and residents of Chitradurga district.</p>.<p>Speaking at the Praja Seva meeting in Hiriyur, he said the district has an allocated share of 12.5 tmc but is entitled to 9.3 tmc based on current water availability. However, only four tmc has been released so far, he said.</p>.<p>Seeking the immediate release of another two tmc as an interim measure, Raghumurthy warned that the difficulties faced by farmers and residents would worsen if water was not made available. Six goshala (cattle shelters) had been established in the district to address fodder shortages amid the prevailing drought, he said.</p>.<p>Raghumurthy recalled that Shivakumar, as Irrigation Minister in the Siddaramaiah-led government, had allocated Rs 4,500 crore for the project.</p>.<p>He noted that 12.5 tmc had been earmarked for the district from the Bhadra Reservoir. Of this, three tmc had been released recently on a trial basis, followed by another one tmc. The releases had drawn the ire of some farmers in Davangere and Shivamogga districts.</p>.<p>Pointing out that farmers in Chitradurga had long been deprived of irrigation facilities, he clarified that the immediate demand was not for agricultural purposes but to meet drinking water requirements. “We are not seeking water for crops. Tankers are having to supply drinking water to 39 villages in Hiriyur taluk. This is why I have requested the CM to release water specifically to fill the lakes and ensure drinking water supply,” he said.</p>.<p><strong>CM inspects grievances</strong></p>.<p>The Praja Seva Andolan, held under the leadership of Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Saturday, succeeded in resolving several issues in the Hiriyur Assembly constituency. The CM personally inspected the grievances and suggested solutions on the spot.</p>.Hiriyur bypoll: D K Shivakumar dares BJP over Upper Bhadra grants.<p>Thousands of people gathered at Nehru Maidan in Hiriyur to meet the CM and submit their grievances. A total of 18 counters belonging to various departments had been set up to receive applications. However, Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, who attended the programme, went directly to the people, personally received their applications and examined their grievances.</p>.<p><strong>50,000 sites</strong></p>.<p>Housing Minister Zameer Ahmed Khan said the department had decided to distribute 50,000 residential sites to eligible beneficiaries. The initial proposal was to allot sites measuring 600 sq ft (20x30). However, the chief minister had directed that the size be increased to 1,200 sq ft to enable poor families to live comfortably. The Cabinet had approved the revised proposal, he said.</p>.D K Shivakumar: The Kanakapura rebel who loved silk shirts .<p><strong>Kadu Golla issue</strong></p>.<p>Rajya Sabha member K C Chandrashekhar said a prominent state leader had raised the demand to include the Kadu Golla community in the Scheduled Tribes list during a discussion in Parliament, but the Centre had rejected the proposal.</p>.<p>He said Shivakumar and other leaders had since held discussions on ways to secure justice for the Kadu Golla community and other similar communities, he said.</p>.Political activity gathers pace in Karnataka ahead of Hiriyur bypoll.<p>Municipal Administration Minister H C Balakrishna, former MLA Poornima Krishnappa, MLAs, MLCs and others were present.</p>.<p><strong>Rs 1,500 cr earmarked for Hiriyur: Minister</strong></p>.<p>Water Resources Minister N Cheluvarayaswamy said a Detailed Project Report (DPR) had been prepared for the modernisation of selected canals of the Vani Vilasa Sagar project, and more than Rs 1,500 crore earmarked for Hiriyur taluk alone.</p>.Hiriyur bypoll: H D Kumaraswamy says no rift with BJP over ticket issue, says talks will happen.<p>Over the past year, the department had sanctioned more than Rs 3,000 crore for various irrigation projects, construction of check dams, canal<br>modernisation and schemes to fill tanks, he said.</p>.<p>Referring to the Upper Bhadra Project, he said the Centre had announced<br>Rs 5,300 crore for the project three years ago, but not a single rupee had been released so far.</p>

headline: Bihar now known for development rather than scams and crimes: PM Modi takes jibe on Congress-RJD
content: <p>Prime Minister <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/narendra-modi">Narendra Modi</a> on Saturday trained guns on Opposition RJD-Congress alliance in <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/india/bihar">Bihar</a>, asserting that the state, under the NDA’s rule, was making news for development and investments 'in place of scams and crimes'.</p><p>Modi addressed a rally in Jafarpatti of Vaishali district, about 50 km from the state capital, where he dedicated to the nation projects worth more than Rs 34,000 crore, including a bridge over the Ganga. The bridge has been named 'Nitish Setu'.</p><p>The PM said that he was short on time and had to visit the adjoining Uttar Pradesh.</p><p>He said the bridge was named after the JD(U) president, who gave up the post of chief minister in April to make way for a BJP-helmed government, “as a mark of respect for his contributions to the state”.</p>.In last 12 years, India has shown it can break limits, unlock possibilities: PM Modi.<p>“The state has come a long way since the NDA took over. Earlier, only scams and crimes were talked about. Now Bihar makes news for investment proposals and action taken against those who indulge in any type of wrongdoing," he said.</p>.<p>Modi, who was speaking in an area falling under the Hajipur Lok Sabha constituency, represented by Union minister Chirag Paswan, also recalled the contributions of the latter’s late father Ram Vilas Paswan, who had represented the parliamentary seat several times.</p>.<p>The PM also trained his guns at the Congress, accusing it of having “misled people with slogans of garibi hatao”, drawing a contrast with the NDA government at the Centre over the last 12 years during which “50 crore people have moved out of the clutches of poverty”.</p><p><em>(With PTI inputs)</em></p>

headline: From BJP pressure to Congress warmth: How Tamil Nadu CM Vijay charts selective political course
content:
Chennai: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay attending the launch of Sonia Gandhi’s memoir in New Delhi earlier this week, and the importance accorded to him by the Congress, are significant in more ways than one.

Vijay sent out a strong political message to the BJP that he will continue to stand with the Congress politically, albeit for now, despite the saffron party warning him about the“untrustworthiness” of the national party.

The message from Vijay to the Congress was that though he is dependent on the party’s five MLAs to run his government in Tamil Nadu, he will not toe a blanket “anti-BJP” line day in and day out.

headline: Sanjay Raut's proposal to rename Nagpur as Deekshabhoomi gets Congress backing
content: <p><a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/shiv-sena-ubt">Shiv Sena (UBT)</a> Rajya Sabha MP and senior leader Sanjay Raut on Friday demanded that Nagpur be renamed Deekshabhoomi.</p><p>The leader’s demand comes as the Maharashtra government moves to rename Dadar Metro station in Mumbai to Chaityabhoomi.</p><p>Speaking at the press conference, Raut said that renaming Nagpur to Deekshabhoomi would be the biggest honour to <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/b-r-ambedkar">Dr Ambedkar</a>.</p>.Maharashtra government forms CM-led panel to suggest names of metro stations in Mumbai, Pune and Nagpur.<p>Dr B R Ambedkar, the chief architect of the Constitution, converted to Buddhism along with his followers in Nagpur in October 1956.</p><p>“Dadar is just a station. The biggest honour to Dr Ambedkar would be to change Nagpur’s name to Deekshabhoomi. The chief minister should bring a proposal, and we will support it. Social revolution in Dr Ambedkar’s life began at Deekshabhoomi in Nagpur. We will stand by the government on this if any conflict arises on the issue,” Raut said.</p><p>Recently, the<a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/devendra-fadnavis"> Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis</a> said the Dadar Metro station in Mumbai would be renamed Chaityabhoomi after completing the necessary procedures.</p><p>Dr Ambedkar was cremated at Chaityabhoomi in central Mumbai’s Dadar area following his death in December 1956.</p>.Maharashtra CM Fadnavis announces Rs 23,487 cr metro line to Gateway of India, underground tunnel network.<p>According to a Government Resolution (GR) issued by the Urban Development Department (UDD) on November 18, the Maharashtra government has constituted a six-member committee headed by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis to recommend to the Centre the naming and potential rechristening of metro railway stations in Mumbai, Pune and Nagpur metropolitan regions.</p><p>Backing <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/sanjay-raut">Sanjay Raut</a>’s demand to change the name of Nagpur to Deekshabhoomi, Congress leader Vijay Wadettiwar asked, What is the problem in changing the name to Deekshabhoomi?</p><p>Dr Ambedkar wrote the Constitution in a way that no dictator can end democracy in the country, he said, adding that people across the globe visit Deekshabhoomi.</p><p>Meanwhile, Maharashtra BJP spokesperson Navnath Ban said Raut should first welcome renaming Dadar Metro station as Chaityabhoomi. Lashing out at Raut, he said, “He (Raut) never goes to Chaityabhoomi, nor does he propagate Dr Ambedkar’s thoughts. Such people have no right to speak on the issue.”</p><p>Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders are using the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) as a proxy and opposing the plan to change the name of Dadar Metro station to Chaityabhoomi, he said.</p><p>Chandrashekhar Bawankule, Maharashtra minister and senior BJP leader, said Nagpur is known for Deekshabhoomi. “Every person who comes to Nagpur goes to Deekshabhoomi,” he said.</p>

headline: Maharashtra government forms CM-led panel to suggest names of metro stations in Mumbai, Pune and Nagpur
content: <p>Mumbai: The Maharashtra government has constituted a six-member committee headed by <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/devendra-fadnavis">Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis</a> to recommend to the Centre the naming and potential rechristening of metro railway stations in Mumbai, Pune and Nagpur metropolitan regions.</p>.<p>The panel has been asked to consider the cultural, historical and geographical significance of an area, local public sentiments and the need to avoid controversy while recommending names, according to a Government Resolution (GR) issued by the Urban Development Department (UDD) on November 18.</p>.<p><a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/eknath-shinde">Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde</a>, who holds the UDD portfolio, will be the co-chairperson of the panel.</p>.A track change for Bengaluru's metro viability.<p>The other members will include the Lok Sabha MP and MLA from the area concerned and the mayor or chairperson of the respective local self-government body, while the administrative head of the metro project implementing agency will act as Member-Secretary of the committee.</p>.<p>The committee will function under Rule 3(1) of the Centre's Metro Rail (Naming or Renaming of Stations) Rules, 2026, notified by the Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs in March this year.</p>.<p>As per the rules, the panel must consider six criteria, including cultural heritage, historical and geographical significance, sentiments of local residents, ease of pronunciation and consistency with the locality's identity, while suggesting names or renames of metro stations.</p>.Maharashtra woman gets 4.5 acres back after 30-year land dispute over Rs 25,000 loan.<p>It will also have to avoid confusion arising from identical or similar-sounding station names and balance the symbolic representation of leaders or deities without triggering a controversy, according to the GR.</p>.<p>Under the standard operating procedure, metro railway managements or implementing agencies will first scrutinise representations received for naming or renaming stations and submit detailed proposals to the state government.</p>.<p>The state UDD will place these proposals before the committee, whose recommendations will subsequently be forwarded to the Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs for approval. </p>

headline:
Satheesan’s exclusion from Mahila
Congress event in Thiruvananthapuram sparks row
content: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: The Kerala Jantar Mantar, to be organised by the Mahila Congress state committee in the state capital on Saturday, has sparked a controversy for not inviting Chief Minister V D Satheesan to the event. Following the announcement of the event, Mahila Congress general secretary Sheeba Ramachandran, openly protested and expressed her displeasure over the move and criticised the party’s women’s wing president over the manner in which the event is being organised.“Leaders ranging from Mahila Congress state president Jebi Mather MP, to KPCC president Sunny Joseph and many others were directly invited to the ‘Kerala Jantar Mantar’ protest. Satheesan was the only one not invited. I register my strong protest against organising such a programme that would trigger factionalism in the party,” she wrote on Facebook, indicating that Jebi Mather favouring K C Venugopal was the reason for not inviting the chief minister to the event.Kerala Jantar Mantar, to be held on Saturday near the Lok Bhavan, will be inaugurated by AICC general secretary K C Venugopal. The event is being organised in connection with the Congress’ nationwide protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. “Kerala has a UDF chief minister. When the programme is being organised in the state capital, political courtesy demands that he too should be invited. What we need is politics of inclusiveness, not unilateral decisions. Even Rahul Gandhi ensures that everyone is taken along in such programmes,” Sheeba added. .Meanwhile, Gayathri V Nair, the Thiruvananthapuram district president of the Mahila Congress, said that there was no deliberate attempt to exclude anyone from the event.“This is an event organised to declare our solidarity with Rahulji in the fight against Gyanesh Kumar. There is no deliberate attempt to exclude the CM or anyone from the event,” she told TNIE. Though TNIE contacted Mahila Congress state president Jebi Mather, she was not available for comments.Sources within the Mahila Congress defended the move. “When we organise an event, we need to look at the schedule of the CM too. No one is deliberately excluded from the event. He is our CM, so how will the Mahila Congress exclude him from the event,” the source asked..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Convene all-party meet, take up issue with PM, DMK chief Stalin urges CM Vijay
content: CHENNAI: Expressing concern over the dismissal of two petitions filed by the Tamil Nadu government seeking directions to Karnataka to release 11 tmcft of water, DMK president MK Stalin on Friday once again urged Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay to convene an all-party meeting to discuss the Cauvery water dispute, pass resolutions and take up the issue with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.The DMK president asked what the CM has done to establish Tamil Nadu’s rights over the Cauvery water and what plans he has to safeguard the standing crops. “The extent of Kuruvai paddy cultivation area dropped by 94%. Farmers have been forced to buy water for irrigation,” he said in his social media post. The former CM also asked when Vijay would announce relief assistance to the farmers and also a full waiver of crop loans. He urged the CM to respond to the tears of the farmers instead of shirking his responsibilities and enjoying the comforts of power with zero accountability.Reacting to the development, MP and AIADMK lawyers wing secretary IS Inbadurai also questioned why the TVK government had rushed to approach the Supreme Court instead of exerting appropriate pressure on the Karnataka government through the Cauvery Water Management Authority to secure Tamil Nadu’s rightful share of water in accordance with the top court’s final verdict. In a social media post, Inbadurai asked why the government is undermining the Cauvery rights secured through arduous legal struggle by former CM J Jayalalithaa. .Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: 'Congress misled poor; my government moved 50 crore people out of poverty', says PM Modi in Bihar
content: PATNA: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday launched a blistering attack on Congress’s alleged failure to eradicate poverty despite ruling the country for decades. "Instead, it was my government working with good intentions that moved 50 crore people out of poverty," he asserted. After dedicating the “Nitish Setu” to the nation and unveiling various development projects worth Rs 34,470 crore in Bihar. Addressing a gathering at Rajapakar in Vaishali district, Modi acknowledged former chief minister Nitish Kumar’s various initiatives for the growth of Bihar.Talking about Nitish’s initiative for development, the Prime Minister said that Bihar’s people had lost their hope and faith over three decades ago as the State suffered despair for decades. “Bihar became confident of ‘Sushshan’ only under Nitish’s leadership,” he added.He said that Bihar was progressing fast with the efforts being made by the Chief Minister (Samrat Choudhary) and his team and with the blessings of Nitish Kumar. “Before the NDA came to the power in the state in 2005, the scams were counted, but now the investment data is counted; the earlier state was known for crime data; now action against criminals is in focus,” he remarked..Biharis have full faith in PM Modi's leadership despite abuses hurled by Cong: CM Samrat Choudhary.Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: CM Revanth's Rally rattled Harish: Telangana Congress
content: HYDERABAD: Accusing the BRS of exploiting Telangana sentiment for political gain, Congress MLAs on Friday slammed the pink party’s president K Chandrashekar Rao and senior leader Harish Rao for corruption and misgovernance.Addressing a press conference at the CLP office in Hyderabad on Friday, Warangal West MLA Nayini Rajender Reddy alleged that the KCR family had accumulated vast wealth during its decade in power through irregularities involving government land, RTC properties, liquor and sand businesses. He challenged Harish to an open debate on the 10 years of BRS rule and the Congress government’s three-year tenure. He also demanded that KCR attend Assembly sessions instead of drawing a salary while staying at his farmhouse.Government Whip Vemula Veeresham said the turnout at Chief Minister Revanth Reddy’s Siddipet meeting had rattled Harish, citing Rs 540 crore worth of development works and a Rs 200 crore integrated school. He challenged Harish to swear at Yellamma temple that he had not held talks with the BJP.Veeresham accused the BRS of compromising Telangana’s irrigation interests in Krishna water allocation, corruption in sheep distribution and KCR Kits.Shadnagar MLA Veerlapalli Shankar alleged that the BRS had left Telangana with Rs 8 lakh crore in debt without delivering adequate benefits to the people. He questioned the source of the party’s reported Rs 1,500 crore funds and criticised the Kaleshwaram project..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: 100 days since Monsoon session, PM, HM still seeking 'supertainted' majority for delimitation bill: Congress
content: The Congress on Saturday said that even 100 days after the Monsoon session of Parliament was adjourned sine die, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah continued to seek a "supertainted" two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha to push through the delimitation bill.Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said it is in the nation's interest to let the current Lok Sabha strength and state-wise configuration continue with one-third reservation for women implemented till the Viksit Bharat objective is achieved."Today is the 100th day since the 2026 Monsoon Session of Parliament was adjourned sine die and has not been prorogued."The PM-HM jodi is still in search of a supertainted two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha to get the Constitutional Amendment Bill on Delimitation passed," he said in a post on X.The Congress leader said that nobody knows what the new Bill will contain since the old Bill was defeated “resoundingly” on April 17.He said no new specific proposals have been discussed with any political party “in a serious and structured manner”, and added that an all-party meeting has not been called, “despite four letters to the PM from Mallikarjun Kharge”.."There are far more serious and pressing economic, political, social, military and foreign policy challenges that await and demand attention. Far-reaching and comprehensive Delimitation can wait. Indira Gandhi put it off for 25 years in 1976. In 2001, Atal Bihari Vajpayee put it off for a further twenty-five years, that is, till the results of the first census after 2026 are published. They were wise and nationalist PMs," Ramesh said in his post.He recalled that the Prime Minister expressed grave concerns about the state of the economy at the FICCI conclave on November 19."He seems to be in a very disturbed state of mind, as indeed he should be. Debate and discussions on delimitation require cool heads unburdened by tensions of the type that are preoccupying the PM. Extensive consultations with various stakeholders are also needed."Under the circumstances, it is in the nation's interest to let the current Lok Sabha strength and state-wise configuration continue with one-third reservation for women implemented. This arrangement should then remain frozen till the much-trumpeted Viksit Bharat objective is achieved. It will be a fitting tribute to it since the consequences of a fundamentally new delimitation can best be managed in an environment when Viksit Bharat has become a reality," the Congress leader said.(With inputs from PTI).Congress alleges prorogation record set to give time to Shah to 'manipulate' numbers for delimitation bills.Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Kalakshetram for Arts, Not Government Offices, Says CM Revanth
content: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has made it clear that the Kaloji Kalakshetram, built in memory of the noted people’s poet Kaloji Narayana Rao, should be used exclusively for art, literature, and cultural activities and not for housing government offices. Responding to reports about a proposal to shift government offices to the cultural complex, the Chief Minister directly intervened and instructed Hanamkonda collector Chahat Bajpai not to take any steps in that direction. Revanth Reddy’s intervention assumes significance amid growing discussions over the proposed use of the Kalakshetram premises for government offices. Stressing that the complex has been built to promote art, literature and culture, the Chief Minister made it clear that its original purpose should not be diluted for administrative requirements. He went on to direct the collector to hold consultations with members of the Kaloji Foundation and finalise a clear plan for organising cultural programmes at the venue. He maintained that all activities at the Kalakshetram should reflect the vision behind its construction and uphold the ideals of Kaloji Narayana Rao. Revanth Reddy’s latest directions have put an end to the uncertainty over the proposed relocation of government offices to Kalakshetram premises.

headline: Kerala Health Minister K. Muraleedharan Backs CM V.D. Satheesan Amid Cabinet Rift Reports
content: Thiruvananthapuram: Kerala Health Minister K Muraleedharan has strongly defended Chief Minister V D Satheesan amid reports of internal differences in the cabinet, asserting that the government will complete its full five-year term."The government led by V D Satheesan will complete its five-year term.Whatever anyone tries, nothing will change," Muraleedharan told reporters.He added that the Chief Minister enjoys the support of both the Cabinet and the people of the state and will continue to move forward firmly.Muraleedharan's remarks come after a section of Congress leaders, including UDF Convenor Adoor Prakash, criticised Satheesan's style of functioning, alleging a lack of consultation on important decisions.At the Cabinet meeting on November 18, some ministers reportedly questioned the Chief Minister's approach on issues such as appointing people in key positions, including the Public Service Commission and the recent power crisis.Muraleedharan is said to have backed Satheesan during that meeting.Describing differences of opinion as natural in a democracy, the Health Minister said criticism was part of the system.He also dismissed the online attacks directed at certain ministers following reports of Cabinet discord, noting that no one was taking the cyber criticism seriously."I have faced similar attacks on social media, but I have not let them affect me in any way," the minister said.

headline: Rijiju Hits Back At Rahul Over 'Compromised PM' Remark
content: NEW DELHI: Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Saturday attacked the Congress over Rahul Gandhi's “compromised PM” remark against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and demanded an apology from the Opposition party for India's defeat in the 1962 war with China.In a post on X, Rijiju posed four questions to the Congress, including why India remained poor during its rule and why the country's economic growth had been described as the “Hindu rate of growth”. “My village was occupied by China in 1962. Will Congress apologise for the 1962 humiliation?” he asked. Rijiju alleged that the Congress had abandoned the armed forces and the people of Arunachal Pradesh during the 1962 India-China war. “We'll never forget 1962 humiliation. Congress left the armed forces and people of Arunachal Pradesh to fend for themselves in 1962. This is a big lesson for us,” he said. His remarks followed Gandhi's criticism of Modi over a trilateral meeting involving US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China. Sharing a photograph of the three leaders, Gandhi had said: “If Congress were in power, India's Prime Minister would be sitting at this table. A compromised PM can never sit at this table.” Rijiju said Gandhi should refrain from making statements against India, whether at home or abroad. The exchange triggered a fresh political confrontation between the BJP and Congress, with several BJP leaders criticising Gandhi's understanding of international affairs. BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia also shared an AI-generated image depicting Gandhi serving drinks to the US President at the trilateral meeting, accompanied by a mocking caption.

headline: Anti-SIR Stir: INDIA Bloc to Hold Major Rally in MP on December 12
content: The INDIA bloc is set to hold a major rally in Bhopal on December 12 as part of its ongoing nationwide campaign against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. A preparatory meeting for organizing the ‘mega rally’ was held at the state Congress headquarters here late on Friday. Madhya Pradesh Congress president Jitu Patwari and other senior leaders of the party here attended the meeting. Under the banner of the INDIA bloc, the Congress is going to organize a ‘Vote Suraksha’ march here followed by a joint public meeting, senior Congress leader K K Mishra said on Saturday. Mr. Patwari has set a target of mobilizing more than one lakh people for the Bhopal event of the INDIA bloc. According to the Congress leader, Leader of Opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, senior Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and other senior INDIA bloc leaders such as Samajwadi Party (SP) chief and former chief minister Akhilesh Yadav, Trinamool Congress (TMC) supremo and former chief minister Mamata Banerjee, Shiv Sena (UBT) chief and former chief minister Uddhav Thakre are expected to attend the rally. The decision to hold the joint rally in Bhopal was finalized during a meeting in Delhi. This is the first of a series of major rallies planned in different states by the INDIA bloc to protest against the SIR, according to the Congress leader. The INDIA bloc launched a nationwide campaign on October two against the SIR, by holding protest marches and public meetings at district headquarters. Meanwhile, the state Congress has decided to shift the venue of its ‘Constitution Protection March’, originally scheduled for November 26 in Bhopal, to Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh.

headline: Maharashtra BJP MLA Krishna Khopde Writes To CM Devendra Fadnavis Seeking Ban On Sonia Gandhi’s Memoir Over
content: Nagpur, Nov 21: BJP MLA Krishna Khopde said that he has written to the Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, demanding a ban on sale of senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s memoir 'Belonging: A Journey of Love' in the state, alleging that the contents of the book could incite communal tensions in the state and the country. Speaking to IANS, Khopde said: "Sonia Gandhi had published the book as an autobiography, but it contains issues that could disturb the country's environment and potentially trigger riots."He claimed that the book had been published as part of a "well-thought-out plan".Questioning Sonia Gandhi's awareness about India’s culture, Khopde said: "Countless people have sacrificed their lives for the country's independence, yet she appeared unaware of their contributions. Many revolutionaries devoted and sacrificed everything, including their families, for the nation, but their sacrifices were not reflected in her understanding."Referring to remarks on Veer Savarkar in Sonia Gandhi's book, the BJP legislator claimed that Sonia Gandhi lacked knowledge about the role and sacrifices of the Hindutva ideologue.According to him, Sonia Gandhi should have first understood Indian culture and studied the country's struggle against colonial rule before releasing her book.Khopde also remarked that the Congress leader has no direct connection with India by birth, given her Italian origin, adding that understanding Indian culture is not easy and that even distinguished individuals find it challenging to grasp its depth.Noting that political autobiographies usually discuss a leader's personal journey, achievements in office, developmental work, benefits provided to the public, and future plans, the BJP legislator also criticised the Congress Parliamentary Party Chairperson for including several topics in her book that he described as "objectionable".He said that anyone reading the book would conclude that she (Sonia Gandhi) had made a "mistake".Khopde added that instead of addressing such issues, Sonia Gandhi should have reflected on the ideology and decline of the Congress party.Eight Minors Booked For Allegedly Assaulting Couple With Hockey Sticks And Stones At Kurla Garden, Six Detained | Video"Congress once held around 400 seats but has now fallen below 100 and has been wiped out in several states. In Maharashtra too, the party had suffered a significant decline. If Sonia Gandhi had analysed the differences between the Congress of the past and the present, it might have benefited the party. Instead, including subjects capable of creating a divisive atmosphere and provoking unrest for political gain was unfortunate," he said.Khopde claimed that the then-Congress leadership at the Centre "attempted to suppress" the incidents related to the 2002 Godhra riots and also accused the party's 1984 leadership of supporting the anti-Sikh riots, in the aftermath of the assassination of former Prime Minister late Indira Gandhi.Referring to Sonia Gandhi's remark that she was moved to tears following the demolition of the Babri Masjid, the BJP legislator also accused the Congress of delaying the construction of the Ram Temple for many years."Sonia Gandhi has never spoken about the temple, not visited Ayodhya to offer prayers at the Ram Temple," Khopde said while describing it as a "prejudiced mindset".Level up your brain the fun way. headline: What Kind Of PM Talks About Toilets?: PM Modi Recalls Being Mocked In Parliament Over Promise To Build
content: Kharagpur: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday recalled being mocked in Parliament for announcing the construction of toilets for the poor, saying that his government had worked over the past 12 years to change the mindset that poverty could not be eradicated in a country as populous as India.PM Modi Unveils Commemorative Coin At IIT Kharagpur's 75th Anniversary, Highlights Institute's Role In India's Self-Reliance Journey | Watch Addressing the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur, PM Modi said that poverty had long been considered a permanent problem, with policy decisions often failing to translate into action because of this prevailing mindset. "India has declared, loud and clear, break the limit, unlock the possibilities. Until 20 years ago, poverty was considered a permanent problem in our country. Five decades ago, slogans about eradicating poverty were being raised from the ramparts of the Red Fort. Yet, whenever it came to taking action at the policy level, the entire system would simply bury the matter in files. This was because the prevailing mindset was that poverty could never be eradicated, especially given the size of our population. No one even dared to implement the right policies to actually eliminate poverty," he said.Recalling his announcement from the Red Fort after his government first came to power, PM Modi said he had faced criticism for prioritising the construction of toilets for the poor.PM Modi Attends IIT Kharagpur's Platinum Jubilee Celebrations, Interacts With Students As Institute Marks 75 Years Of Excellence | Video "When we first came to power, I announced from the Red Fort that I would build toilets for the poor. In Parliament, people mocked this, asking, 'What kind of Prime Minister is this? He's talking about building toilets.' Such people failed to grasp how essential a toilet is, how critical it is for the poor, and especially for poor women and mothers," he said.He said his government had worked to change this mindset over the past 12 years, adding that he followed the guiding principle of "Power to Empower".The Prime Minister also cited a recent World Bank report, saying it stated that 50 crore people in India had been lifted out of poverty in 12 to 13 years. "You must have read or heard about the recent World Bank report. The World Bank has stated that in just 12 to 13 years, 50 crore people in India have been lifted out of poverty. This is no small change; it is the outcome of a mindset that advocates for breaking the limits," he said.PM Modi further urged students and alumni of IIT Kharagpur to adopt the mindset of "Nation First", saying their efforts should contribute to the country's progress as well as create new opportunities for themselves. "You have done outstanding work over the past 75 years. Now you must move forward with the firm resolve that when IIT Kharagpur celebrates its 100th anniversary, it should do so in a developed India," he said.Speaking about India's growing space sector, the Prime Minister said the government had opened it up to young people, enabling startups to contribute to the country's space programme.He cited the example of Pawan Kumar Chandana, an IIT Kharagpur alumnus and co-founder of Skyroot Aerospace, which developed India's first privately built rocket. "We have opened up India's space sector to India's youth, and today, look at Pawan, a student from IIT Kharagpur, who founded Skyroot Aerospace and brought India the distinction of launching its first private rocket. Today, many such space startups are propelling India's space programme forward at a new pace," he said.PM Modi added that developments once considered impossible had become a reality, crediting IIT Kharagpur alumni for their contribution to the country's progress.The Prime Minister also spoke about India's semiconductor ambitions, recalling that a company had approached India 50 years ago to manufacture semiconductors but was turned away. "You will be surprised to know that a company had come to India 50 years ago to manufacture semiconductors. However, it was shown the red flag and sent back. So, when I spoke about launching the Semiconductor Mission, people said it was already too late. We went ahead and initiated the mission, and today, India has begun exporting chips," he said.In another part of his address, PM Modi spoke about the need to overcome what he described as "limiting beliefs", saying individuals and nations must not restrict their aspirations or potential. "Often, people impose boundaries on their own thinking--they set limits for themselves--and these are what we call 'limiting beliefs.' What are limiting beliefs? They mean placing limits on your dreams, on your talents, and even on the potential of your own nation," he said.He added that India had demonstrated in recent years how breaking such mental barriers could help a nation recognise and realise its potential."Those who live with a stagnant, lifeless mindset cannot truly live life at all. We have come to accept the boundaries of our own thinking as the boundaries of our world. A nation, too, recognises its true potential only when it breaks through the limits of its own thinking. In the last few years, India has demonstrated exactly that," the Prime Minister said.Earlier during the Platinum Jubilee celebrations, Prime Minister Narendra Modi unveiled a special commemorative coin marking 75 years of IIT Kharagpur.
