headline: Centre Didnt Give A Single Rupee: Tejashwi Yadav Targets PM Modi Ahead Of Nitish Setu Inauguration,
content: Patna: Ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Vaishali for inaugurating 'Nitish Setu', RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav launched a blistering attack on him, claiming the Centre did not give a single rupee for the project. Taking to "X" to lash out at Modi, Tejashwi said, "Respected Prime Minister, the central government has not contributed a single rupee towards this project.The bridge was inaugurated one year and five months ago by the then chief minister, Nitish Kumar.Bihar Minister Nishant Kumar Allegedly Pushed By CM's Security During Vaishali Visit; JD(U) Demands Probe After Video Goes Viral "The bridge has been operational for the past 17 months, and lakhs of vehicles have crossed it during this period. Are you inaugurating it again merely to have your name included on the foundation plaque, despite the Central Government having made no contribution to the project?" he asked while intensifying his attack on the the PM."According to the Bihar government, the bridge was to be named either after freedom fighter late Akshaywat Rai or the Tenth Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, as it is located close to the latter's birthplace.Therefore, please refrain from trying to take credit for this project and avoid unnecessary self-glorification, as you had no role in either the decision to construct this bridge or its execution." he claimed.

headline: Dont Defame India Out Of Hunger For Power: Ravindra Chavan Slams Rahul Gandhi Over Remarks On PM Modis
content: Mumbai: BJP Maharashtra president Ravindra Chavan on Friday hit back at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his criticism of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership and India’s position on the global stage, accusing him of defaming the country for political gains.'If Congress Were In Power, Indian PM Would Be Sitting...': Rahul Gandhi Takes Swipe At PM Modi Over Trilateral Meeting, Calls Him 'Compromised'Chavan countered Gandhi’s remarks by sharing photographs from two G20 summits, highlighting what he described as the difference between India’s global standing before and after 2014. Gandhi had questioned India’s international role by referring to a photograph featuring US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping together.In response, Chavan shared a photograph from the 2011 G20 summit in France, showing then Prime Minister Manmohan Singh standing in the back row, alongside another from the 2024 G20 summit in Rio de Janeiro, where Modi was seen at the centre of the gathering. He captioned the images as ‘India before 2014’ and ‘India after 2014’.Taking a dig at Gandhi, Chavan said, “When the hunger becomes unbearable, one loses sight of everything else. Rahulji seems to be facing the same situation due to his hunger for power.”'Acts Like Pak Fan Boy': BJP Hits Back At Rahul Gandhi Over 'Side Player' RemarkHe further warned Gandhi against allegedly tarnishing India’s image for political reasons, saying that no true Indian would tolerate such attempts.Chavan maintained that the comparison between the two photographs reflected the change in India's international stature under Modi's leadership, turning the Congress leader's criticism into a fresh political confrontation between the BJP and Congress.To get details on exclusive and budget-friendly property deals in Mumbai & surrounding regions, do visit: https://budgetproperties.in/

headline: India Inc must summon the courage to challenge government policy openly
content: The most apt description for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s mass admonition of corporate India at the Ficci annual general meeting is that it was a cri de coeur. I use this even as I’m reminded of the late and venerable D N Singh, my first news editor at The Indian Express in 1977. He had banned “foreign” words in our writing. English is foreign enough for all of us, he’d say. In this case, however, a cry from the heart doesn’t fully capture where the Prime Minister was coming from. The dictionary tells us that a cri de coeur is more profound. It’s a “passionate, heartfelt appeal, protest, even an outcry”. The Prime Minister spoke in anger, frustration, helplessness even. What more can I do to get you guys moving? It was way more fraught than a mere cry from the heart. It’s a bit like a general failing to implore his troops to assault a hill despite a thousand war cries, words of inspiration, even a dash of “spirit”. Since we started with a bit of French, that “spirit” reference is from the Duke of Wellington at the Battle of Waterloo. While his original line, as recorded in history, was less dramatic, Christopher Plummer, playing Wellington in the 1970 film Waterloo, tells the Duchess of Richmond, who wants to know where his troops get their inspiration to fight: “Gin is the spirit of their patriotism.” I’m avoiding the full quote because the Prime Minister certainly didn’t want to call corporate India ‘scum, beggars and scoundrels,’ as Wellington called his troops. It’s just that his frustration is as profound. What’s the spirit that a government can offer entrepreneurship? It can be many things: Deregulation, minimum government, fair market supervision, fiscal discipline, freedom from licensing and investment restrictions. And certainly, the gin equivalent of this “spiritual” package would be tax cuts. One big cause of Mr Modi’s frustration is corporate India’s unwillingness to pass this benefit on to employees through raises, hiring or investment. This hasn’t happened even as corporate profits have risen. These troops are unwilling, either too scared to assault that hill or simply too comfortable in safety, pocketing the tax breaks. Let’s read some of Mr Modi’s words to Ficci. “In 2014, the basic corporate tax rate was 30 per cent. We reduced it to 22 per cent. Today, there’s no income tax on earnings up to ~12 lakh in India.” And then he turns the knife. “I know you won’t clap, because however much one gives, your appetite never seems to be satisfied. (aap ka pet nahin bharta). Did you increase the salaries of your employees? Did you increase the number of employees? No. The attitude remains: ‘Modi ji, you do it, we will see’.” While India Inc was left licking its wounded pride, the Congress quickly latched on to the Prime Minister’s words. Isn’t this what we’ve been saying all along, it hit back. Jairam Ramesh was first out of the blocks. “For the first time in 12 years, a nervous and rattled PM has pulled up the captains of industry... (who) must have been taken aback and shocked.” In an elaborate post on X, he blamed not businesses but the government for this stall. He blamed it on crony capitalism, regulatory capture, “an atmosphere of fear and intimidation”, and the unleashing of “investigative agencies”. He concluded by suggesting the Prime Minister look inwards. Rahul Gandhi, on his speaking tour in the United States, also said: We told you so. It’s not my place here to hold forth on the state of the economy. But we know corporate India hasn’t been investing, expanding and hiring, at least nowhere near what 7 per cent-plus growth would indicate. Startups are rising, but largely there’s an entrepreneurship freeze. Much of the growth comes from government spending, especially in heavy infrastructure. If corporate India looks so risk-averse, this isn’t a sudden development. The mood has been festering for years. Some complain of a lack of demand, others say regulation is asphyxiating. Still too many forms need to be filled for too many small things, even something as virtuous as exports. Because, I suppose, the Reserve Bank of India wants to track every dollar that comes in. And, of course, everything in triplicate please. The government may have loosened policies here and there, but the bureaucratic grip is tighter than before. A quick quiz, and no Googling. Can you name the ministers of mines, pharmaceuticals and steel? I mention these three because the Prime Minister highlighted corporate India’s failures specifically in these areas. Why do we export raw materials like iron ore, have so much bauxite, yet import finished steel and specialised aluminium alloys? How come, despite robust pharma exports, we remain dependent on China for APIs, or active pharmaceutical ingredients? With key ministers too lightweight or distracted by party work, and power centralised in the PMO, which is obviously far too overburdened to attend to everything, discretion devolves to the bureaucracies. Corporate India is resigned to this. It’s buying peace in the manner it knows best: Distributing some of the spoils in a way that’s entirely legal and above board, but also revealing. Check out the number of retiring secretaries, especially in the finance ministry, finding sinecures on the boards of influential companies and as chairpersons of almost all significant private-sector banks, and the recently listed stock market titan, NSE (National Stock Exchange). The more the Modi government thinks it’s reforming — and reforming it is — the more it does so in a way that passes power into the hands of the bureaucracy. Corporate India buys peace with them in advance, merely by dropping hints. Here’s the paradox. This is a super-strong government with a very weak implementation spine. As a result, what’s decentralised at the top gathers in the middle. A strong government isn’t immune to policy confusion. On the contrary, it can be prone to flip-flop-flips given its overwhelming power. Long term capital gains (LTCG) tax is a big discussion point now. Count how many changes this government has brought in. The same goes for taxes on dividends. Since 1991, successive finance ministers have said that the essence of a reformed economy lies in moderate, predictable taxes. You most certainly cannot say the same about this government, which also taxes individuals at almost twice the rate of corporations. It’s also been breathtaking in its use of sovereign power. A striking example is the retrospective changes it made to sovereign gold bonds to suit itself and cover for those brilliant people who floated these without hedging for gold prices. The message is an old one. In India, the government, the almighty Sarkar-e-Hind, can never be wrong. Corporate India has a lot to answer for, but for some, the chappal is on the government’s foot. On copper and aluminium imports, two of the largest projects have been shut under activist pressure. If this government has failed to move on these, it cannot blame India Inc. Sadly, corporate India knows this, but nobody would dare speak up. They whisper dark things on the sidelines. But in front of an angry Prime Minister, or the finance minister who’s been delivering the same admonitions for two years, they sit silent and contrite, like schoolkids whose homework the dog ate. This isn’t just a Modi-era phenomenon. At the 2007 CII AGM, then Prime Minister Manmohan Singh had chided corporate leaders for paying themselves too much. The irony: The mood and message then were opposite to now. Sunil Mittal, then CII chief, responded by pledging ‘a significant part of his salary bonus’ to charity. I had then written, and repeated in a 2013 column, that corporate India has to grow the spine to tell the Prime Minister he didn’t fix their wages. He should leave them alone if they paid their taxes honestly. Of course, no such thing happened. Corporate India also swallowed that retrograde idea of near-mandatory corporate social responsibility. Even at Ficci, and in the corporate and financial universe, too many good people have too many important points to make. But nobody would dare. Corporate India is waiting for its next Rahul Bajaj. Or preferably a few of them. By special arrangement with ThePrint

headline: Bihar now known for development, not scams and crimes: PM targets Cong-RJD
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday made a stinging attack on the opposition RJD-Congress alliance in Bihar, asserting that the state, under the NDA's rule, was making news for development and investments "in place of scams and crimes".Modi addressed a rally in Jafarpatti of Vaishali district, about 50 km from the state capital, where he dedicated to the nation projects worth more than ₹34,000 crore, including a bridge over the Ganga. The bridge has been named 'Nitish Setu'.The PM, who delivered a relatively short speech, said that he was short on time and had to visit the adjoining Uttar Pradesh.He said the bridge was named after the JD(U) president, who gave up the post of chief minister in April to make way for a BJP-helmed government, "as a mark of respect for his contributions to the state"."The state has come a long way since the NDA took over. Earlier, only scams and crimes were talked about. Now Bihar makes news for investment proposals and action taken against those who indulge in any type of wrongdoing," he said.Modi, who was speaking in an area falling under the Hajipur Lok Sabha constituency, represented by Union minister Chirag Paswan, also recalled the contributions of the latter's late father Ram Vilas Paswan, who had represented the parliamentary seat several times.The PM also trained his guns at the Congress, accusing it of having "misled people with slogans of garibi hatao", drawing a contrast with the NDA government at the Centre over the last 12 years during which "50 crore people have moved out of the clutches of poverty".

headline: PM Modi to launch development projects worth ₹34,470 cr in Bihar's Vaishali
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Bihar's Vaishali district on Saturday to launch projects worth nearly 34,470 crore, including a six-lane bridge over the Ganga river, and address a public meeting, officials said.This would be the Prime Minister's first visit to the eastern state since May, when he had attended a function marking the expansion of the cabinet headed by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, the first BJP leader to lead a government in Bihar.Elaborate security arrangements, including the suspension of vehicular movement on the national and state highways concerned for a stipulated period, have been made in Vaishali and Patna for the PM's visit, they said.The 9.76-km-long six-lane bridge, which connects Bidupur block in Vaishali to Kachchi Dargah on the outskirts of Patna, has been named 'Nitish Setu', in deference to the former Bihar chief minister, on whose watch the project was conceived and came close to completion."The PM will visit 'Nitish Setu' in Vaishali. Thereafter, at around 2 pm, he will inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects and lay the foundation stone of several projects, worth around Rs 34,470 crore altogether," an official said.However, the naming of the bridge has triggered a war of words between the ruling NDA and the main opposition party RJD, which has shared power with Nitish Kumar, albeit briefly, and seeks to claim its own share of credit.The projects span road connectivity, energy, urban infrastructure, water resources, education, healthcare, transport and other important sectors, and are aimed at strengthening infrastructure and improving public services across the state.The PM will flag off 100 PM-eBuses, giving a further boost to cleaner public transport in the state.Griha Pravesh ceremonies for over 26,900 beneficiaries under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) will also be held, marking an important milestone in providing housing to urban families, another official said.

headline: India to host WorldSkills Asia 2027 in Greater Noida, announces PM Modi
content: India will host the WorldSkills Asia competition in Greater Noida in Uttar Pradesh in 2027, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced on Saturday, saying the country was moving towards becoming the world's skill capital.The 48th WorldSkills Competition was held in Shanghai, China, in September 2026. The competition is the world's largest international gathering of skills talent.Addressing the fifth National Skill Convocation here, Modi said the international competition would bring young participants from several Asian countries to Uttar Pradesh."Next year, in 2027, India will host the WorldSkills Asia competition. Young people from across Asia will come here, and this event will be organised in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh," he said.Congratulating Uttar Pradesh in advance for hosting the international event, Modi said the country was progressing towards becoming the world's skill capital."India is moving forward towards becoming the skill capital of the world. And at the centre of this ambition are you," he told the young participants, referring to the country's skilled workforce.Modi said he was speaking not just about India's aspirations but also its potential to contribute to the global skilled workforce.Union defence minister Rajnath Singh, Minister for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Jayant Chaudhary, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak, and UP BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary were also present at the event, among others.

headline: India has shown it can break limits, unlock possibilities: PM Modi
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday said India has shown over the past 12 years that breaking barriers in thinking can help the country realise its potential, create opportunities and empower the poor.Addressing the platinum jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur, the country's first Indian Institute of Technology, here, Modi said India had declared "loud and clear" its resolve to "break the limits and unlock the possibilities"."The nation only understands its capacity when it breaks its limits and unlocks the possibilities," he said.The Prime Minister said that over the last 12 years, his government had worked to break existing limitations and empower the poor."Earlier, people used to talk about removing poverty from the Red Fort, but they never did anything except making files," he said.Referring to a World Bank report, Modi claimed that around 50 crore people had come out of poverty in the last 12-13 years, describing it as a result of a change in the country's approach and thinking."The country discovers its capabilities only when it breaks the boundaries of thinking. Over the past few years, India has shown exactly that," he said.Modi said West Bengal was a land where ideas had gained strength, and national movements had taken shape, adding that IIT Kharagpur stood on a site that once housed a detention camp for freedom fighters.He urged students to draw inspiration from the lives, thoughts and activities of freedom fighters who were detained at the site."Imagine what the freedom fighters who stayed here must have talked about and thought about all day," he told the students, adding that their ideas and sacrifices continued to inspire generations.The PM said the institution had completed 75 years of its journey and achieved several milestones during this period.India, too, had witnessed tremendous transformation over these decades, moving "from bullock carts to bullet trains, from postal letters to social media messages", he said.As India moves towards the goal of a 'Viksit Bharat', IIT Kharagpur's 75 years of experience would play a significant role in the country's development and innovation ecosystem, Modi said.The institute's contribution to education, research and technological advancement would be important in shaping India's future, he added.

headline: ITI graduates deserve same respect as IIT alumni, says PM Narendra Modi
content: Underlining the imperative of skilling in an AI-driven world, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday asserted that he was striving to accord the same respect to Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) as to the premier Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs). Addressing the '5th Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh' in Lucknow on Saturday evening, Modi said that while only a handful possessed "paper certificates" (purporting to high-value degrees), big corporations were functioning owing to a workforce of 200-300 ITI pass-outs. "Today, doomsayers are talking about job losses due to AI, but no one can take away the jobs of those having skills," he predicted. Lamenting that the parents of ITI students felt embarrassed by the ITI tag, the PM said he was determined to alter the status quo in favour of the skilling ecosystem. He waxed eloquent on the traditional craftsmanship of India, including chikankari of Lucknow, pashmina of Kashmir, Kanjeevaram of Tamil Nadu, etc., saying the ancient Indian societal fabric centred around skills. Modi noted that the invaders' first assault was on our skills, while the education system later introduced by the British under Macaulay was focused on churning out clerks. "As a result, we started focussing on clerical jobs, and the skills took a back-seat due to our slavery mindset," the PM underlined. Further, Modi claimed that the trade deals India was inking with foreign countries encompassed a high demand for Indian skilled workers in such offshore geographies. "These countries do not require people with university degrees but ITI workers possessing skills," Modi added. He said the Gulf countries also acknowledged that their sparkling cities and flagship projects were possible only due to Indian skilled workers and not their wealth. Modi recalled that in 2023, he had nudged people to invest in PSUs, while last year he had urged people to defer gold purchases. He claimed both his statements had proved true to the benefit of people. "Today, I am making another statement. More than the suited-booted, carrying paper certificates, those people with skills will command greater respect, and they will be in high demand," he asserted. The PM opined that the dream of Viksit Bharat in another 20 years would be based on skills. "Earlier, India imported mobile phones, today Made in India mobile phones are exported globally." Since 2014, more than 5,000 new ITIs have been set up, while an additional 0.5 million students have been enrolled, even as 30 new trades are being taught, he claimed. These include aeronautical, cyber security, drone and green hydrogen, semiconductor technicians, etc. He said 500 million people had come out of poverty in India, which was a big achievement and one that would pave the path to becoming a developed nation. Talking about the Gulf crisis, he said plumbers were in short supply in India for piped natural gas (PNG) connections. "India is progressing to becoming the skills capital of the world owing to you people (ITI students)," Modi said. Next year, India will host the World Skills Competition in Greater Noida. Modi's remarks came against the backdrop of his recently questioning India Inc for not raising employee salaries or expanding its workforce despite receiving tax relief and benefiting from an improved business environment. In 2014, the corporate tax rate was 30 per cent; we reduced it to 22 per cent. For income up to ₹12 lakh, there is no income tax. "But your hunger is such that, no matter how much you are fed, your stomach is not full. Have you increased the salaries of your employees? Have you increased your number of employees?” Modi asked at a Ficci event in New Delhi. Instituted in the 2021-22 academic session, the Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh has emerged as an annual national platform to recognise excellence in skill development and celebrate the transition of skilled youth from training to the world of work. Since its inception, the platform has felicitated all-India toppers and high achievers from the skill development ecosystem, fostering a culture of pride, achievement and aspiration around vocational education and skilled careers. This year, 52 national-level toppers from Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs) and Institutes for Training of Trainers (IToTs) were felicitated for their outstanding achievements.

headline: Delhi air quality this year better than in past decade: CM Rekha Gupta
content: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said strict enforcement and regulations had improved the city's air quality this year compared to the past 10 years.Gupta's remarks came after inaugurating a new academic block at Kamla Nehru College and university-special buses for students."In Delhi over the last 10 years, the AQI is better this year, and the people of Delhi are feeling a sense of relief this time. This is an achievement for Delhi. This was achieved by enforcing strictness; we introduced the necessary rules, regulations, and policies that were needed," Gupta said, addressing students.The chief minister also said that the government is working to construct hostels to accommodate 10,000 students and add more U-special buses across the city."U-special buses were not available in the city for the past 25 years. When our government came to power, this was one of our priorities. Today, we have also achieved 75 per cent electric vehicles in public transport," Gupta added.Gupta also highlighted women helming important posts in the country."The President of the country is a woman; we see women gracing many significant and prestigious positions. From agriculture to Chandrayaan, women and daughters of the country are leading the way," she said.The chief minister also announced the government has set a target to end the three mountains of garbage (landfill sites) by the end of 2027.

headline: PM Modi's ‘insatiable hunger for concessions’ remark rattles India Inc; companies prepare to defend jobs, salary growth
content: After Prime Minister Narendra Modi criticised India Inc for failing to translate government tax relief into higher employment and salaries, corporate executives were still assessing the implications of his remarks, with some fearing that the government could become less receptive to future demands for tax concessions.Modi's comment about the industry's "insatiable hunger for concessions" at a Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) event reportedly caught business leaders off guard. Several executives are now interpreting the statement as a clear indication that the government expects greater contributions from companies in return for the policy support extended to them.Industry representatives are expected to compile data in the coming weeks to demonstrate improvements in employment generation and wage growth. "It's a signal to back off before the budget," said an industry veteran, according to a Times of India report. Industry cites rising input costs and currency pressures Corporate executives have pointed to several challenges that businesses have faced, including higher fuel and raw material costs and the impact of rupee depreciation. They argue that these pressures have affected companies' ability to expand operations and increase employee compensation. Government sources, however, acknowledged the difficulties faced by businesses while maintaining that the corporate sector could have done more to reciprocate the support provided by the government to help companies expand and compete internationally, according to the Times of India report. Officials have highlighted measures such as reductions in direct taxes and Goods and Services Tax (GST) rates, along with initiatives to improve the ease of doing business. They believe these steps have created favourable conditions for companies to accelerate growth, according to the Times of India report. Government pushes companies to increase salaries and employment Modi's remarks are being viewed as an attempt to encourage companies to improve real incomes, an issue that has remained a concern for employees and workers since the Covid-19 pandemic. The government's concerns are also reflected in the Economic Survey 2025, which highlighted that corporate profitability had reached a 15-year high in 2024, even as the growth in employee expenses moderated. The issue has brought the relationship between corporate profitability, employment generation and wage growth into sharper focus. Employment and employee compensation show improvement Data from the Annual Survey of Industries indicates that employment growth was estimated at 5.6% in 2023-24, while employee emoluments increased 11.8%. Corporate profits rose 10% during the same period. The latest survey data showed further improvement in employment and compensation in 2024-25. The number of persons engaged in the industrial sector increased 7.2% to 2.1 crore, while total employee emoluments rose 12.1% to ₹8 lakh crore. Industrial profits also increased 7.7% to ₹11.6 lakh crore, indicating continued growth in corporate earnings. Private investment remains a concern despite consumption recovery The government and industry have repeatedly differed over the pace of private-sector investment in recent years, with policymakers expressing concerns that companies have not invested enough despite favourable economic conditions. However, private-sector activity has shown signs of improvement in recent months. Lower GST rates have supported consumption demand, helping businesses navigate global economic uncertainties. Modi's latest remarks signal that the government now expects corporate India to translate policy support and improved profitability into stronger investment, more jobs and better wage growth.

headline: Meta offices in Gurugram, Hyderabad, Mumbai see protests from Congress's youth wing: Here's why
content: The Indian Youth Congress (IYC) staged protests outside Meta offices in Gurugram, Hyderabad and Mumbai after the social media giant allegedly removed Instagram accounts belonging to some of its members, escalating the party's confrontation with the company in India, its largest market by users.The protests came amid growing concerns over social media censorship and freedom of expression in India, with the Congress accusing Meta and other platforms of restricting dissenting voices and allegedly favouring Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.According to footage shared by the youth wing on Saturday, Congress workers in Hyderabad entered a building housing Meta's offices on Friday, raised slogans and clashed with police. Some protesters were seen smashing plants during the demonstration.In Mumbai, another video showed Congress workers spray-painting anti-Meta slogans on walls outside the building housing the company's office. They also confronted security guards who attempted to stop them.In Gurugram, near New Delhi, IYC members staged a demonstration carrying banners that read "restore youth Congress accounts" and raised slogans against the company, according to posts shared online by the organisation.Why is Congress protesting against Meta?The demonstrations followed Meta's removal of Instagram accounts belonging to some Indian Youth Congress members. The party has alleged that social media platforms are restricting its leaders' accounts and suppressing political dissent.The IYC also issued a warning on X, threatening to "storm your offices across the country and stage protests" unless Instagram accounts belonging to its leaders were restored.Two of the accounts were reinstated following Friday's demonstrations. However, thousands of accounts belonging to journalists, content creators and influencers critical of the government remain restricted, Manu Jain, who oversees social media for the youth organisation, told Reuters on Saturday.Jain also demanded that Meta explain how its algorithms restrict posts and restore accounts removed following government orders.Congress has repeatedly accused Meta and other social media companies of curbing online dissent while allegedly favouring the ruling party. Meta, however, has maintained that it restricts content in India to comply with local laws.BJP accuses Congress of vandalising Meta officeThe protests triggered a political backlash from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).Pradeep Bhandari, a national spokesperson for the ruling party, criticised Congress on Saturday, alleging that its workers had "not only vandalised and destroyed Meta's office in Hyderabad" but were also "flaunting it on social media"."This is Congress Model: Vandalise offices of Private companies," he wrote on X.Meta declined to comment on the demonstrations, while India's IT ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment, the report noted.Why has Meta's content removal in India become controversial?The protests have unfolded against the backdrop of a wider debate over online censorship and freedom of expression in India.The Modi government maintains that it directs social media platforms to remove content only when it violates Indian laws or poses risks to public safety or national security.However, free speech advocates have raised concerns about the growing number of government-mandated takedowns and the limited time available to platforms to assess such requests.In February this year, the government directed social media companies to remove unlawful content within three hours of receiving a notification, tightening the earlier 36-hour deadline.Reporters Without Borders has also flagged an increase in the removal of journalistic content from social media platforms in India this year.Meta's own disclosures indicate the scale of content restrictions. The company restricted more than 5.4 million posts or accounts in India under local laws during the first half of 2026. India ranked second only to Indonesia, with the figure marking a significant increase from approximately 70,000 restrictions in the preceding six months."The large majority of these items included instances where we were obligated to proactively restrict content... based on local law requirements," Meta stated.(With inputs from Reuters)

headline: None but BJP lifted 50 crore above poverty line, says Modi
content: Stopping short of naming the Congress or other opposition Governments, Prime Minister NarendraModi on Saturday claimed that his administration had pulled 500 million people above the poverty line — an accomplishment that remained a pipe dream during his predecessors’ regimes.Without naming the Congress governments, he said how five decades ago GaribiHatao (eradicate poverty) slogans rang out from the ramparts of the Red Fort while policies files were allowed to gather dust.“Policies were buried in files,” on account of the prevailing mindset of the previous rulers, he iterated. The Prime Minister was addressing the Platinum Jubilee (75th anniversary) celebrations of IIT Kharagpur the first such institution to be established in India.Citing a recent World Bank report, he claimed that 50 crore people in India have moved out of poverty in the last 12-13 years. The Prime Minister said when his Government came to power, “I announced from the Red Fort that toilets would be built for the poor … but people mocked at the proposal, wondering how out of everything, a Prime Minister could set a goal of constructing toilets only … but those people failed to understand how important toilets were for the poor people specially the women and the mothers.”He said how “slogans were raised about eradicating poverty from the Red Fort but when it came to implementation of those policies the system would bury those policies in the files,” as a result of which “until 20 years ago poverty remained a permanent problem in a big and populous country like India.”Notwithstanding, India managed to bring 50 crore people out of poverty just because of the change of mindset, he said. There are challenges but “it is my nature that I cannot live without challenging the challenges,” he said before citing a World Bank report iterating “in just 12-13 years 50 crore people in India have been lifted out of poverty… this is no small change … it is the result of a change in the mindset that stands for breaking the limits.”Highlighting India’s semiconductor and chip push, he said, “Questions were asked when I India’s semiconductor mission as other countries were already making semiconductors … but I went ahead with the programme and in a matter of a few years several semiconductor facilities have been established throughout the country.”During an interaction session with the students of India’s premier institution, the Prime Minister advised the students to think big and think in terms of her Viksit Bharat mission programme.Reminding how the Kharagpur IITians had taken lead role in innovative ventures including in the field of rocket technology — where Pawan Kumar Chandana, an IIT Kharagpur alumnus and co-founder of Skyroot Aerospace, whose company developed and launched India’s first privately built rocket — the Prime Minister said the students of the institution had done “outstanding work over past 75 years. Now you must move forward with the firm resolve that when IIT Kharagpur celebrates its 100th anniversary, it should do so in a developed India.”Asking the students to adopt the “Nation First” principle, the Prime Minister said that India’s future development would depend on young people willing to confront problems rather than accept existing limitations.The Bengal Congress leadership was prompt to react to Modi’s statements even as PCC president SubhankarSarkar said, “The Prime Minister should remember that the IIT campus from where he was delivering his speech was set up during the Congress like many other institutions that his Government is selling out to private businessmen.”

headline: Public dissatisfaction with Congress growing in Telangana, says Harish Rao
content: Hyderabad: Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) deputy floor leader and former minister T Harish Rao on Saturday said the BRS would return to power in the next Assembly election under the leadership of K Chandrashekar Rao (KCR), as public dissatisfaction with the Congress government was growing.Speaking at Telangana Bhavan after welcoming Khairatabad Congress leaders into the BRS, Harish Rao said that when Congress MLAs themselves were criticising Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy over the government's functioning, one could imagine the concerns of the people. He cited allegations made by Congress MLA Komatireddy Rajagopal Reddy concerning corruption and the party's electoral prospects.He said the regular joining of leaders from other parties at Telangana Bhavan indicated growing support for the BRS. He also referred to the disqualification of Danam Nagender by the High Court and claimed that elections could be held soon.Harish Rao also claimed that surveys conducted by different agencies indicated that the BRS, led by former chief minister KCR, would return to power in Telangana.Turning to Hyderabad's development, Harish Rao said the previous BRS government had strengthened the city's international reputation through infrastructure development and improved civic amenities.He recalled actor Rajinikanth's comparison of Hyderabad with New York and said the city's image had improved considerably during Chandrashekar Rao's tenure.The BRS leader alleged that the Congress government had failed to maintain the previous administration's standards in drinking water supply, electricity and sanitation.Harish Rao claimed that Hyderabad residents were increasingly dependent on water tankers, with nearly 80,000 tankers being purchased daily. He said the BRS government had improved water supply by bringing Krishna and Godavari waters to the city."The government of increasing electricity charges through surcharges and alleged that power cuts and drinking water shortages had returned under Congress rule," Rao said.Questioning the government's industrial policy, he alleged that the state had been without full-time secretaries for the industries and information technology departments for two years.He said Revanth Reddy, who also holds the Home portfolio, should take responsibility for the alleged deterioration in law and order. Harish Rao alleged that garbage collection, sanitation and mosquito control had deteriorated across Hyderabad. He questioned the government's focus on developing Future City while existing civic problems in Hyderabad remained unresolved.Harish Rao also criticised the government's performance in education and recruitment. Referring to the Chief Minister's daughter establishing corporate schools around Hyderabad, he questioned the government's failure to improve public education.Criticising the Congress and BJP, Harish Rao alleged that both parties had failed to protect Telangana's interests. He accused the Centre of neglecting Telangana in drought relief allocations, claiming that Central teams had visited Andhra Pradesh but not Telangana.He alleged that a political understanding between the BJP and Congress was adversely affecting Telangana's interests.

headline: PM Modi inaugurates Nitish Setu, waves at locals during tour
content: Patna, Nov 21: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday inaugurated the six-lane 'Nitish Setu' over the Ganga River, connecting Kachchi Dargah in Patna with Bidupur in Vaishali, marking a major addition to road connectivity between north and south Bihar.The Prime Minister toured the bridge along with Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Kumar Chaudhary and Union Minister Chirag Paswan.During the visit, he waved a traditional gamchha to greet residents of Raghopur.PM Modi arrived at the venue in a security convoy, travelling in the same vehicle as Samrat Choudhary, Chirag Paswan and Vijay Kumar Chaudhary.He later proceeded towards the stage in an open-top jeep, accompanied by them, greeting people gathered along the route.On reaching the stage, the Prime Minister acknowledged the crowd with folded hands and embraced Nishant Kumar, son of former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar.Addressing the gathering, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary said the inauguration of Nitish Setu marked an important milestone during the government's first year in office.He said projects worth around Rs 34,000 crore were being inaugurated or launched during the Prime Minister's visit.He also said the railway projects worth Rs 1 lakh crore were being implemented in Bihar and claimed that the state had benefited significantly from the GST regime.He also referred to the acquisition of 1,200 acres of land in Rajapakar, saying the proposed development would generate employment for one lakh people.He announced that the Bihar government would establish a university in the name of former Chief Minister and Bharat Ratna awardee Karpoori Thakur.Highlighting the government's grievance redressal initiative, he said the 'Sahyog Karyakram' had received 10.50 lakh applications.Officials are issued notices if complaints are not addressed within 10 days, while those failing to complete the work within 30 days face automatic suspension from the 31st day, he claimed.Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Kumar Chaudhary welcomed the decision to name the bridge after Nitish Kumar.He also highlighted Bihar's Silt Management Policy, saying the Centre was developing a framework based on the state's initiative.He said Bihar was prepared to contribute to the country's goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047.Union Minister Chirag Paswan said the NDA's double-engine government was implementing several development initiatives in Bihar.He also thanked Nitish Kumar for his role in the bridge project.(IANS)

headline: PM Rahman faces mounting pressure as BNP-Jamaat rift deepens in Dhaka
content: New Delhi, Nov 21: Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s remarks on Friday, implying India’s hand behind rising violence in his country, coincidentally came a day after he met with Jamaat-e-Islami chief, now Leader of the Opposition, Shafiqur Rahman. The meeting was described in several media reports as an attempt to forge greater unity against the now-banned Awami League.The meeting took place days before Awami League chief and former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s much-anticipated arrival in Dhaka.Interestingly, the Jamaat leader advised Rahman “to hold dialogue with political parties to uphold anti-fascist unity and uproot fascism from the country”, reported Bangladesh ‘Prothom Alo’.Interestingly, earlier this month, reports emerged that the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) was planning to hold talks with political parties that participated in the 2024 protests against the then government, with the stated aim of “preserving unity” among forces opposed to the Awami League.“However, the BNP will not invite parties affiliated with the Jamaat-e-Islami-led alliance. The talks may take place in late November or December,” it added.Separate reports indicated that in the absence of the Awami League from the country’s political stage, once allies, the BNP and Jamaat appeared to be drifting away since the time of the elections.Relations have increasingly become bitter, especially on the issue of implementation of the July National Charter and the verdict of the referendum, observed commentators.The National Charter, drafted after the 2024 mass uprising and endorsed by most major political parties, set out a broad agenda for state and constitutional reforms, including measures to strengthen judicial independence, rebalance executive power, and expand democratic accountability.In the national referendum held alongside the February 2026 general election, the charter was approved by a majority of voters.While the BNP argues that the charter's reforms should be implemented through constitutional amendments passed by Parliament, the Jamaat insists that voters specifically endorsed a separate Constitution Reform Council and broader structural reforms beyond ordinary parliamentary amendments.This disagreement over the mechanism of reform has turned into a significant political dispute lately. Reports have even cited instances where each has been accusing the other of secret understandings with the Awami League.The BNP has apparently been trying to distance itself from the Jamaat to gain wider support among secular and international communities, but the move is said to have led to some disagreements within the party.Meanwhile, Bangladesh is experiencing a period of renewed political turbulence, with rising street violence, economic discontent, and intensifying competition among the country's major political forces.According to reports, paramilitary forces were mobilized across the country as violence, crude-bomb attacks, and political clashes spread to multiple districts. Yet, some media analyses suggest that the government is trying to avoid an aggressive security crackdown, fearing such action could invite comparisons with past episodes and unpleasant repercussions.The Jamaat itself remains mired in controversy in Bangladesh politics because of its opposition to the country's independence during the 1971 Liberation War.The party and several of its leaders were accused of collaborating with the Pakistan army. Some of its senior leaders were later even convicted by Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal for war crimes committed during the conflict.This legacy has contributed to Jamaat's long-standing political alienation, where its critics view the party as an unreliable partner because of its radical views on religion, shifting political alliances, and the enduring mistrust from its 1971 stance.Yet, major parties have repeatedly found electoral value in cooperating with it, where the Jamaat’s organisational strength and electoral influence have made it a partner that larger parties have periodically embraced when coalition-building served their interests.Media narratives on the latest developments portray the current regime as under strain amid Awami League mobilisation even under a ban, labour unrest, and growing Islamist pressure, and seeking assurance from a powerful and influential adversary to contain another.(IANS)

headline: MP Medical Teachers Announce Statewide Stir From December 14 Over 12 Pending Demands; Vidhan Sabha March In
content: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): Progressive Medical Teachers’ Association (PMTA) has announced a statewide agitation on December 14 to press for their demands. Before that, the association will take out a march to Vidhan Sabha on December 8. This decision follows the failure to address 12-point charter of demands.As per medical teachers, reasons for the agitation include the fact that despite instructions of the deputy chief minister on February 4, 2025, to establish a time-bound resolution schedule, no concrete action has been taken at the departmental level, even after nearly one year and nine months.Similarly, despite directives issued during meetings held on March 7, 2025 and on January 9, 2026, of a high-level committee, the relevant files have remained pending at commissioner's office/directorate level for over a year.Key demands include non-implementation of Dynamic Assured Career Progression (DACP) scheme and its associated pay scales in the state, failure to include associate professors and professors under DACP scheme to date, implementation of time-bound promotions for all medical faculty members under DACP scheme, failure to rectify Non-Practicing Allowance (NPA) issue, despite its approval by the Cabinet, lack of service protection for all medical faculty members working in Madhya Pradesh and non-settlement of gratuity payments to date, despite the existence of relevant rules.Level up your brain the fun way. headline: MP OBC Reservation Row Intensifies As Advocates Body Moves Supreme Court Seeking 27% Quota, Questions 14%
content: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): After the Madhya Pradesh government, the OBC Advocates’ Welfare Association has now filed a special leave petition (SLP) in the Supreme Court (SC) to get 27% OBC reservation. The state government had filed an SLP in the SC on October 16, 2026, challenging the High Court (HC) ruling that had struck down the 27% OBC quota and restored it to 14%.The OBC Advocates’ Welfare Association’s primary argument is that under Articles 15(4) and 16(4) of the Constitution, provisions for reservation exist not only for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes but also for Other Backwards Classes (OBCs). Despite this, and although the OBC population in Madhya Pradesh is approximately 51%, they are being granted only 14% reservation.The petition questions why, given that the constitutional objective of reservation is to ensure adequate representation for socially and educationally backward classes, there exists such a disparity between population proportion and the actual representation in the case of OBCs. The association has also challenged this in the context of the right to equality, as enshrined in Article 14 of the Constitution.OBC Advocates’ Welfare Association president Rameshwar Thakur said, “HC had rejected 27% OBC reservation, stating the state government did not present sufficient grounds and data for it. So, we have filed an SLP in the SC regarding OBC reservation in the ratio of population.”Level up your brain the fun way. headline: BJP slams Rahul Gandhi of growth after Trump praise
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Saturday criticised the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, after US President Donald Trump cited India’s 7 per cent GDP growth as an example while attacking the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate policy.Trump made the comments on Friday at a White House press conference. He said high borrowing costs were stifling the economy and pointed to India as an example of a country where lower rates could actually lead to faster growth.“If you look at India, they have low interest rates, and they have a 7 per cent GDP. We’d have a 14, 15, maybe even a 20 per cent GDP. It’s absolutely tragic when you’re doing so well, and then they (the Fed) raise interest rates. The fact of the matter is we’ve blown through it,” Trump said. He described the Fed as “extremely political” and stated that when you have good US data, you invariably get a hike rather than a cut. Trump said good performance would improve the US credit rating and that would, in turn, allow lower rates, which would lead to much higher growth and much faster debt reduction.The comments provoked an immediate political reaction in India. BJP leader Ashish Sood posted on X that Trump’s recognition of the 7per cent growth figure clearly indicated India’s growing global standing and economic strength. “The world sees India’s progress; Rahul Gandhi and the Congress continue to ignore it,” he said.The BJP’s response comes as the Opposition has been vociferous in its criticism of the Indian economy. Gandhi has on several occasions described the economy as ‘dead’ and, more recently, as sitting on an ‘economic disaster’, citing unemployment, the state of manufacturing, and the state of education as problems. This followed earlier remarks by Trump in 2025, who also described India as a ‘dead economy’, which Gandhi picked up at the time.Trump’s latest remarks are at odds with earlier assessments. Indian officials and the ruling party have pointed to a consistent growth rate of around 7 per cent (or above) in recent quarters, citing government data as well as World Bank and Goldman Sachs forecasts. The RBI has been relatively accommodative compared with the much higher rates currently in place in the US.As of Saturday evening, Gandhi and the Congress had not publicly responded to Sood’s post or Trump’s comments.The exchange comes amid the ongoing domestic debate over India’s economic performance, with the Government pointing to headline growth numbers and the global recognition that brings.The Opposition, of course, is pointing to employment, inequality and sectoral performance. Trump’s use of the Indian example is part of his wider push for the Fed to cut rates much more aggressively. He has been very clear that lower borrowing costs would spur the US economy far beyond where it is now and would go a long way toward helping with the national debt. The White House comments were made with VP JD Vance and Sec Marco Rubio both present.The 7 per cent figure that Trump referenced is in line with the most recent official and private estimates of Indian growth - India is very much in the group of the fastest-growing major economies.The political reaction in New Delhi clearly shows how the Government and the main Opposition are using external validation of those figures in the contest over economic management.

headline: Bangladesh minister vows action against those behind arson, blames Awami League-linked groups: Reports
content: Bangladesh will take firm legal action against those behind recent arson and petrol bomb attacks, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir has said, blaming groups linked to the banned Awami League for the violence amid escalating political unrest in the country, according to local media reports.Kobir, on Friday, said law enforcement agencies were working to bring those responsible to justice and alleged that the Awami League’s leadership, including those based abroad, was encouraging the attacks.“We will go after these terrorists, and the long arm of justice will reach them,” he said, responding to questions from reporters on the sidelines of a media briefing, according to the state-run BSS news agency.Kobir alleged that the Awami League leadership was encouraging the attacks from abroad and that others based overseas were also involved in efforts to instigate violence. The minister’s remarks come amid a spate of political violence and arson attacks across Bangladesh.At least four people were killed in separate incidents earlier this week, including three leaders of the ruling BNP and its affiliated organisations and a bus helper who was burnt alive after unidentified assailants set fire to parked buses, the Dhaka Tribune reported.In separate remarks at the foreign ministry, Kobir described the Awami League, whose political activities remain banned, as a “terrorist organisation” and warned of strong action against those involved in petrol bomb attacks, arson and other violence, The Daily Star reported.On the return of fugitives from abroad, Kobir said attempts to bring them back from New Delhi through acts of violence would not succeed, as their return would be pursued under the extradition treaty.“No fugitive terrorist can be brought back to Bangladesh from Delhi even by throwing petrol bombs… that will actually happen through the extradition treaty,” he said, according to The Daily Star, without directly naming anyone.The issue of ousted Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s return has emerged as a major source of tension between Dhaka and New Delhi, with the latest wave of unrest in Bangladesh following the government’s rejection of her request for a fresh passport and national identity card earlier this month. Hasina’s lawyers had approached the Bangladesh mission in New Delhi seeking the documents to facilitate her planned return in December.The interim government had revoked her passport and national identity card after she fled Bangladesh in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government. The Awami League subsequently announced a week-long protest programme demanding her return, culminating in a nationwide shutdown on November 19.The protests were accompanied by arson, crude bomb attacks and clashes across several districts.Hasina has been living in India since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024. Her extradition has remained a point of friction between the two countries, with both the interim administration led by Muhammad Yunus and the subsequent BNP government headed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman pressing New Delhi to hand her over under a bilateral extradition treaty.  Dhaka has insisted that Hasina, who was sentenced to death in absentia in November 2025 for crimes against humanity over the 2024 crackdown on protesters, must be brought back from India under the bilateral extradition treaty rather than allowed to return as an ordinary traveller. Hasina has said she intends to return to Bangladesh in December and surrender before a court. She has denied the charges against her.

headline: ‘TV serial governance’: Akash slams BJP, calls SP ‘B-Team’ | Hindustan Times
content: LUCKNOW Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) national convenor Akash Anand launched a sharp attack on both the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Samajwadi Party (SP) on Friday during a public meeting in the Bikapur assembly constituency. The rally came amid an ongoing exchange of public challenges between chief minister Yogi Adityanath and SP president Akhilesh Yadav over contesting from Ayodhya.Urging voters to bring BSP chief Mayawati back as chief minister, Anand highlighted the development, welfare schemes and law-and-order record of previous BSP administrations.Referring to the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, in which BJP’s two-time sitting MP Lallu Singh lost the Faizabad seat to SP’s Awadhesh Prasad, Anand said Ayodhya had sent a clear message to the country. “They did not vote for a government running on advertisements, but voted on the performance of the BJP government,” he said.Hitting out at the BJP, he said each year the state government is breaking the record of lighting lamps in Ayodhya during Diwali festivity, and at the same time, the government is also breaking the record of unemployment in the state. Taking a jibe at CM Yogi Adityanath’s statement “saab changa si” (all is well) in the state, Akash said: “When I ask people what BJP government has done for them in 10 years, they reply that they do not know of the work, but have seen advertisements of developed UP on hoardings.” He alleged that BJP MLAs from Ayodhya claimed that the town is shining, but patients have to take bus rides to Lucknow for medical treatment. “This government has achieved zero on education, security and employment. UP is number one in crime against women and heinous crimes. They call themselves an ‘encounter government’, but FIRs are not being registered in police stations, instead there is photo shoot of encounters. It seems that instead of running the government, BJP is indulged in shooting of a TV serial,” claimed Akash.“In 10 years, no new school has opened in UP, but 25,000 schools have been shut. Today, 1.40 lakh posts of teachers are lying vacant. The BJP does not want to empower poor people but wants them to stand in line for rations. Two crore youths are unemployed in UP,” he alleged.Launching an attack on the SP, Anand said: “Their leaders allege that BSP is the B team of the BJP. It seems that SP chief Akhilesh Yadav is a confused leader – sometimes he terms ‘P’ of PDA as Pichhda (OBC) and at other times terms ‘P’ as Pandit (Brahmin). During the Dalit conference in Agra, SP leader Ram Gopal Yadav humiliated the Dalit community. Both Ram Gopal Yadav and Akhilesh Yadav should apologize to Dalits.”Anand also accused the SP of being opposed to the Dalit community, citing its past opposition to reservation in promotions in Parliament and the renaming of districts named after Dalit icons.“Recently, the SP sent the son of a BJP MP to the Rajya Sabha, ignoring the claims of Dalit, OBC and Muslim community. It is clear that SP is the B team of the BJP,” added Akash.“During the Lok Sabha elections, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi moved with the Constitution to seek votes of Dalit community, but after the polls, he abandoned the community. Dalits are exploited in Congress ruled states,” he alleged.

headline: Bail for BJP worker accused of ‘extortion’, MP says police admitted ‘mistake’
content: Ranaghat: A Ranaghat court on Saturday granted bail to BJP functionary Piyali Biswas, 38, a member of the party’s Nadia South organisational district committee, 48 hours after she was remanded in 14 days’ judicial custody on charges of assault and extortion in CM Suvendu Adhikari’s name. Ranaghat BJP MP Jagannath Sarkar, who backed her, had written to the CM.Police had failed to submit the case diary and injury report at the Nov 19 hearing, when she was remanded. On Saturday, the magistrate said the injury report did not support the police claim that Biswas and her associates had broken limbs and caused head injuries to complainants. The public prosecutor had no satisfactory reply when the court questioned the charges.Defence counsel Mrinmay Chakraborty submitted video evidence and argued that Biswas was falsely implicated for protesting against a land syndicate and illegal liquor and gambling dens in Ranaghat, Rathtala and Talpukurpara. She and her associates were attacked and chased even at the hospital before police rescued them, he said, and were booked despite a lack of evidence and medical proof.A complaint by local residents alleged Biswas phoned Ranaghat businessmen demanding money and threatened to shut their businesses and implicate them in cases if they refused. Police say she went to a Rathtala premises with associates on Thursday, livestreamed a gambling allegation and challenged those present, leading to vandalism, assault and injuries to one person. A liquor bottle was recovered from her scooter.Biswas denied the extortion charge and claimed she was framed for trying to expose a gambling racket run under the patronage of Trinamool neta and former Ranaghat municipality vice-chairperson Ananda Dey. Local sources said Dey had not been seen in the area since. Police are probing both the extortion and gambling allegations.Sarkar had called the charges politically motivated and sought an inquiry against the Ranaghat police station inspector-in-charge. After the bail order, he said: “I fought for her bail. Based on my letter, there was a stir in police circles. The SP and DSP contacted me, admitted their mistake and promised to take action against the gamblers.”

headline: BJP to Launch Chandigarh Municipal Corporation Election Campaign Under the Guidance of National President Nitin Nabin: Jatinder Pal Malhotra
content:
Chandigarh, November 21, 2026:The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has intensified its preparations for the upcoming Chandigarh Municipal Corporation elections. In this regard, a press conference was organized today by BJP Chandigarh Pradesh, addressed by State President Jatinder Pal Malhotra and Chandigarh Municipal Corporation Election In-charge and MLA from Delhi’s Malviya Nagar Assembly Constituency, Satish Upadhyay. During the press conference, they shared details of the visit of BJP National President Nitin Nabin to Chandigarh on November 22 and the schedule of his programme.

The grand event will be held at Ramlila Ground, Sector 27, at 2:00 PM, and a large number of party workers are expected to participate.

BJP Chandigarh Pradesh In-charge Mahendra Pandey, former State Presidents Sanjay Tandon and Arun Sood, Mayor Saurabh Joshi, and State Media Coordinator Ravi Rawat were also present on the occasion.

State President Jatinder Pal Malhotra informed that a grand Booth Workers’ Conference will be organized on Sunday, November 22, at Ramlila Ground, Sector 27. BJP National President Nitin Nabin will attend the conference as the chief guest and address office-bearers and party workers from the booth level to the state level. His guidance and valuable direction will further strengthen the party organization in Chandigarh and provide a clear roadmap for the upcoming Municipal Corporation elections.

He said that this conference is not merely an event but an important opportunity to accelerate the organization’s preparations for the forthcoming Municipal Corporation elections in Chandigarh. Approximately 11 workers from each of the 575 booths will participate. In addition, state office-bearers, representatives from all six districts, Mandal office-bearers, and workers from various Morchas and cells will also attend. Around 6,500 party workers and office-bearers are expected to participate in the conference.

headline: Himachal Assembly passes resolution to set up permanent High Court Bench in Dharamshala
content: CHANDIGARH: The Himachal Pradesh Assembly has unanimously passed a resolution seeking the establishment of a permanent Bench of the Himachal Pradesh High Court in Dharamshala to ensure faster and easier access to justice for people living in Kangra and other districts of lower Himachal. Moving the resolution during the concluding day of the winter session at Tapovan, Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said that Article 214 of the Constitution of India and Section 51(2) of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, empower the President of India to establish a permanent Bench of a High Court at a place other than its principal seat, after consultation with the Governor of the state and the Chief Justice of the High Court. Citing the high volume of pending cases originating from Kangra and adjoining districts, the resolution stated that people from Kangra and other lower Himachal districts have to undertake long and difficult journeys to reach Shimla, thus resulting in additional financial expenses and delays in legal proceedings. Setting up a dedicated Bench is fully justified to ensure speedy, accessible and affordable justice at the citizens' doorstep. Sukhu noted that litigants, advocates and the general public from Kangra and other districts of lower Himachal face severe hardship, heavy financial burden and avoidable delays in accessing timely justice due to the long geographical distance and difficult terrain separating the region from the principal seat of the High Court in Shimla. .Himachal sets up panel to reorganise districts, subdivisions & tehsils after 54 years.He also reaffirmed the government's commitment to providing clean land, court buildings, residential complexes, digital infrastructure and financial resources to make the Dharamsala Bench operational at the earliest.Clarifying the intent behind the move, Sukhu said that the initiative is not aimed at diminishing the importance of Shimla, but rather at making justice accessible to a larger section of the state's population.The Assembly has decided to send a formal and detailed proposal to the Central Government for the establishment of the permanent Bench. The House also reiterated the state government's commitment to making the proposed Bench operational at the earliest.The state government will provide the required land, court buildings, residential facilities, digital infrastructure and financial resources for the proposed Bench.Meanwhile, Sukhu also announced the establishment of a second women's reserve battalion in Himachal Pradesh during the Assembly proceedings.The first women's reserve battalion was established on November 17, 2009. headline: Chandigarh boys, girls win softball gold at National School Games
content: Chandigarh's boys' and girls' Under-19 softball teams won gold medals in their respective categories at the 70th National School Games (2026-27), organised by the Department of School Education, Chandigarh Administration. The tournament concluded at Government Model Senior Secondary School (GMSSS), Sector 37B, on Sunday.In the boys' category, Chandigarh finished on top, followed by Chhattisgarh in second place and Maharashtra in third. Haryana finished fourth, followed by Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Delhi and Rajasthan in the fifth, sixth, seventh and eighth positions, respectively.In the girls' category, Chandigarh claimed the gold medal, while Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh finished second and third, respectively. Odisha secured the fourth position, followed by Haryana, Telangana, Rajasthan and Kerala.On the concluding day, Chandigarh's boys registered a 15-5 victory over Chhattisgarh. Maharashtra finished third after recording a convincing 10-0 win against Haryana.In the girls' final, Chandigarh eves defeated Maharashtra 4-2 in a closely contested encounter to take the gold medal. Chhattisgarh finished third after beating Odisha 6-3 in the third-place match.The official results were released by Arvinder Kaur, Convener of the Fixture, Result and Record Committee; Dr Gurcharan Singh Gill, Chief Technical Officer; and the District Education Officer (UT, Chandigarh).

headline: PGIMER Chandigarh bags silver award for health research excellence for second consecutive year
content: PGIMER, Chandigarh, has been conferred the Silver Category Award for Health Research Excellence under the Publication Evaluation Metrics at the 3rd DHR-ICMR Health Research Excellence Summit 2026. This marks the second consecutive year that the Institute has received this distinction.The award was presented on November 17 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, during the two-day summit held on November 16–17.It was presented by Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Director General, ICMR, and Secretary, Department of Health Research (DHR), along with other dignitaries. Dr. Prateek Bhatia, Faculty In-charge, MERC Cell, PGIMER, received the award on behalf of the institute.

headline: Chandigarh residents demand civic solutions, not poll promises & rhetoric
content: QUESTION for next weekWith extortion calls, firing and gang war incidents happening repeatedly, is gangsterism making its presence felt in Mohali. Why are the police unable to keep a check on anti-social elements?Write to openhouse@tribunemail.com with your ideas, within 150 words, and your photograph by Thursday (November 26).Don’t deface wallsPolitical parties must first commit to not defacing the city’s walls and public spaces with posters, banners and graffiti. Second, election expenditure should be audited daily, with a complete ban on inducements such as cash, liquor, gifts or donations to voters. Third, every candidate should file a public affidavit outlining a time-bound plan to improve security, cleanliness, road and drainage maintenance.Capt Amar Jeet (retd), KhararPrioritise cleanlinessPolitical parties must prioritise cleanliness, scientific waste management, uninterrupted water supply, efficient sewerage systems, traffic decongestion, adequate parking and regular maintenance of roads and public infrastructure. Equal emphasis must be placed on protecting green spaces.Dr Parvinder Singh, Mandi GobindgarhTime-bound actionThe Chandigarh Municipal Corporation elections must focus on improving citizens’ quality of life, not merely political promises. Residents deserve clean surroundings, efficient waste management, reliable water supply, well-maintained roads, proper drainage and adequate parking. Political parties should present clear, time-bound action plans and ensure transparency and accountability.Vineet Gandhi, ChandigarhHouse tax waiverWater supply, sewerage and rising user charges are likely to dominate MC poll discourse. Questions persist over the Rs 1,400-crore 24x7 water project in Manimajra and its impact on supply and quality. The long-pending clearance of the Dadu Majra dump, better roads, parking and civic infrastructure remain key concerns. Residents are also seeking waiver of house tax on CHB flats, greater transparency in MC finances, clean campaigning and mandatory use of CNG-powered official vehicles to curb pollution.Surinder Kaur, Chandigarh Road recarpetingPolitical parties must first address the unfinished promises made in previous elections. Long-pending issues such as parking shortages across the city remain unresolved. Road recarpeting, streetlight repairs and park maintenance continue to lag despite repeated assurances. The relocation of the Dadumajra dumping ground and the long-delayed. Tribune Chowk flyover project have also seen little progress.Wg Cdr (Dr) JS Minhas (retd), Mohali Stray animalsChandigarh was envisioned as a model city, but civic governance remains a key concern. Ahead of the MC elections, residents want solutions to persistent issues such as the Dadu Majra dump, irregular waste collection, broken roads, parking shortages, erratic water supply and sewerage problems. Stray animals and non-functional streetlights continue to raise safety concerns.Yash Khetarpal, PanchkulaGovernance agendaAhead of the Chandigarh Municipal Corporation (MC) elections, candidates must present a practical governance agenda focused on better public transport, repaired roads, uninterrupted water supply, smart parking and sensor-based traffic signals. Scientific waste management, cleaner parks and greener neighbourhoods should be priorities. Upgrading dispensaries, ensuring school vaccination drives and providing dedicated support for senior citizens can significantly improve residents’ quality of life.Shashi Guglani, ChandigarhPollution controlAhead of the Chandigarh MC elections, political parties must focus on core civic issues rather than rhetoric. Priorities include scientific waste management, clearance of legacy dumps, better traffic management, adequate parking and action against encroachments. Pollution control, de-siltation of Sukhna Lake and improved water, sewerage and electricity services are equally important.Harinder Singh Bhalla, ChandigarhBetter policingRising crime, drug abuse and civic issues require urgent attention in Chandigarh. Better policing, rehabilitation programmes, improved drainage, timely desilting and efficient waste management are essential. Vacant civic posts should be filled, road repair quality strictly monitored and grievance redressal strengthened through dedicated helplines.Kapil Thakur, Panchkula Encroachments in UTEncroachments across Chandigarh require regular and impartial removal drives, backed by surprise inspections by senior officials to ensure accountability. Streetlight maintenance also needs attention, as lights in some areas remain switched on during the day due to poor monitoring, leading to needless wastage of electricity and public funds. Political parties must strengthen oversight and ensure efficient use of civic resources.KC Rana, ChandigarhQuality of lifeThe Chandigarh Municipal Corporation should be a model institution that enhances residents’ quality of life. Ahead of the elections, parties must focus on efficient service delivery, reliable public transport, uninterrupted water supply, healthcare, public safety and development of newly merged areas. Voters should elect councillors committed to public service rather than partisan interests.Abhyam Sharma, PathankotTraffic managementWith the Chandigarh MC elections approaching, parties must prioritise traffic management, better parking and a reliable public transport system with improved bus connectivity and last-mile access. Rather than relying on slogans, parties should present time-bound plans for sustainable mobility, transparent governance and improved civic services.Amit Jain, ChandigarhPitch for manifestoAhead of the Chandigarh Municipal Corporation elections, voters should demand manifestos that go beyond infrastructure promises and focus on civic empowerment. Candidates must explain how they will help residents’ access welfare schemes, free legal aid and public services. Chandigarh needs councillors who solve problems, reduce bureaucratic hurdles and promote tools like the RTI Act to strengthen accountability.Dr Madhuri Sharma, United StatesMore transparencyA modern waste-processing plant is needed to reduce the Dadumajra garbage mountain. Voters are concerned about rising water and garbage collection charges, low water pressure, poor-parking management, stray cattle and dog-bite incidents. Above all, residents want greater transparency, independent oversight and stronger accountability from elected councillors.Anita K Tandon, Mundi KhararPotholed roadsWith Chandigarh Municipal Corporation elections approaching, political parties must address persistent civic problems rather than rely on broad promises. Key concerns include pothole-ridden roads, inadequate parking, water shortages, overflowing sewers, poor waste management, stray cattle, encroachments and neglected public spaces.Vaibhav Goyal, ChandigarhLaw and orderPolitical parties must address Chandigarh’s ground-level concerns and focus on responsive, people-centric governance. Key priorities include better healthcare, efficient public transport, improved law and order, job creation through MSME growth and cleaner surroundings. Voters also expect uninterrupted power and water supply, safer roads, more cycling infrastructure, e-governance and modern civic facilities. Parking shortages and frequent traffic jams continue to inconvenience commuters. Political parties must prioritise these everyday problems and present practical, time-bound solutions.Anil Kumar Sharma, ChandigarhCivic neglectThe City Beautiful is losing its charm as rapid population growth strains roads, parks, dispensaries and schools.
