Residents expect transparent governance, efficient digital grievance redressal and time-bound action plans.Raj Kumar Kapoor, RoparHigher tax BurdenInstead of burdening residents with higher taxes, political parties should prioritise cleanliness, sanitation, drainage and maintenance of civic infrastructure. Better waste management and more accessible dustbins can improve public participation in keeping the city clean. Ahead of the MC elections, parties must promise citizen-friendly municipal by-laws and ensure their effective implementation.Dr Neha Saini, ChandigarhGarbage disposalThe Municipal Corporation must move beyond routine garbage collection and adopt an integrated system based on segregation, recycling and scientific disposal. Decentralised composting, efficient processing facilities, prevention of open dumping and proper management of construction waste are essential. Accountability of sanitation contractors, better support for sanitation workers and a long-term zero-landfill approach can help preserve Chandigarh’s status as a clean and green city.Dr Bharat, ChandigarhPublic safetyWith Chandigarh MC elections approaching, political parties should prioritise scientific waste management to prevent another Dadumajra-like crisis, alongside key infrastructure projects such as the Tribune flyover, ring road and metro connectivity. Priorities include scientific waste management, resolving the Dadumajra dumping-ground crisis, improving drainage, ensuring reliable water supply, repairing roads and easing traffic and parking woes. Transparency in municipal finances, timely grievance redressal and accountability are equally vital.Gurpreet S Malhotra, MohaliAdequate parkingPolitical parties must ensure 24×7 drinking water, efficient sewerage, better traffic management, adequate parking and quality roads and footpaths. Above all, parties should commit to transparency by disclosing ward-wise spending, project timelines and councillors’ performance. Voters deserve accountability, not slogans.Narinder Banwait, Chandigarh Waste managementAs the Municipal Corporation elections approach, citizens need more than slogans and promises. They expect clean roads, proper drainage, uninterrupted water supply, efficient waste management, functional streetlights and reliable public transport. Concerns such as women’s safety, senior citizens’ welfare, quality healthcare and accessible public spaces also deserve priority.Asha Trakroo, Chandigarh Affordable housingPolitical parties must rise above partisan politics and focus on Chandigarh’s pressing civic challenges. headline: University Grants Commission flags 32 fake universities across country, Delhi accounts for 12
content: Twelve institutions operating in Delhi have been identified by the University Grants Commission (UGC) as unrecognised, making the national Capital the biggest contributor to the list of 32 institutions flagged across the country for lacking the authority to award recognised degrees.The latest list places Delhi ahead of Uttar Pradesh, which has four institutions, while six other states and Union Territories have two each. The remaining four states have one institution each. The findings have once again raised concerns over students potentially enrolling in institutions whose degrees may not be recognised for higher education or employment.In an advisory, the UGC cautioned students, parents and guardians against seeking admission to such institutions without verifying their recognition status. The advisory was issued in pursuance of a Supreme Court order dated October 9, 2026. The commission has asked the concerned authorities and institutions to give the notice wide publicity to ensure that students are aware of the risks involved.The 12 Delhi-based institutions named in the list are Mountain Institute of Management & Technology, World Peace of United Nations University, Institute of Management and Engineering, National Institute of Management Solution, All India Institute of Public & Physical Health Sciences, Commercial University Ltd, United Nations University, Vocational University, ADR-Centric Juridical University, Indian Institute of Science and Engineering, Viswakarma Open University for Self Employment and Adhyatmik Vishwavidyalaya.The UGC list, marked as updated in February 2026, covers institutions across Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Delhi, Haryana, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, Puducherry, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.The commission has advised students to verify an institution’s legal status and its authority to award degrees before seeking admission. It has also cautioned them against relying solely on advertisements, promotional material or claims made on institutional websites while making academic decisions.The issue is particularly significant for students who invest considerable time and money in higher education, only to risk ending up with qualifications that may not be accepted by universities, employers or other statutory bodies.The UGC has urged students and parents to consult its official records and check the relevant statutory approvals before enrolling in any institution. The advisory aims to prevent students from being misled by institutions projecting themselves as universities without the requisite legal recognition.12 institutions in Delhi on UGC's fake universities list:S No.Name of institution1Mountain Institute of Management & Technology2World Peace of United Nations University3Institute of Management and Engineering4National Institute of Management Solution5All India Institute of Public & Physical Health Sciences6Commercial University Ltd7United Nations University8Vocational University9ADR-Centric Juridical University10Indian Institute of Science and Engineering11Viswakarma Open University for Self-Employment12Adhyatmik Vishwavidyalaya

headline: Law and order can’t be blanket justification for interfering with journalistic activities, Supreme Court told
content: Law and order powers cannot be invoked as “blanket justification” for interfering with journalistic activities, a women journalists body—which has alleged forcible detention and assault on media persons covering the Delhi protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in October – has told the Supreme Court.In a rejoinder to the Delhi Police counter-affidavit, petitioner Network of Women in Media India said that obstruction, forcible removal, assault or sexual harassment directed at journalists strikes simultaneously at their personal liberty and bodily integrity, their freedom to practise their vocation, and the freedom of the press to gather and communicate information.The Network pointed out that the Supreme Court had directed on October 11 that the discharge of professional duties of lawyers, journalists, and other professionals must not be hindered.Earlier, the Delhi Police had said that they hold freedom of the press in the highest regard. However, drawing a distinction between journalists and reel-makers, the Delhi Police told the Supreme Court that the latter can’t be given the protection available to media persons.In an affidavit filed in the Supreme Court, Delhi Police Joint Commissioner of Police Surender Kumar had defended the police action during protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar here last month.Now, the petitioner has said “The reliance upon the label ‘reel-makers’ in the counter affidavit is wholly misconceived and appears to be a retrospective justification for the obstruction and detention of journalists.”The petitioner Network requested the top court to pass such other order or orders as it may deem fit “to secure press freedom, the bodily integrity, dignity and safety of journalists, particularly women journalists, their equal and unhindered right to practise their vocation, accountability of public authorities, democratic scrutiny and the effective protection of fundamental rights.”

headline: 1 counsellor for 1,593 students in Delhi schools, ‘Ehsaas’ promises to bridge the gap
content: One counsellor for every 1,593 students. That is the existing counselling strength in Delhi government schools, where the government now aims to bring down the ratio to one for every 500 students under its newly launched mental health policy, ‘Ehsaas 2026’.The ambitious target comes against the backdrop of 1,151 student suicides recorded in the Capital over three years, raising questions about whether the proposed support system can reach students in distress before their problems escalate into a crisis.National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) data shows that Delhi recorded 385 student suicides in 2022, 388 in 2023 and 378 in 2024. Although the figure declined marginally in the latest year, the three-year total highlights the continuing challenge before the education and health systems. The numbers also underline the need for sustained mental health interventions within educational institutions, where students often face academic pressure, emotional difficulties and other personal challenges.The existing infrastructure in Delhi government schools illustrates the gap that the new policy seeks to address. The schools have around 16.57 lakh students and around 1,040 counsellors, including 540 educational and vocational guidance counsellors (348 regular and 192 guest) and more than 500 teacher counsellors. While educational and vocational guidance counsellors provide psychological, emotional, personal, academic and career guidance, teacher counsellors contribute through student guidance and awareness activities. Together, they translate into approximately one counsellor for every 1,593 students.According to the Economic Survey of Delhi, the Capital has 1,071 government schools with an enrolment of 16.57 lakh students. Another 1.28 lakh students are enrolled in 199 government-aided schools, while 16.71 lakh attend 1,677 unaided schools, taking the total school enrolment across these categories to around 34.56 lakh.Under ‘Ehsaas 2026’, the government has proposed one counsellor for every 500 students, specialised district well-being centres and a six-tier mechanism to identify and respond to mental health concerns, including cases involving self-harm and suicide risks. The proposed centres are expected to provide psychological assessments, therapeutic interventions and psychiatric consultations.However, mental health professionals believe that increasing the number of counsellors alone will not be enough unless the quality of services improves and students feel comfortable approaching them.Dr Paramjeet Singh, Consultant Psychiatrist at PSRI Hospital, New Delhi, said, “The current numbers are much lower. More importantly, the quality of services and their acceptability among students, families, school management, etc., need to be improved rather than focusing only on increasing the numbers.”He emphasised that awareness and sensitivity towards mental health concerns must extend beyond counsellors to teachers, parents and school administrations. Training school staff to recognise signs of distress and respond appropriately would be essential to making the proposed system effective.The challenge, therefore, begins much before a student reaches a counsellor. Schools need to create an environment where students can discuss emotional difficulties without fear of judgement or stigma. Early identification and accessible support mechanisms could help ensure that warning signs are not overlooked.“Parents, students and teachers need to be educated for early identification. Universal screening of all students and other mechanisms such as suggestion boxes and help boxes should also be introduced. A safe space for open discussion needs to be created, both in terms of the overall environment and physical infrastructure. Peer mentors and peer support are also effective ways forward,” Singh said.Setting up district well-being centres will be another important step, but their effectiveness will depend on timely assessments, referrals and access to specialised treatment. The policy also provides for a digital monitoring portal and quarterly assessments through a school wellness services index to track the delivery of mental health services.Singh, however, pointed out that monitoring and accountability often remain weak links in the implementation of such initiatives.“Accountability, surveillance, monitoring and auditing of these services remain major challenges and are often missing links in ensuring their effectiveness. Multiple monitoring mechanisms can be planned at different levels, including classroom, school, parent, district, state and national levels. The monitoring requirements at each level are different but complementary,” Singh said.

headline: Delhi’s air quality better than in last 10 years, says CM Rekha Gupta
content: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday claimed that the Capital’s air quality this year was better than in the last 10 years, crediting stricter enforcement and new measures to curb pollution. Speaking at the College Day celebrations of Kamala Nehru College, where she inaugurated a new academic block, Gupta said Delhi residents were feeling a sense of relief because of the government’s efforts. “In Delhi over the last 10 years, the AQI is better this year, and the people of Delhi are feeling a sense of relief this time. This is an achievement for Delhi,” she said. “This was achieved by enforcing strictness; we introduced the necessary rules, regulations, and policies that were needed,” she said. This year, the Delhi government introduced a winter action plan under which restrictions on polluting activities are imposed during the winter months irrespective of pollution levels. This is unlike the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), under which restrictions are triggered by air quality levels. At the event, Gupta inaugurated the college’s newly-constructed ‘Vande Mataram Academic Block’ and flagged off two Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) ‘University Ladies Special’ bus services for women students. The buses will connect Laxmi Nagar and Green Park Metro stations directly to the area around Kamala Nehru College and Gargi College in South Delhi. The two colleges have a large number of women students. The buses will operate from the Metro stations between 8 am and 10.30 am and from the college area between 3 pm and 5.30 pm, at 30-minute intervals. Gupta said the government was committed to providing women students with safe and reliable transport, along with better educational facilities. The new bus services, she added, were part of efforts to improve facilities for students.

headline: Delhi air hurts more than lungs: Studies link pollution to heart disease, depression, ADHD and premature deaths
content: Delhi’s toxic air may be doing far more damage than leaving residents coughing and struggling to breathe. Studies conducted over several decades have linked Delhi's air pollution to high blood pressure, heart disease, depression, attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and premature deaths, suggesting that its health impact extends well beyond the lungs. A review by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) of 184 peer-reviewed studies – published between 1975 and 2025 – found that 169, or 91.8%, reported at least one association between air pollution and an adverse health outcome. Twenty-six of these studies were conducted in Delhi – the most studied area – followed by Punjab, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh. Across India, respiratory diseases were examined in 86 of the 184 studies, followed by mortality in 16 and cardiovascular diseases in 11. While respiratory illnesses remained the most widely consequence, the studies highlighted evidence of pollution’s impact on the heart and mental health, particularly among children and the elderly. Impact on the heart In Delhi, studies examining daily deaths found that higher exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) was associated with an increase in “non-accidental deaths”, including deaths from cardiovascular and respiratory causes. Further, the studies linked prolonged exposure to particulate pollution to higher blood pressure, increased risk of hypertension and more hospital admissions for cardiovascular conditions. Of the 11 studies examining cardiovascular diseases across India, 10 reported at least one association with air pollution. Three studies, meanwhile, found links between PM2.5 and hypertension, atherosclerosis (build-up of plaque in arteries) and arterial stiffness. Seven studies found no significant association for certain pollutants or outcomes. Impact on mental health Further, multiple studies suggested that polluted air may also affect mental health and brain development. One study involving asthma patients in Delhi found that short-term exposure to PM2.5, PM10, nitrogen dioxide and sulphur dioxide was associated with severe depression and poorer asthma control. While a study associated exposure to household cooking to depression, another linked exposure to PM10 with ADHD. “What we are is a reflection of our environment, and pollution is a major part of the environment,” Dr Rajesh Sagar, Professor of Psychiatry at AIIMS, New Delhi, told The Indian Express. “Therefore, the mental health impact of air pollution extends beyond anxiety and depression to include brain development and cognitive functions, particularly among children and young people,” he added. Sagar further said that pollutants may trigger inflammation that affects the brain, influencing mood and cognitive functions. “Anxiety and depression, the mood disorders, are one aspect of the impact,” he added. Impact on children, elderly and outdoor workers According to Dr Manojkumar N, an analyst at CREA and an author of the review, children living in industrial areas showed a higher prevalence of asthma. “Research on household cooking fuels identified associations with respiratory allergies and infections. Elevated blood lead levels were also documented among schoolchildren in areas with higher environmental lead exposure,” he added. Older residents, particularly those above the 60-65 age group, are particularly vulnerable. Studies examining mortality in Delhi found stronger links between PM2.5 exposure and daily deaths among the elderly. Studies involving autorickshaw drivers, street vendors and sweepers also documented respiratory complaints, eye irritation and reduced lung function among some participants. They are impacted more than those who work indoors. Not just a winter problem Although Delhi’s pollution draws the most attention during winter, the review indicates that health risks extend throughout the year, even indoors. Studies comparing populations in areas with different pollution levels found poorer lung function among those living in more polluted neighbourhoods. Long-term PM2.5 exposure was also associated with higher blood pressure and a greater likelihood of hypertension. Indoor pollution emerged as another concern in the studies. Prolonged exposure to solid cooking fuels such as biomass, coal and dung was linked to respiratory allergies, infections and tuberculosis. What needs to change The CREA review called for policies to focus on reducing people’s exposure to pollutants. It recommended stricter enforcement of the National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS), wider monitoring, time-bound targets for reducing pollution from each sector and tighter industrial emission controls. It also called for a faster shift from biomass, coal and dung to cleaner cooking and heating fuels. “The findings highlight the need to move beyond a city-centric approach and explicitly include rural areas through a regional, airshed-based approach in the next phase of the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP 2.0),” Manojkumar said. Further, the review recommended updating NAAQS, which was last revised in 2009. Sagar said the response should focus on awareness and prevention rather than panic. “We need to educate people about the risks, protect vulnerable populations such as pregnant women, children and the elderly, and encourage them to minimise exposure during periods of high pollution,” he added.

headline: Delhi government formally notifies 24-member Medical Council | India News
content: The Delhi government has formally notified the constitution of the 24-member Delhi Medical Council (DMC), nearly a year and a half after the previous council was dissolved amid allegations of administrative and financial irregularities, a notification published in the Delhi Gazette stated.The council is the statutory regulatory body responsible for matters concerning the registration of medical practitioners and professional conduct and ethics in Delhi. Its functions include examining complaints of medical negligence and professional misconduct and taking disciplinary action against registered practitioners.According to the health and family welfare department notification dated November 18 seen by HT, the new council includes the eight members elected in the May 31 elections.The notification states, “In exercise of the powers conferred by section 3 and sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Delhi Medical Council Act, 1997 (Delhi Act 5 of 1997), the Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi is pleased to publish the names of members of the Delhi Medical Council.”It should be noted that the DMC was dissolved on June 17, 2025, following allegations of administrative and financial irregularities.The new 24-member council comprises four members nominated by the Delhi government under clause (a) of Section 3(3) of the Act, ten representatives from medical colleges and institutions under clause (b), eight elected members under clause (c), and two ex-officio members.Who are the members?The four members listed under clause (a) are Dr Ajay Kumar, Dr Hans Raj Baweja, Dr S K Tandon (Dr Sarvesh Kumar Tandon) and Dr Vinod Kumar Monga. The institutional representatives include Dr Amarinder Singh Malhi of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Dr Vivek Jangira of Lady Hardinge Medical College and Dr Manisha Agarwal of Maulana Azad Medical College, among others.The eight elected members are Dr Prakash Lalchandani, Dr Manjusha Goel, Dr Ajay Bedi, Dr Piyush Jain, Dr Rakesh Kumar Gupta, Dr Ashok Kumar Grover, Dr Ashwini Dalmiya and Dr Vipender Sabherwal. The Dean of the Medical Faculty, University of Delhi, and the Director of Health Services, Delhi, are the two ex-officio members.Specifying the tenure, the notification states: “Subject to provisions of the aforesaid Act, the term of office of the above members shall be five years from the date of publication in the official Gazette.” It further states that the notification “issues with the prior approval of LG”.

headline: Delhi's air quality best in 10 years, people feel relief this year: CM Rekha Gupta
content: <p>New Delhi: <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/rekha-gupta">Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta</a> on Saturday said strict enforcement and regulations had improved the city’s air quality this year compared to the past 10 years.</p>.<p>Gupta’s remarks came after inaugurating a new academic block at Kamla Nehru College and university-special buses for students.</p>.<p>"In Delhi over the last 10 years, the AQI is better this year, and the people of Delhi are feeling a sense of relief this time. This is an achievement for Delhi. This was achieved by enforcing strictness; we introduced the necessary rules, regulations, and policies that were needed," Gupta said, addressing students.</p>.<p>The chief minister also said that the government is working to construct hostels to accommodate 10,000 students and add more U-special buses across the city.</p>.Air purifier sales surge as Delhi-NCR AQI deteriorates; demand spreads beyond traditional markets.<p>"U-special buses were not available in the city for the past 25 years. When our government came to power, this was one of our priorities. Today, we have also achieved 75 per cent electric vehicles in public transport," Gupta added.</p>.<p>Gupta also highlighted women helming important posts in the country.</p>.<p>“The President of the country is a woman; we see women gracing many significant and prestigious positions. From agriculture to Chandrayaan, women and daughters of the country are leading the way,” she said.</p>.<p>The chief minister also announced the government has set a target to end the three mountains of garbage (landfill sites) by the end of 2027.</p>

headline: DU awards digital degrees to 1.7L; Goyal urges students to set high goals
content: NEW DELHI: The University of Delhi (DU) issued digital degrees to 1,72,668 students at the press of a button during its 103rd convocation on Friday, marking the graduation of students from regular courses, the Non-Collegiate Women’s Education Board (NCWEB) and the School of Open Learning (SOL). The total included 1,60,438 undergraduate and 11,758 postgraduate students. It may be noted that Amit Shah was supposed to be the chief guest for the event but later replaced with Goyal.Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal, who attended the ceremony as the chief guest, presented medals to meritorious students. A total of 472 scholars were awarded PhD degrees, including 245 women and 227 men. The varsity also presented 163 gold and silver medals and conferred 34 awards on undergraduate and postgraduate students. Addressing the students, Goyal urged them to carry a sense of duty and responsibility along with the qualifications they had earned. He said positive thinking would drive the nation forward and called upon students to contribute towards maintaining the country’s unity and integrity. Goyal also appreciated the university’s decision to replace the traditional convocation gown with the angavastra, saying that respect for culture and history was important for a nation’s development. Referring to India’s ambition of becoming a developed nation by 2047, he urged students to set ambitious goals, learn from history and work towards the future.DU Vice-Chancellor Yogesh Singh presided over the ceremony at the university’s multipurpose sports complex..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Delhi was not diminished by arrival of outside civilisations: Pak Minister Malik lauds cultural amalgamation, diversity
content: New Delhi [India], November 21 (ANI): Pakistan Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination Musadik Masood Malik on Saturday lauded Delhi's ability to embrace and flourish through the arrival of different civilisations, saying the city's cultural identity had grown stronger through the assimilation of diverse influences.Addressing the inaugural Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in the national capital, Malik said, "So Delhi was not diminished by the arrival of outside civilisations; it was not diminished by people coming from outside. Rather, through civilisations arriving from outside and through people coming from beyond, it only expanded, flourished, and grew stronger."Leading the Pakistani delegation at the three-day forum, Malik emphasised the importance of celebrating diversity, distinct cultural identities and the free exchange of ideas among civilisations.Drawing on the literary legacy of Delhi and its association with Urdu poet Mirza Ghalib, Malik began his keynote address by explaining why he chose to speak in Urdu rather than English."It felt quite strange to sit here, just a few miles from Ghalib's grave, and speak in English. So my heart felt that today I should speak the voice of my heart to you in Urdu," he said.Reflecting on Ghalib's literary journey and his association with Persian and Urdu, the Pakistani minister remarked on the irony that the poet, despite considering himself a great poet of Persian, achieved global recognition through Urdu."And how strange it is that Ghalib—whose grandfather came from Samarkand and who lies buried right here beside Nizamuddin—and who considered himself a great poet of Persian, is recognised today by the entire world because of Urdu," Malik said.He also referred to Delhi's distinctive literary culture, highlighting the contributions of Delhi and Lucknow as centres of poetry, literature and culture."And this is the spirit with which I stand before you today: there are indeed many voices, many poets; Delhi has been a cradle of poetry—Lucknow too, Delhi too, Lahore too—these are centres of poetry, literature, and culture. Yet Ghalib's style of expression is something else entirely," he said.Connecting the literary example to the theme of the forum, Malik said the gathering represented an opportunity for different cultures and identities to come together without losing their individual character."So, it is this very diversity that you have invited us to celebrate. This is what you termed as the conversation of civilisations—that is, the Dialogue of civilisations," he said.Explaining his understanding of dialogue, Malik described it as a free exchange of ideas and meaning across different civilisations."In Greek origin, in 'dialogue', 'dia' means 'through', and 'logos' means 'meaning' or 'ideas'. So what does a dialogue amount to? A 'free flow of meaning through us, across civilisations.' That is what dialogue truly is," he said.He further stressed that meaningful dialogue could take place only when distinct identities and diversity were acknowledged and respected."Dialogue exists within distinct identities and within diversity. And this is the very dialogue we have come to engage in: numerous voices, numerous identities, and a dialogue among them; a free flow of ideas, a free flow of identities among them," Malik said.Invoking the works of Allama Iqbal, the Pakistani minister also drew an analogy from the poet's imaginative journey to Paradise, accompanied by Mawlana Rumi, highlighting how intellectual and cultural exchanges could transcend geographical boundaries and centuries."Since Ghalib was mentioned, the name of Allama Iqbal naturally came to my mind. Allama Iqbal undertook an imaginary journey—an imaginary journey to Paradise. That is, while on the one hand, you excavated here and delved deep into the earth, Allama Iqbal undertook an imaginative journey and ascended into the heavens," he said.Describing Iqbal's imagined companionship with Rumi, Malik pointed to the historical distance between the two poets, noting that a Punjabi poet had brought into his imagination a poet born in Balkh who lived centuries earlier."On that imaginary journey, his companion was Mawlana Rumi, whom he took along with him. There was an interval of six hundred years between them," he said.Malik subsequently explained how Iqbal's account presented two ways of looking at oneself: through one's own eyes or through the perspective of another person."One is our own perspective, meaning we continue to perceive ourselves solely through our own eyes. And the other perspective is one where we perceive ourselves through someone else's eyes—viewing ourselves from another's vantage point, through someone else's lens," he said.Concluding the analogy, Malik linked it to the gathering of representatives from different countries and civilisations at the forum."So today, we are looking at ourselves through the lens of all of you, through the eyes of all of you, and from the perspective of all of you," he said.Malik is leading the Pakistani delegation to the inaugural SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, being hosted by India in New Delhi from November 20 to 22. The three-day gathering brings together participants from SCO member states, observers and dialogue partners to explore the region's interconnected civilisational heritage and strengthen cultural cooperation.The Pakistani minister arrived on Friday and was received at the airport by Pakistan High Commission's Chargé d'Affaires in India, Saad Warraich. His visit marks the first visit by a Pakistani minister to India in three years.The forum aims to promote cultural exchange, mutual understanding and people-to-people ties among countries in the SCO region. (ANI)(This content is sourced from a syndicated feed and is published as received. The Tribune assumes no responsibility or liability for its accuracy, completeness, or content.)

headline: Pakistan minister calls for dialogue, mutual respect among diverse identities at SCO forum in Delhi
content: NEW DELHI: Pakistan’s Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination Musaddiq Masood Malik on Saturday underscored the importance of dialogue and mutual respect among diverse identities, highlighting the region’s shared history and cultural heritage at the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilizational Dialogue Forum being hosted by India in New Delhi.Malik said the region’s shared history and cultural heritage had shaped its way of life for thousands of years, emphasising the need to foster dialogue and mutual respect among diverse identities.He appreciated the description of the event as ‘Tehzeeb Ki Guftagu’, or ‘Dialogue of Civilisations’.Referring to his conversation with union culture minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat on Friday, when the Folrum was inaugurated, Malik said that the layers of history and culture had been an integral part of the region's way of life for thousands of years.It was therefore important to recognise that distinct identities have their own significance, while dialogue among diverse identities is equally essential, the Pakistani minister stated. He added that the participants had gathered precisely for this purpose--to bring together multiple voices and identities and facilitate the free flow of ideas among them. Malik further emphasised that wisdom and courage lie in acknowledging, respecting, embracing, and moving forward together with these diverse identities.It was the second day of the Forum.Referring to archaeological remains from different periods discovered during excavations at 16th-century Purana Qila, the venue of the Forum, Malik said that the fort in which the delegates were seated was, in itself, a story. "Its foundation was laid by Humayun, who belonged to the Timurid dynasty and had arrived from Central Asia. Its construction was further carried forward by Sher Shah Suri, who came from Afghanistan. Thus, within a single wall, one could find the art of two different rulers, two cultural layers, and traces of two traditions. This, he said, was the very diversity that the delegates had been invited to celebrate," read a culture ministry's press statement quoted him saying.The second day of the SCO Forum featured a series of sessions focusing on the cultural expressions of civilisations, shared heritage in art and architecture, and historical trade relations. The day-long deliberations explored various dimensions of cultural exchange, shared artistic traditions, and historical connections among different civilisations.Shekhawat, who chaired two joint sessions on the theme ‘Civilizational and Cultural Expressions’ on the second day, said that historical connections have played a significant role in bringing countries closer to one another. They have also effectively highlighted the immense potential of cultural cooperation in fostering mutual understanding, trust, and friendship, he said.Shekhwat further observed that our civilisations are not merely legacies of the past but living traditions whose knowledge continues to illuminate our present and inspire future generations.He emphasised that the shared civilizational knowledge and heritage should be harnessed to advance collective efforts through dialogue, institutional partnerships, cultural exchanges, and meaningful cooperation. The culture minister also expressed confidence that the Forum would emerge as a lasting platform for fostering civilizational understanding, strengthening cultural ties, and deepening connections among the member states of the SCO..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: India says no change in Indus Waters Treaty position amid Pakistani minister's Delhi visit
content: NEW DELHI: India on Friday reiterated that there was no change in its position on the Indus Waters Treaty, as Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Musadik Masood Malik attended the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation's (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi.Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India's position on the 1960 treaty was clear and remained unchanged."There is absolutely no change" in India's position, Jaiswal said during a media briefing when asked about Malik's participation in the forum and his earlier remarks criticising India's decision to place the treaty in abeyance.Malik arrived in New Delhi on Friday to lead Pakistan's delegation at the three-day forum, being held from November 20 to 22 at the historic Purana Qila. Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the event.India had announced on October 28 that invitations had been extended to all member countries of the SCO, including Pakistan, in keeping with established practice. Pakistan subsequently confirmed Malik's participation.The Pakistani minister had earlier criticised India's decision to place the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance following the April 22, 2025, terror attack in Pahalgam, which killed 26 people. In June, Malik warned that Pakistan would not accept any attempt to interfere with its share of water under the treaty..India announced its decision to hold the treaty in abeyance on April 23, 2025, a day after the Pahalgam attack. New Delhi linked the decision to Pakistan's alleged support for cross-border terrorism and said the treaty would remain in abeyance until Islamabad credibly and irrevocably ended such support.The treaty, signed in 1960 with the World Bank as a signatory, governs the sharing of the waters of the Indus river system between India and Pakistan. It allocates the eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej to India, while the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab are primarily allocated to Pakistan, subject to specified Indian uses.Malik, speaking on the sidelines of the SCO forum, said discussions at the event were taking place within a multilateral framework. His visit is being viewed against the backdrop of strained bilateral relations between the two countries.(With inputs from agencies)

headline: Pregnant woman assaulted with chilli powder, dragged into Dehradun spa; FIR registered | India News
content: A three-month pregnant woman was allegedly assaulted, sprayed with chilli powder and threatened with death outside a spa centre in Dehradun after she went there looking for her husband, police said on Saturday.Saima, a resident of Khurbura in Dehradun, filed a complaint against a woman, Neha, and two unidentified men at the Patel Nagar police station on Friday evening.Patel Nagar station house officer (SHO) Naresh Rathore said, “We have registered an FIR based on the complainant’s statement and launched a detailed investigation into the matter.”According to Saima’s complaint, the incident occurred around 1 pm on November 19, when she visited the Amenj Spa Centre near Niranjanpur Mandi to look for her husband. When the staff refused to share any information, she decided to return home.“I was leaving when a black car pulled up at the parking gate. A man and a woman stepped out and began abusing and assaulting me before spraying chilli powder into my eyes. They forcibly dragged me upstairs into the spa centre and threatened to kill me,” Saima said in her complaint.She added that two men and a woman associated with the spa establishment were involved in the assault. “I was in no condition to visit the police station immediately. I was so scared that I narrated the ordeal to my husband, who took me to the hospital for treatment,” she said.A First Information Report (FIR) was registered under sections 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 351(2) (criminal intimidation) and 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of peace) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

headline: Mohali shocker: 4 friends attacked after they object to women’s harassment outside mall | Hindustan Times
content: A cab driver from Mandi Gobindgarh and his three friends were allegedly attacked with a sickle after they intervened to help some women who were being harassed by a group of youths near Jubilee Walk, Sector 70, on Wednesday night.According to information, Mandeep, the taxi driver, had gone to the mall with his friends Varinder Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Husan to celebrate Husan’s birthday. They had arrived in a Fortuner (PB-08-DS-4296), belonging to their friend, and were eating pizza inside the vehicle.Around 10.50 pm, the friends saw eight to 10 youths harassing some women nearby. Mandeep said in his complaint that the women approached the four friends for help, following which they intervened and confronted the youths. The group subsequently left the spot.However, around 15 to 20 minutes later, the same youths returned and opened attack on the four friends. Mandeep alleged that the assailants attacked them with an intention to kill. One of them hit him on the head with a sickle, leaving him bleeding.Based on his complaint, a case under Sections 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 118(2) (voluntarily causing grievous hurt), 324(2) (mischief), 126(2) (wrongful restraint), 351(2) (criminal intimidation), 191(3) (rioting) and 190 (unlawful assembly) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) has been registered against eight to 10 unidentified persons. No arrests have been made so far. Police are yet to establish the identities of the attackers or the women who were allegedly harassed.GfxFacing street harassment, call for helpIn case of harassment, stalking, eve-teasing or any other threat, women can seek immediate police assistance by calling the women’s helpline 1091 or the emergency response number 112.

headline: 17 officials face action for Rs 8-cr reputational loss to Baghat bank
content: Seventeen officials, including a former Managing Director and former members of various Boards of Management (BoMs), have been identified as responsible for causing a reputational loss of Rs 8 crore to the Solan-based Baghat Urban Cooperative Bank Limited, which has been facing restrictions imposed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) since October 8, 2025.An elaborate surcharge inquiry, ordered by the Registrar of Cooperative Societies (RCS), Shimla, in March to fix financial accountability and recover losses caused by the alleged violation of statutory lending norms, has quantified the reputational loss of Rs 8 crore, according to reports accessed by The Tribune.The amount will be recovered from the 17 officials held responsible for the loss. These include the outgoing chairman and a former Managing Director, who will each be liable to pay Rs 1 crore for the substantial damage caused to the bank''s reputation following the RBI-imposed restrictions. Besides, seven BoM members, seven former managers and another employee will be liable to pay amounts ranging from Rs 25 lakh to Rs 50 lakh each. The individual liability has been determined on the basis of the responsibilities entrusted to them."These 17 officials have been served notices seeking their explanations by December 3. Following this, the formal process of issuing chargesheets and conducting the subsequent inquiry will be initiated," an official confirmed.The RCS had initially issued a show-cause notice to the BoM under Section 37 of the Himachal Pradesh Cooperative Societies Act, 1968, on June 20, after the RBI issued a notice to the bank regarding the possible cancellation of its licence. In a strongly worded communication, the RCS had flagged persistent and serious irregularities in the bank's functioning, which were in violation of statutory provisions and RBI guidelines.In September 2026, the RCS removed all nine members of the bank's BoM over its poor financial performance and debarred them from contesting bank elections for three years. Their replies to the show-cause notices were found unsatisfactory.Pertinently, the RBI has imposed several financial restrictions on the bank since October 8, 2025, including a ban on fresh loans, loan renewals and advances. It has also capped withdrawals by individual depositors at Rs 10,000. The restrictions were imposed after the bank's financial parameters breached the prescribed statutory limits. These measures have severely damaged the bank's reputation, eroding the trust of its 80,000 depositors and 11,000 shareholders.Although the bank has made significant improvements in its financial health, the RBI is yet to extend further relaxations pending a statutory audit. The bank has reduced its gross non-performing assets (NPAs) to Rs 95 crore from Rs 138 crore as on October 8, 2025. Its net NPA has also declined to 3 per cent from 22 per cent, while its Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) has improved to 12 per cent from a negative 12.21 per cent as of March 2026.

headline: Himachal passes Bill mandating 80% jobs for locals in industries, single window clearance
content: Industries operating in Himachal Pradesh will have to reserve 80 per cent of the jobs for residents of the state under a new Bill passed by the Vidhan Sabha on Saturday. The Bill seeks to provide statutory backing to local employment while creating a time-bound, single-window mechanism for investment clearances. The Himachal Pradesh Investment Promotion and Facilitation Bill, 2026, introduced by Industries Minister Harshwardhan Chauhan, was passed by voice vote on the last day of the Assembly's winter session. It provides a comprehensive legal framework to attract investment, expedite industrial approvals, strengthen infrastructure and promote sustainable industrialisation. During the debate on the Bill, BJP MLA Bikram Singh Thakur questioned the need for a new legislation, pointing out that the state already had an industrial policy formulated in 2019 and a Single Window System for granting clearances. He also questioned the government's intentions behind bringing the Bill. Responding to him, Chauhan said every state had its own industrial legislation and the new law would bring industries in Himachal Pradesh within a statutory framework, making them legally accountable for complying with government conditions. He said a similar legislation had been drafted in 2018 but was not implemented by the previous government. The minister said the present government had brought the Bill keeping the state's interests in mind, particularly the need to provide legal protection to employment opportunities for Himachalis. Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said, "The legislation would replace procedural complexities with transparent and time-bound facilitation while ensuring that investment generates quality employment for Himachali youth and promotes balanced development”. A key provision of the Bill is the creation of a Single Window Approval, Clearance, Reviewing and Monitoring Authority, headed by the Chief Minister, to oversee investment proposals and coordinate clearances across government departments. The Bill provides for a dedicated state-level investor facilitation mechanism, a digital platform and a Combined Application Form for regulatory and non-regulatory approvals. It also introduces self-certification for eligible investors, auto-renewal and perpetual validity of notified approvals, risk-based inspections, easier exit procedures and an automatic appeal mechanism for applications delayed beyond prescribed timelines. An Industrial Advisory Forum has also been envisaged to facilitate stakeholder participation in decision-making. The legislation further provides for the creation of a land bank comprising suitable public and private land, optimal utilisation of industrial plots, and development of industrial estates, clusters and green corridors. Public-private participation will be encouraged in developing industrial infrastructure. A high-powered mechanism involving the government, industry representatives and registered transport operators will also work towards rationalising freight rates to address logistics costs. The framework provides for action against investors violating agreed conditions as well as officials responsible for substantial delays in processing applications. Chauhan said the legislation would provide the statutory foundation for the state's upcoming Industrial Policy. Besides the investment legislation, the House passed five other Bills on Saturday, taking the total number of Bills passed during the winter session to 13. Chief Minister Sukhu introduced the Public Safety and Convenience (Third Amendment) Bill, 2026, aimed at ensuring the safety and convenience of road users and pedestrians in Shimla. Under its provisions, residents living along sealed roads will be eligible for three-year vehicle permits. The Bill was passed without discussion. Chauhan also introduced the Himachal Pradesh Khadi and Village Industries Board (Amendment) Bill, 2026, and the Himachal Pradesh Jan Vishwas (Trust-based Governance) Provisions (Amendment) Bill, 2026. Both were passed without discussion. In the absence of Public Works Minister Vikramaditya Singh, Ayush Minister Yadvinder Goma introduced the Himachal Pradesh Municipalities (Amendment) Bill, 2026, and the Himachal Pradesh Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026. Both were passed without discussion or opposition.

headline: High Court bench in Dharamshala: Himachal Assembly passes resolution, seeks Centre’s approval
content: The Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly on Saturday unanimously passed a resolution seeking the establishment of a permanent bench of the Himachal Pradesh High Court at Dharamshala, with Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu saying the move would make justice more accessible to people in Kangra and other lower districts of the state. Sukhu moved the resolution on the last day of the Assembly’s winter session. It calls for the state government to submit a formal and comprehensive proposal to the Union government after consultations with the Chief Justice of the Himachal Pradesh High Court and the Governor. The resolution cited the difficulties faced by litigants, lawyers and others from Kangra and neighbouring districts in travelling to Shimla for court proceedings. The long distances, difficult terrain and travel costs often result in financial hardship, loss of time and delays in accessing justice, it said. “The proposal is based on the difficulties faced by litigants, lawyers and ordinary citizens from Kangra and other lower Himachal districts in travelling to Shimla to attend court proceedings. Long geographical distances, difficult road conditions and the associated travel expenses often cause inconvenience, financial burden and delays in accessing justice,” Sukhu said. The resolution also pointed to the substantial number of pending cases originating from Kangra and other lower districts as a reason for the proposed bench. Sukhu said the proposal was not intended to dilute the importance or status of the High Court’s principal seat in Shimla, but to bring judicial services closer to people living in the lower parts of the state. The resolution invokes Article 214 of the Constitution, which provides for a High Court for every state, and Section 51(2) of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, under which the President can establish a permanent bench of a High Court at a place other than its principal seat, subject to consultations with the Governor and the Chief Justice. The state government has also committed to providing land, court buildings, residential facilities, digital infrastructure and financial resources required to make the proposed Dharamshala bench operational at the earliest. The resolution will now form the basis of the state government’s proposal to the Centre, which will have to take the proposal forward under the applicable constitutional and statutory provisions.

headline: Fake medicine probe reveals multi-state network
content: Lucknow: The ongoing investigations into the supply of fake medicines in UP have thrown up that the network has been operational in other states as well. UP Food Safety and Drug Administration, which has been carrying out raids against fake medicines and also identified two manufacturing units in Himachal Pradesh, revealed that fake billing and multiple drug licences were being used and multiple firms were operating under the same name. Over the past few days, the department has seized fake and suspect medicines worth Rs 7.57 crore and registered 24 FIRs.A UPFSDA official said that in Amroha and Moradabad, licences for eight drug firms were obtained under the same name and partnership, and instead of genuine counter-to-counter sales, medicines were being stockpiled and illegally traded through fake billing. Police have arrested three accused in this case.The department has also said that packaging and labels of more than 30 brands of well-known companies were being copied and all kinds of fake medicines like antibiotics, painkillers, gastric medicines, etc, were being released in the market.In the 24 FIRs filed till now, the department has named 45 firms and 90 individuals. These include nine FIRs each in Agra and Lucknow, two in Varanasi, and one each in Saharanpur, Gonda, Meerut and Raebareli.During the investigation, action was taken against an illegal manufacturing unit in Deoband, two illegal manufacturing units in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, one in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, and two in Solan, Himachal Pradesh.“The state govt’s highest priority is to provide citizens with safe and effective medicines. The trade in fake medicines is a play with the health and lives of patients, and it will not be tolerated at any cost. The objective of UPFSDA is not limited to seizing fake medicines and arresting the accused, but to reach from the original manufacturing source of the entire network to the last link of the supply chain and eliminate it,” said Roshan Jacob, secretary and commissioner, UPFSDA.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. headline: Sukhu accuses previous BJP regime of ‘selling’ Himachal assets | Hindustan Times
content: Himachal Pradesh chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Friday accused the previous BJP government of putting state’s assets up for sale and allotting land to private firms at throwaway prices in the name of customised packages.Replying to an adjournment motion under Rule 67 brought by the opposition BJP legislators on Tuesday, during the ongoing winter session of the House, on the alleged sale of state assets, Sukhu said industrial land was given to big companies at concessional rates while young entrepreneurs from Himachal were made to pay market prices.When Speaker Kuldeep Singh Pathania asked the CM to begin his reply, the Opposition began protesting and trooped into the well of the House, alleging that some of their members were yet to speak on the motion.Despite the protests, Sukhu continued with his reply, and the Opposition continued sloganeering in the well of the House. Afterwards BJP MLAs staged a walkout.Sukhu alleged that during the previous BJP government’s tenure, industrial plots were converted into real estate projects. The CM said 300 bighas were allotted to a private firm at ₹1 per square metre, along with a waiver of electricity duty of ₹3 per unit. He claimed that no work had been undertaken on the proposed project so far.He also alleged that around 4,000 bighas were allotted at the same rate, while another 150 bighas were given to another private firm. He claimed that nearly 5,000 bighas in the Baddi-Nalagarh belt were being considered for a 99-year lease at the nominal rate.The CM accused the previous regime of favouring a company associated with a film personality by allotting around 124 bighas in Manali, allegedly worth more than ₹500 crore, despite the company being a defaulter in Uttarakhand.Targets BJP over financial crisis, walkoutTaking a dig at BJP’s walkout, Sukhu said the opposition had brought the motion but did not stay in the House to hear the government’s response. He also accused the BJP of being divided into five factions.On the state’s financial position, he said the discontinuation of the revenue deficit grant (RDG) had resulted in a loss of ₹8,000 crore to Himachal Pradesh. However, he assured government employees and pensioners that salaries and pensions would not be withheld, while arrears would be cleared in a phased and systematic manner.Defends electric bus procurementResponding to allegations concerning electric buses, Sukhu said the tender conditions provided for 12 years of free maintenance by the supplier and a minimum range of 180km on a single charge. He claimed that buses had subsequently covered 246km and 276km on a single charge.He said his government had withheld payments wherever corruption allegations had surfaced and would take action if irregularities were established.

headline: Shimla’s iconic Peterhoff Hotel mired in political controversy over its future | India News
content: Perched on Shimla’s tranquil Chaura Maidan enclave, Hotel Peterhoff has witnessed history unfolding across the arc of India’s journey, from a British colony to an independent nation. Flanked by the Himachal State Museum on one side and the stately Viceregal Lodge on the other, the Tudor-style estate is ringed by dense deodar forests. Commissioned in 1863 as the summer seat of the British Raj, the estate housed seven consecutive Viceroys at the zenith of imperial power. Following Independence and the horrors of Partition, the hotel became the temporary seat of the high court.Between 1948 and 1949, its courtroom was the focus of a grieving nation during the trial of Nathuram Godse and his co-conspirators for the assassination of Mahatma Gandhi. In 1971, the estate transitioned into Himachal Pradesh’s Raj Bhavan upon the hill state’s attainment of full statehood. A decade later, on a cold January night in 1981, a blaze ripped through the mansion. It was rebuilt and in 1991 opened as a 35-room government luxury hotel, the architecture pairing steeply pitched roofs and wide sunlit verandas with warm, wood-panelled interiors.But now, the historic estate is caught in a spiralling political controversy between the Congress and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) as the state government appears ready to hand the property over to a private operator under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model.Former chief minister and leader of opposition, Jai Ram Thakur has accused the state government of handing over the property to “close associates” in the name of the PPP model.Chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu of the Congress-ruled state that “we are not selling Peterhoff” and it is being “demolished” to be converted to a 100-room hotel.On January 19, the state cabinet decided to demolish the estate, citing “leakage problems and deteriorating condition” for the move. As per the proposal, the government plans to demolish the structure, but the tender process is yet to start.On Friday, the CM, while speaking in the state assembly, said: “I wish to clarify in this House that we are not selling Peterhoff. A tender has been issued for its demolition—which will be opened on the November 27—and we intend to construct over 100 rooms there; this is well within our authority”.The hotel was also asked to stop taking bookings from June but the decision was deferred in light of advance bookings for events.The hotel stopped bookings after November 25.The issue dominated the winter session with the BJP accusing the state government of putting “Himachal on sale”.But chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu denied the charges. “We will neither sell any public assets nor allow them to be plundered. Peterhoff is not being sold, and the government has no intention of selling any government property,” he said.Sukhu said the government was working towards developing an even larger Peterhoff, with at least 100 rooms, to improve its facilities. “The old Peterhoff was destroyed in a fire, and a new building was subsequently constructed during the tenure of the previous government,” he added.The Himachal Pradesh Tourism Corporation Employees’ Union (HPTCEU) appealed to the government to keep Peterhoff under the current management, citing a potential loss of jobs. The union said that 70 to 80% of the hotel can be restored to a functional state and upgraded with modern amenities.“The union has already appealed to the Himachal Pradesh government to keep Hotel Peterhoff under its management instead of handing it over to private hands as this would lead to loss of jobs,” HPTCEU general secretary Raj Kumar told HT.The row is only the latest twist in the hotel’s journey.In 1971, when Himachal Pradesh became a full-fledged state, Peterhoff was the Raj Bhavan, the official residence of the governor. In 1981, a massive fire broke out there during the tenure of governor Aminuddin Ahmed Khan. The Raj Bhavan was then shifted to the Barnes’ Court building.The then BJP government led by Shanta Kumar in 1990 renamed the building Meghdoot.It also decided to develop it as a five-star hotel, which was built in 1991.When the Congress assumed power in 1993, chief minister Virbhadra Singh renamed it Hotel Peterhoff.The original building was in the Tudor style, with wooden frames and shingled eaves and a pitched roof set within landscaped grounds. The hotel was managed jointly by Himachal Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation and the state government, and converted into a state-run guest house-cum-hotel. Interior spaces reflected a blend of grandeur and colonial styling, with large suites, a grand lawn, and period-appropriate detailing.In November 2021, Peterhoff got a makeover worth ₹11.5 crore. It has 34 rooms, of which 17 are owned by the Himachal Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation; two suites are with the governor, one with the CM, six allocated for state guests, and eight with the state’s general administration department.

headline: 150-year-old animal sacrifice tradition discontinued at Mata Nagarkoti Temple in Himachal Pradesh
content: CHANDIGARH: A 150-year-old tradition of animal sacrifice has been discontinued at the Mata Nagarkoti Temple in Daroti village of Shimla district, Himachal Pradesh, with villagers unanimously deciding to replace the practice with symbolic, virtuous and non-violent rituals.The decision was formalised during a two-day consecration ceremony of the newly constructed Nagarkoti Mata Daroteshwari Temple, a shrine dedicated to the local deity, built at a cost of around Rs 2 crore. The temple construction began nearly a decade ago and was recently completed.State Public Works Minister Vikramaditya Singh and Education Minister Rohit Thakur attended the ceremony, which drew thousands of devotees.The celebrations began on Thursday with a grand Dev Milan ritual between Daroteshwari Mata and Devta Narayan, followed by a Shikha Pujan ceremony on Friday, as devotees gathered at the village to pay obeisance to the deity.Ahead of the consecration, around 25 devotees, accompanied by the sacred symbols of the deity, undertook a 300-km pilgrimage beginning November 1. They travelled to Kangra, proceeded to Haridwar in Uttarakhand to take a holy dip in the Ganga, and returned to Daroti on November 19.According to locals, the original abode of Mata Nagarkoti is believed to have been at Nagarkot, from where the deity is said to have appeared in Daroti several centuries ago. A Shand Yagna was earlier held at the temple in 1962.Temple priest Ved Prakash Bhardwaj said animal sacrifice had long been an established practice at the shrine, but villagers and members of the Dev Samaj community decided a couple of months ago to prohibit it at all religious ceremonies and events in the future.“It is a positive change in the present time. Such changes will not only help give a new direction to society but also preserve our spiritual and cultural traditions and values,” he said.Animal sacrifice has remained a centuries-old practice at several hill temples in Himachal Pradesh, where goats and sheep are offered as part of religious rituals rooted in faith and belief. However, the Himachal Pradesh High Court, on September 1, 2014, imposed a statewide ban on animal sacrifice at public places and during religious ceremonies..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest
