headline: Deputy Commissioner Anupam Kashyap stresses need to make governance people-oriented
content: Deputy Commissioner Anupam Kashyap today said the main objective of the administration was to make government functioning more people-oriented so that the benefits of government schemes and development activities reached the last person in society.Kashyap was chairing a meeting with officials of various departments in Shimla district to review preparations for the Local Fund Accounts (LFA) Committee meeting scheduled for November 27, 2026. He said the LFA Committee meeting was not merely an exercise to review financial data and audit objections but also an effective platform to make the administrative system more transparent, accountable and results-oriented.He said LFA Committee meetings played an important role in ensuring financial discipline, transparency and accountability in administrative functioning. Such meetings helped assess the actual utilisation of government funds, review the progress of development projects and promptly address financial irregularities and procedural deficiencies. This ensured the optimum use of public resources and helped improve the delivery of development schemes and their benefits to the public, he added.He stressed that every department should discharge its responsibilities with complete integrity, transparency and commitment. Prudent utilisation of financial resources, timely settlement of pending cases and ensuring quality in development works were important pillars of good governance, he added. He directed officials to prepare a comprehensive report on various development works undertaken during the past three years. He also asked them to provide clear and authentic details of the budget allocated to their respective departments during this period, expenditure incurred, unspent balances and the current financial position.He said a comparative assessment of budget allocations and actual expenditure was essential to understand the pace of development works, departmental efficiency and financial management. The committee’s review would also help identify areas where funds had not been utilised at the expected pace and enable the departments to take corrective measures, he added.

headline: Trump, Xi Agreed on AI Curb in Military Action, Bessent Says
content: President Donald Trump and China’s Xi Jinping agreed that artificial intelligence should never be allowed to make autonomous major military actions, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday.“President Trump, and President Xi agreed that humans should always be involved in any military decisions that SI makes, and the SI should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions,” Bessent told CNBC, using Trump’s preferred abbreviation. He spoke after returning from a trip to Asia during which Trump met with Xi and Russia’s Vladimir Putin. Bessent is the lead American official on maintaining relations with China, and has previously met with Vice Premier He Lifeng to create a dialogue on AI between the two countries where they can notify each other on threats related to the technology.Trump said that he spoke with Xi about AI and that both leaders want regulations, according to a Thursday report from Fox News. The president’s meeting with Xi came after the ouster of Nvidia Corp’s CEO Jensen Huang, who stepped down after confirming that he had been in a relationship with a suspected Chinese agent, Alice Huang, who was also an AI chips-related business executive, and is under investigation by the US government for potentially smuggling chips. Bessent said that Jensen Huang did not come up in his conversation with the Chinese. Trump said earlier he didn’t raise the issue with Xi.Bessent last week pointed to the Commerce Department for not adding Megaspeed International, a company tied to Alice Huang, to a US trade blacklist. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has come under increasing scrutiny for his role in preventing the export of advanced AI chips to China. Lutnick and Bessent both joined Trump on his trip to Asia. When asked Friday if there was any disagreement within Trump’s cabinet over how aggressive to be with China, Bessent said “I think we’re all committed to following President Trump’s instructions.”The Trump administration earlier this week moved to heighten scrutiny on the exports of processors to several countries and restrict Chinese companies from obtaining remote access to artificial intelligence chips and servers. The interim Commerce Department rule was directed and written by the Treasury Department and National Security Council. “I think we we are going to see that the the proper chip restrictions are in place, the and the remote access has been curtailed,” Bessent said Friday. The Treasury chief added that he does not expect any change in current Trump administration policy related to Nvidia’s chip exports, nothing that there’s been a “paucity” of Nvidia H200 orders from China due to their efforts to develop competing chips within the country. ©2026 Bloomberg L.P.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Only 4 of 10 richest Indians rank among country's top philanthropists
content: India’s wealthy gave 11 per cent more to philanthropy in 2025-26 (FY26), with the number of philanthropists on the EdelGive Hurun India Philanthropy List reaching a record 219, up from 192 a year earlier, but only four of the 10 richest Indians on the M3M Hurun India Rich List 2026 — Shiv Nadar & family, Gautam Adani & family, Mukesh Ambani & family and the Poonawallas (Cyrus and Adar) — also featured among the top 10 philanthropists. The remaining six positions were occupied by donors who did not make the country’s top 10 richest list. These included the Bajaj family, Nandan Nilekani, Kumar Mangalam Birla, Sudhir and Samir Mehta, Ranjan Pai and Rohini Nilekani (who does not feature on the Rich List at all). The top 10 philanthropists gave ₹6,572 crore, or almost 57 per cent of the total. Together, the 219 Indians donated ₹11,554 crore between April 1, 2025 and March 31, 2026, an 11 per cent increase from ₹10,380 crore in FY25. The list covers Indians who gave at least ₹5 crore. It includes only those willing to disclose their giving, so the actual number of philanthropists and the total donated could be higher. A donor’s total includes personal giving as well as donations made by companies they own, in proportion to their shareholding. Personal giving still under half Out of the 192, only 42 donors donated from their personal wealth, contributing ₹5,413 crore, making 47 per cent of the total. 53 per cent still came through company Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives. Only six of the top 10 philanthropists gave majorly from personal wealth, while the other four — Adani, Bajaj, Ambani and Birla — based their giving mostly on CSR. Nadar leads, Adani surges Shiv Nadar and family retained the top spot for the fifth year, giving ₹2,593 crore, or ₹7.1 crore a day. This was 4 per cent lower than last year, and 93 per cent of it was personal. Arts, culture and heritage took the largest share at ₹1,220 crore. Gautam Adani and family moved up three places to second, with giving up 127 per cent to ₹877 crore from ₹386 crore. The ₹491 crore rise is the largest on the list. The Bajaj family stayed third at ₹632 crore, and Mukesh Ambani and family were fourth at ₹620 crore. Nandan Nilekani rose to fifth with ₹380 crore, almost all of it personal. He has also donated 10.1 per cent of his wealth since 2019, the highest percentage among anyone in the top 10. Kumar Mangalam Birla and family were sixth at ₹366 crore, with 16 per cent of it coming from personal funds. Cyrus S Poonawalla and Adar Poonawalla (₹336 crore) and Sudhir Mehta and Samir Mehta (₹334 crore) followed. Ranjan Pai and family entered the top 10 philanthropists list at ninth with ₹219 crore, of which 98 per cent came from personal funds. Women philanthropists increase their presence Twenty-nine women feature in the list this year, up from 24 last year. Rohini Nilekani, who ranks tenth with ₹215 crore, is the most generous woman on the list, ahead of Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw (₹93 crore) and Anu Aga and family (₹78 crore). Rohini Nilekani is the only person on the overall list to have donated almost a 100 per cent in a personal capacity, and has donated ₹1,121 crore since 2019. The 19 donors who gave ₹100 crore each or more, just 9 per cent of the list, accounted for ₹7,838 crore, or 68 per cent of all donations. At the other end, 80 donors who gave ₹5-10 crore each make up 37 per cent of the list but only 5 per cent of the giving. New donors, new causes There were 45 new entrants, up from 12 last year, and they contributed ₹696 crore. Raamdeo Agrawal (₹120 crore) and Motilal Oswal (₹119 crore) led them, followed by Chandrika and Ranjan Tandon (₹100 crore), whose gift will set up a School of Artificial Intelligence at IIM Ahmedabad. Self-made donors number 125, or 57 per cent of the list, and account for 65 per cent of the total donations. Education remained the top cause at ₹4,188 crore (share of 36 per cent). Healthcare rose 82 per cent to ₹1,768 crore, and environment and sustainability rose 86 per cent to ₹813 crore. Social development and Skill development saw the fastest growth, at 1,466 per cent and 1,614 per cent respectively. Mumbai has the most philanthropists at 64, but New Delhi leads by value with ₹3,168 crore. The biggest movers The sharpest jump in rank belongs to Farukbhai Gulambhai Patel of KP Group, who climbed 105 places to 48th by giving ₹30 crore, up from ₹7 crore a year earlier. The largest percentage increase was recorded by Irfan Razack, Noaman Razack and Rezwan Razack of Prestige Estates Projects, whose giving rose 425 per cent to ₹42 crore. CSR: Record unspent funds Among BSE 200 companies, CSR spending was ₹18,922 crore, close to last year’s record of ₹18,963 crore. But unspent CSR hit a record ₹2,290 crore, up from ₹1,920 crore, while spending above the mandate fell to ₹1,107 crore from ₹1,821 crore. The net shortfall of ₹1,183 crore is the widest in over a decade. Reliance Industries spent ₹1,223 crore against a mandated ₹1,032 crore. Anas Rahman Junaid, founder of Hurun India, said India’s earlier stage of wealth creation suggests room to grow. China’s list has 30 donors giving at least $15 million each, against 19 in India giving ₹100 crore or more. “As our economy doubles, our ambition should be to more than double the number of large philanthropists,” he said.

headline: Tipper stuck as manhole cover collapses on Basant Nagar Road in Ludhiana | Hindustan Times
content: A tipper unloading bitumen for road repair on Basant Nagar road along the Buddah Nullah got stuck after the slab covering a manhole collapsed.The tipper’s rear wheels were parked on the manhole slab when it was unloading bitumen for blacktopping of the road. “As the tipper rose the carrier section to unload bitumen, its load transferred to the rear tyres. The cover fell into the manhole, leading to the tipper losing its balance,” said Himanshu Sharma, junior engineer, operations and maintainance (O&M) cell.He said the slab was placed there in 2003 and had served its time. These slabs can carry up to 50 metric tonnes of weight, he said.This is the third incident involving heavy vehicles getting stuck on the road on the same stretch. The earlier incidents took place in April and September. However, Sharma claimed that the three incidents were not linked.He said that three lines passed under the road — a water supply pipe, an eight-inch sewer line and a 30-inch sewer line.“The first incident in April had taken place after a leakage from the water supply line had eroded the soil under the road. Then a similar incident took place in September involving the eight-inch sewer line,” he added.

headline: Indian sports wrap, November 21: Tata Steel World 25K Kolkata set for 11th edition on December 20
content: CHENNAI ATHLETICS Tata Steel World 25K Kolkata returns on December 20 The Tata Steel World 25K Kolkata will return for its 11th edition on December 20, with organisers expecting another strong turnout as the event continues to promote fitness, inclusivity and community participation. Promoted by Procam International, the event will be flagged off from the iconic Red Road. With 30 days to go, the organisers said registrations for the 25K category closed in just 14 hours following an overwhelming response. The Open 10K, Champions with Disability, Senior Citizen Run and Ananda Run categories have also received an encouraging response, underlining the event’s growing appeal across age groups and abilities. The event has also received the support of the West Bengal government, with Ashok Dinda, Minister of State for MSME and Food Supply, and Dr. Subrata Gupta, Chief Advisor to the Chief Minister, highlighting its role in promoting physical fitness and sporting participation. “Running a marathon is not as easy as it sounds. It requires dedication, discipline and proper preparation. Having participated in distance runs in Asansol, Tamluk and Kolkata, I understand the physical challenges that come with long-distance running,” Dinda said in a release. “My aim is to prepare well and complete the run on December 20. I hope this edition becomes a historic event where people across Bengal come together, participate and run with the spirit of never looking back.” A major attraction of this year’s edition will be the unveiling of the ‘Medal of Steel’ for 25K finishers. Crafted from Tata Steel, the medal celebrates the endurance, determination and perseverance required to complete the challenging distance. The organisers also unveiled medals for participants in the Open 10K, Ananda Run, Senior Citizen Run and Champions with Disability categories. -Press Trust of India HOCKEY Punjab Hockey League Season 3: Roundglass Hockey Academy score 10 past SDAT Roundglass Hockey Academy registered its second straight win as it thrashed Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu (SDAT) 10-0 in the third edition of Punjab Hockey League at the Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium in Mohali on Saturday. A total of 94 boats representing 17 clubs competed across nine Olympic classes, making it the largest Senior National Championships in terms of participation in the last five years. As many as 91 races were completed during the competition held off the Sunk Rock and Prongs Lighthouses. Two-time Olympian and Asian Games bronze medallist Vishnu Saravanan clinched his seventh national title in the ILCA 7 class, winning seven of the nine races. Asian Games 2026 silver medallists Prince Noble and Manu Francis won the 49er title, while bronze medallist Harshita Tomar, partnering Ritika Dangi, topped the 49erFX class after winning nine of their 10 races. Doiphode SI and Ramya Saravanan dominated the Nacra 17 class, winning all 10 races, while Shraddha Verma and Ravindra Kumar Sharma secured their fifth national title in the 470 mixed class. Neha Thakur won the ILCA 6 title, while Aditya Sangwan topped the iQFOiL men’s category. Prarthana Bhoi won the iQFOiL women’s title, and Asish S Roy emerged victorious in Formula Kite men. The championships were conducted by the Indian Naval Watermanship Training Centre, Mumbai, under the aegis of YAI and the Indian Naval Sailing Association. -PTI SNOOKER Anupama defeats Man Yan, retains World snooker title India’s Anupama Ramachandran found her rhythm at the right juncture to outplay So Man Yan and retain her IBSF World Snooker title in Indore on Saturday. After losing the scrappy first frame, Anupama raised her game to score a comfortable 3-1 win over her Hong Kong China rival, becoming the first Indian to win back-to-back crowns. Reacting to the win, Anupama told Sportstar: “I didn’t start very well in the final and I was a little nervous, but I did better. I think I played much better in the last three frames. I am genuinely happy with how I performed throughout the tournament.” Defending the title and winning it in India made the victory special, said Anupama. “I beat Tessa (Davidson) of England 3-1 in the semifinals and Keerthana (Pandian) 3-1 in the quarterfinals. They all pushed me to do my best,” she added. In the men’s title clash, Ali Gharahgozlou of Iran outclassed Hong Kong China’s Tam Yun Fung 5-1. After edging out India’s Pankaj Advani 5-3 in the semifinals earlier in the day, the Iranian enthralled the crowd with a brilliant exhibition of potting and amazing consistency, taking home a USD 10,000 cheque. Anupama, who was richer by USD 4,000 for her splendid triumph, started a trifle tentatively. However, she gathered her wits quickly to put her rival in trouble, making fine runs of 31, 19 and 16 to clinch the second frame. Further breaks of 16, 28 and 18 helped Anupama take a 2-1 lead. In the fourth frame, Man Yan began aggressively with an early 20, but Anupama was equal to the task, making breaks of 14 and 26 before missing the blue to the top-right pocket. But Anupama soon potted a long blue to the bottom-right and the pink to the top-right to retain her title. - PTI GYMNASTICS Maiden Youth Artistic Gymnastics National Championship to be held in Mumbai The Indian Navy Sports Control Board (INSCB), on behalf of the Services Sports Control Board (SSCB) and under the aegis of the Gymnastics Federation of India (GFI), will host the first-ever Youth Artistic Gymnastics (Men & Women) National Championship 2026–27 at INS Hamla, Malad (West), Mumbai, from November 24 to December 1. headline: ‘Riot victims deserve sympathy & empathy’: HC orders Punjab govt to restore plot to 1984 survivor
content: Chandigarh: Directing Ludhiana Improvement Trust (LIT) to restore a 40-square-yard plot allotted to a 1984 Delhi riots victim, which was cancelled in 1992 for non-payment, Punjab and Haryana high court has said that riot victims “deserve sympathy and empathy”.The division bench of Justice Jasgurpreet Singh Puri and Justice Pravindra Singh Chauhan also imposed Rs 50,000 in costs, to be paid equally by the state and LIT. HC termed the state’s rejection “totally cryptic”, arbitrary and violative of the Constitution.“While passing orders, particularly in cases involving persons who have suffered under extraordinary circumstances, the authorities are expected to exercise due care and diligence and should not reject the claims of riot victims in a casual or routine manner,” the bench observed in the recent order.“Riot victims deserve not only sympathy and empathy, but their rights under Article 21 of the Constitution of India also get severely impaired if caution and prudence are not adhered to. Therefore, the state should be extremely careful in dealing with such cases,” it added.The petitioner, Mohinder Singh, was allotted a plot in the 475-acre Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar Scheme in Ludhiana under Sikh Migrant Quota on Aug 12, 1987, for Rs 3,520. He was required to pay the amount within 30 days, either in full or by depositing one-fourth and paying the balance in instalments. He was unable to pay because of extreme poverty after the riots, and his allotment was cancelled in 1992.His request for a second chance was rejected in 2007. In 2015, Punjab govt offered defaulting allottees a one-time opportunity to deposit outstanding charges, including interest, penalty and deemed restoration charges, and get their allotments regularised. But Singh’s request was again rejected on Nov 24, 2015, citing failure to deposit 25% of the price within 30 days and a delay of 23 years.He approached high court. His counsel, S S Salar, argued that the policy covered allottees whose plots had been resumed or cancelled. He said the plot was still vacant and the petitioner was ready to pay the requisite amount with reasonable interest.Punjab AAG Raghav Goel submitted that the case was not covered by the policy, and Advocate Manbir Singh Batth for LIT argued that the cancellation had been communicated and there was a considerable delay in filing the writ petition.The bench held that default in payment could not be used to deny the petitioner benefit of the very policy framed to address such defaults, pointing out that the 2015 policy covered allottees who had not paid even after expiry of the deadline.On the delay, the court noted that Singh had been approaching the authorities from the beginning and the policy prescribed no time limit for seeking its benefit. “Once the petitioner is admittedly a riot victim, he could not have been non-suited on the ground of delay,” the bench observed.On LIT’s objection that Singh had not mentioned his poor financial condition in his application, the bench said that being a riot victim, “it was not necessary for him to have proved his bad economic condition”.HC set aside the cancellation order and directed LIT to restore the plot and deliver possession. The petitioner was told to pay the allotment price prevailing in 1987, with simple interest at 10% per annum, within 30 days of LIT’s order regarding resumption. headline: Two Punjab brothers killed in Greece, relative held; family seeks probe
content: Two brothers from Punjab, who had gone to Greece in search of better livelihood, were allegedly killed by a relative there earlier this month, their family on Saturday alleged. Their bodies reached Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar, on Friday, 18 days after the November 3 killings. They were cremated at their native Talwandi Sanghera village in Shahkot subdivision of Jalandhar district on Saturday. Daljit Singh, 26, and his younger brother Gurwinder Singh, 23, were allegedly attacked with a knife at a pig farm in Livanates in Greece’s Fthiotida region, where both were working. Greek police arrested their 45-year-old relative, Sandeep Singh, who was also employed at the farm. He was subsequently remanded in judicial custody, according to Greek media reports. The brothers’ father, Boota Singh, said the family was financially weak and had borrowed money to send Daljit to Greece on a work permit around eight months ago. Sandeep, a distant relative from Gumtali village in Jalandhar, had allegedly persuaded the family to send Daljit, promising better employment opportunities. “Both my sons were mechanics in India. One worked as an air-conditioner mechanic and the other was skilled in installing security cameras. Had I known that my sons would meet such a fate there, I would never have thought of sending them,” Boota Singh said. Around five months after reaching Greece, Daljit called his younger brother there, the father said. Gurwinder had been in Greece for about three months when the two were killed. The family has not been able to ascertain what led to the killings. “We do not know the exact reason because no one from our family was there. We are trying to find out what happened,” Boota Singh said. Some family members claimed that money had been promised to Sandeep for arranging the brothers’ safe passage and that the family had been unable to pay the entire amount. They have sought a thorough investigation into whether this had any connection with the killings. According to Greek media reports, the attack took place around 11 am on November 3. Sandeep allegedly attacked the brothers with a knife, seriously injuring both. One died at the spot, while the other succumbed to his injuries after being taken to a health centre. Following the attack, the accused reportedly climbed onto a feed silo and threatened to jump. Police and a negotiator persuaded him to come down before taking him into custody. He had also sustained injuries during the incident. Greek media reported that Sandeep was remanded in custody on November 9. During questioning, he reportedly told authorities that his nephews had behaved disrespectfully towards him. The victims’ family, however, has questioned the circumstances leading up to the attack. Boota Singh alleged that Sandeep had also recorded a video of the incident and said the family suspected that others could have been involved. They have appealed to the Punjab and Union governments to intervene and coordinate with Greek authorities to ensure a comprehensive investigation and bring all those responsible to justice. The deaths have left the family devastated, particularly because the brothers had gone abroad with the hope of improving their financial circumstances, said village sarpanch Charan Singh Sanghera.

headline: Haryana installs 802 boundary pillars along UP border, accelerates digital land reforms: Official
content: Haryana has intensified efforts to strengthen interstate boundary demarcation and modernise revenue administration, with 802 pillars installed along its Uttar Pradesh border and 2,287 paperless land demarcation reports accepted across the state, an official said on Saturday.Financial Commissioner Revenue and Additional Chief Secretary, Sumita Misra, while reviewing the progress of key revenue initiatives at a meeting with Deputy Commissioners and District Revenue Officers, directed district administrations to accelerate pending work, strengthen field-level monitoring and ensure time-bound delivery of revenue services.She emphasised that accurate land records, transparent procedures and prompt resolution of revenue matters were essential for protecting citizens’ property rights and improving public confidence in the administration.Reviewing boundary demarcation progress along the Haryana-Uttar Pradesh border, Misra said 802 of the 1,221 boundary pillars identified by the Survey of India had been installed across five districts.According to the progress report dated November 13, Sonepat has installed 157 of its 173 identified pillars, Faridabad 145 of 159, Palwal 194 of 385, Karnal 181 of 302 and Panipat 125 of 202, an official statement said here on Saturday.Misra called for special attention to Palwal district, where a substantial number of pillars are yet to be erected.She directed the concerned officers to intensify efforts to complete the remaining boundary pillar installation work and ensure that adequate additional manpower is deployed wherever required.She said the district administration must coordinate with the executing agencies to remove operational bottlenecks and expedite the work.Misra said that 2,287 paperless land demarcation reports had been accepted across Haryana as of November 17. Significantly, 143 reports were processed in just 13 days, reflecting progress in the adoption of digital procedures for land demarcation.She directed district revenue officers and Kanungos to ensure timely examination of pending reports and strengthen monitoring at the field level.Misra said that paperless demarcation would help bring greater transparency, accuracy and accountability to land-related processes while making services more convenient for citizens.She appreciated Sirsa district for its comprehensive efforts in revenue administration and the progress made across various revenue-related activities.She said that a systematic approach, effective coordination and regular monitoring at the district level were important for achieving better outcomes.Misra said that revenue administration reforms must translate into tangible improvements in the everyday experience of citizens.She called upon all Deputy Commissioners and revenue officers to maintain close supervision of ongoing initiatives and ensure accountability at every level.

headline: PM inaugurates, lays foundation stones for, and dedicates to the nation development projects worth around Rs. 34,470 crore in Vaishali, Bihar
content: We are building a Bihar that is stronger, more prosperous and full of opportunities: PM Built across Maa Ganga, the six-lane Dargah-Bidupur cable bridge has been dedicated to the people; As a tribute to respected Nitish Ji, this modern bridge has been named ‘Nitish Setu’: PM We have prioritized enhancing the ease of living for crores of poor citizens and providing them with essential amenities: PM Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today inaugurated, laid the foundation stones for, and dedicated to the nation development projects worth around Rs. 34,470 crore in Vaishali, Bihar. Addressing the gathering on the occasion, the Prime Minister noted that the great festival of public faith, Chhath, has just concluded, during which mothers and sisters observed the arduous Nirjala fast to pray for the welfare of their families, society, and the world. “Now, with the blessings of Chhathi Maiya, we are celebrating the festival of development here,” remarked Shri Modi. Emphasizing that Bihar’s development journey has advanced with the mantra of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’ by turning the strength of democracy into a medium for public welfare, the Prime Minister noted that Vaishali, the great land of democracy, was fittingly chosen to mark the completion of one year of the government’s current term. Bowing to the soil of Vaishali and Bihar, he congratulated everyone involved in the milestone. Recalling how Bihar chose a new path of hope and trust nearly three decades ago, transitioning to a new assurance of good governance under respected Nitish Kumar’s long tenure as Chief Minister, which is now being carried forward by Samrat Choudhary with his blessings, the Prime Minister highlighted the inauguration and foundation stone laying of development projects worth thousands of crores, including the dedication of the six-lane Dargah-Bidupur cable bridge over Mother Ganga named ‘Nitish Setu’ in honor of Nitish Kumar. Pointing out that the bridge reduces distance and difficulties between Patna and Vaishali while making it easier to transport crops, fruits, vegetables, milk, and curd to major markets, he underlined its social impact. “The youth here will have easier access to education, and the elderly to healthcare,” noted Shri Modi.

headline: Illicit alcohol kills 11, poisons 180 in northeast India’s Manipur state
content: At least 11 people have died after drinking what authorities suspect was spurious alcohol in northeast India’s Manipur state, prompting an investigation. More than 180 people, who were believed to have consumed toxic liquor, had been admitted to hospitals in Manipur as of Friday. According to local media, officials have advised locals who have drunk alcohol from Sugnu town in Manipur in the past week to seek medical evaluation. Meanwhile, the deputy police commissioner has advised people not to drink alcohol of unknown origin. “Over 180 patients have been admitted in the two hospitals so far, while the death toll has reached 11 in the last 48 hours,” Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh said in a statement on Friday. Illicit alcohol is a lucrative industry in India, attracting customers who are too poor to afford licensed brands. Vendors regularly use chemicals to increase the potency of their alcohol. Methanol is one of the substances used and can be fatal in doses as low as 60ml. Battery acid has also been found in unregulated alcohol in India.

headline: He allegedly took a Rs 10 lakh bribe. Then CBI found items worth crores at his home
content: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has allegedly recovered cash, foreign currency, gold and silver, collectively worth approximately Rs 1.86 crore, during searches at the residential premises of a Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) employee posted in Haryana. The items were allegedly recovered from the Panchkula residence of Luvkush Kumar, a CGST superintendent arrested in a bribery case on November 19. The CBI had registered a case against Kumar following a complaint alleging that he had demanded a bribe from a private firm partner in exchange for extending undue favours in GST proceedings against the firm, including not imposing heavy penalties and issuing further demand notices. Reduced bribe amount: CBI According to the CBI, Kumar had initially demanded a bribe of Rs 50 lakh, which was subsequently reduced to Rs 20 lakh, with Rs 10 lakh to be paid as the first instalment. During verification, the bribe demand was prima facie substantiated, investigators said. The CBI laid a trap at Panchkula on November 19, during which Kumar was allegedly caught red-handed while accepting Rs 10 lakh from the complainant. During subsequent searches conducted at his residential premises, the CBI said it recovered Indian currency worth Rs 24.29 lakh and foreign currency equivalent to approximately Rs 15.65 lakh. Gold jewellery, gold bullion and silver collectively valued at approximately Rs 1.46 crore were also seized, taking the total value of the recoveries to around Rs 1.86 crore. Property, investment documents under scanner The searches also led to the recovery of documents relating to six bank accounts, investment portfolios, a life insurance policy and multiple immovable properties. Documents concerning a vehicle and financial transactions of the accused and his family members were also found, the CBI said. The central agency is examining the documents to ascertain the assets, investments and financial transactions of the accused and his family members. Further investigation is underway, the CBI said on Saturday.

headline: Last rites of UP CM Yogi Adityanath’s mother held in Haridwar
content: The last rites of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s mother were held at the Chandi Ghat in Haridwar on Saturday.Adityanath paid floral tributes to his mother’s remains before they were taken to the funeral pyre. His younger brother then consigned it to flames.Adityanath’s mother, Savitri Devi, passed away at her native village in Uttarakhand on Friday morning at the age of 91.On Saturday morning, the UP chief minister and his family took his mother’s remains from her ancestral home in Panchur village in Pauri Garhwal district for the funeral at Chandi Ghat cremation ground in Haridwar.At the ghat, Adityanath looked emotional as he stood by his mother’s remains. After paying respect to his mother at their home, Adityanath shared on X, “There is no shade like a mother’s, no refuge like a mother’s. There is no protection like a mother’s, no love like a mother’s.”नास्ति मातृसमा छाया नास्ति मातृसमा गतिः।नास्ति मातृसमं त्राणं नास्ति मातृसमा प्रिया॥🙏 https://t.co/usBszRtWjQ— Yogi Adityanath (@myogiadityanath) November 21, 2026A large crowd has gathered at the Namami Gange Ghat, also known as Chandi Ghat, to pay their respects. Tight security arrangements are in place.Prominent politicians, ministers, party officials from both Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand, including Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, as well as seers and representatives from various social organisations were present at the ghat.Senior UP ministers like Sanjay Nishad and many senior bureaucrats were also spotted at the place.Top leaders including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, along with many chief ministers, top opposition leaders like Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and veteran leader Azam Khan, BSP chief Mayawati, and Congress leaders like UPCC chief Aradhana Misra Mona have mourned the demise of Adityanath’s mother.Uttar Pradesh Cabinet Minister Swatantra Dev Singh and Minister of State Kunwar Brijesh Rawat also expressed their condolences and paid tribute to Adityanath’s mother.Several saints, including yoga guru Baba Ramdev, Mishri Math Peethadhishwar Karoli Shankar and Akhada Parishad president Mahant Ravindra Puri, also paid their respects, describing her passing as an irreparable loss.

headline: Bikaner railway division records 12% revenue growth, earns Rs 954 crore till October
content: The Bikaner railway division of the North Western Railways has grossed 11.96 per cent increase in its total revenue during the current financial year, earning Rs 954.17 crore up to October against Rs 852.27 crore during the corresponding period last year.An official of the Bikaner Railway Division informed that the growth has been recorded across passenger fares, freight traffic and other revenue sources.The passenger ticket sales showed a rise of nearly 13 per cent. The officials claimed that the improvement in the passenger facilities and coordinated efforts by various departments are contributing factors for this growth.Haryana’s Hisar, Bhiwani, Sirsa, Charkhi Dadri and Mahendergarh rail sections are part of the Bikaner Division of NWR.Giving a breakup of the earnings, the officials informed that the revenue from the sale of reserved and unreserved tickets stood at Rs 395.81 crore during April-October 2026, compared with Rs 350.31 crore, an increase of 12.99 per cent.Freight revenue registered growth of 7.59 per cent, from Rs 322.02 crore to Rs 346.46 crore. The division also recorded a significant 22.52 per cent growth in miscellaneous earnings, which went up from Rs 138.92 crore to Rs 170.20 crore.The railway officials said that the number of passengers travelling in the trains too has shown upward trend as a total of 298.77 lakh passengers travelled on the division's network up to October this year, as compared to 293.34 lakh during the corresponding period last year.The division which is led by Divisional Railway Manager Gaurav Govil has also recorded 94.24 per cent punctuality of mail and express trains in October.

headline: BJP turns women outreach into electoral strategy, deploys 403 workers across UP
content: Bharatiya Janata Party's decision to deploy 403 women expansion workers, one in every Assembly constituency, marks an attempt to turn its women-centric governance narrative into a sustained electoral network ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.The workers, drawn from eight states, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Bihar, Jharkhand, Rajasthan and Maharashtra, were assigned their constituencies at a Mahila Morcha meeting in Lucknow on Friday.They will undertake door-to-door outreach, establish direct contact with women voters and communicate the Centre's and state government's welfare initiatives.The strategy builds on a political calculation Prime Minister Narendra Modi has repeatedly articulated. In November 2020, he described women as the BJP's 'silent voters', crediting them with strengthening the party's electoral prospects. In a 2024 interview, he reiterated that women's empowerment was his commitment, citing initiatives intended to expand their opportunities beyond traditional roles.Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has similarly made women's safety, dignity and self-reliance central to his government's political messaging. In October, he described these as the foundations of an empowered society, citing schemes covering girls' education, maternal assistance, cooking fuel and social security.At Friday's meeting, BJP national general secretary and UP in-charge Vinod Tawde, co-incharge Rajya Sabha MP Medha Kulkarni asked the women functionaries to accelerate public contact across all 403 constituencies and explain the government's welfare measures. State president Pankaj Chaudhary described the coming election as a test of organisational strength and public trust.Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya called women party workers the BJP's 'star campaigners', while Brajesh Pathak asked them to communicate the government's claims on women's safety.The significance of the exercise goes beyond adding another campaign layer. By sending women workers into households well before polling, the BJP is seeking to establish a constituency-level feedback and communication network rather than depend solely on rallies and election-time messaging.

headline: Congress beats BJP in Rajasthan panchayat, zila parishad polls
content: The Congress on Friday registered a comprehensive win against the ruling BJP in Rajasthan's panchayat samiti and zila parishad elections.It won 3,701 panchayat samiti seats against the BJP's 2,181 and 599 zila parishad seats against the ruling party's 301, according to State Election Commission (SEC) data.The results across the state's rural heartland are significant as these come just two months after the BJP had swept urban local body polls in the state.These elections followed a recent administrative revamp in Rajasthan where zila parishads were increased from 33 to 41 and panchayat samitis from 352 to 457.The results, seen as a shot in the arm for the Congress, showed the ruling party ahead in just four of Rajasthan's 37 districts — Ajmer, Balotra, Salumber and Udaipur.Rajasthan BJP president Madan Rathore accepted the defeat as people's mandate and said the BJP would review the results.Nagaur MP Hanuman Beniwal-led Rashtriya Loktantrik Party (RLP) bagged 496 seats, Bharat Adivasi Party (BAP) 276, BSP 60, CPM 50 and AAP two, while Independents secured 627 seats. In the Zila Parishad elections, the RLP won 37 seats, BAP 22, BSP and CPI(M) six each, and Independents 10.In Jaipur, the Congress won 216 panchayat samiti seats and the BJP 87.In Jodhpur, the Congress got 195 against the BJP's 81. The Congress got 165 seats against the BJP's 111 in Bhilwara, 155 against 65 in Bikaner, 135 against 59 in Dausa and 179 against 87 in Sikar.In CM Bhajan Lal Sharma's native district of Bharatpur, the Congress bagged 46 panchayat samiti seats against the BJP's 32.The BJP was ahead of the Congress in Ajmer, winning 83 panchayat samiti seats against 80, Balotra (63 against 57), Salumber (38 against 32) and Udaipur (146 against 137).

headline: After Patiala mishap, Ludhiana’s 5 unsafe flyovers under scanner
content: The collapse of a bridge on a National Highway in Patiala has once again raised serious questions about the safety of ageing bridges and flyovers across Punjab. In Ludhiana, concerns are mounting over five major flyovers that were flagged for urgent repairs more than two years ago, but continue to await remedial action by NHAI despite repeated warnings from technical experts.The structures identified as requiring immediate intervention include the ISBT flyover, Dholewal flyover, Gill Chowk flyover, Pratap Nagar Chowk flyover and Dugri flyover. According to inspection reports, damaged and non-functional bearings in these structures pose a potential risk to their long-term stability, exposing thousands of daily commuters to safety hazards.Among them, the condition of the Dholewal flyover is considered particularly alarming. Constructed in 1988, the bridge is now over 38 years old. Technical experts had noted that several of its bearings had become severely rusted and required immediate replacement to prevent deterioration of the structure.The concerns date back to July 8, 2024, when Feedback Infra, appointed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) as the authority’s engineer for overseeing the elevated road project from Samrala Chowk to the municipal limits, submitted a detailed inspection report highlighting serious defects in the bearings of all five flyovers. The report recommended urgent replacement of the damaged components and suggested a comprehensive investigation by a specialised agency such as the Central Road Research Institute (CRRI).The issue was again brought to the NHAI’s attention through a reminder letter dated June 12, 2025. The communication specifically mentioned crushed bearings and cracks in the pedestal of the pier cap at the ISBT flyover. Experts warned that damaged bearings impair the load-transfer mechanism of a bridge, increasing the risk of structural instability if left unattended.According to the technical assessment, the solid slab bearings at the Dholewal and ISBT flyovers, as well as the PSC girder and RCC slab bearings at Pratap Nagar Chowk, Gill Chowk and Dugri, were not functioning properly and required replacement.The urgency of these warnings has assumed greater significance after the collapse of a 60-metre-long bridge over the Bhakra Main Line Canal near Pasiana village on the Patiala-Sangrur highway on November 19. Officials say logistical hurdles have delayed the inspection and repair process in Ludhiana.NHAI Project Director Priyanka Meena said the authority was keen to undertake a detailed structural examination of the flyovers but was facing difficulties due to commercial establishments operating beneath them.“There are multiple shops under these bridges. We have asked the Municipal Corporation to cooperate and get these shops vacated temporarily so that inspections can be carried out. We also wrote to the Chief Secretary several months ago, but no action has been taken so far,” she said.Responding to the issue, Deputy Commissioner Himanshu Aggarwal said he was not aware of the matter and would seek a report from the NHAI. “The matter was not under my knowledge. I will ask the NHAI authorities to submit a compliance report and, if required, conduct a fresh safety audit and furnish an action-taken report,” he said.

headline: District admn harassing candidates in civic body repolls: Opposition leader
content: The Punjab BJP Mahila Morcha state president Jai Inder Kaur on Friday accused the Patiala district administration of deliberately delaying the scrutiny of nomination papers and harassing opposition candidates during the Municipal Corporation elections.Interacting with mediapersons, Jai Inder Kaur alleged that the administration was acting under pressure from the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and adopting high-handed tactics against opposition candidates. She asserted that the BJP would not tolerate such conduct under any circumstances.She pointed out that fresh elections were being conducted in 30 wards of the MC on the directions of the Supreme Court, alleging that earlier irregularities and high-handedness by the state government had necessitated the court's intervention."It is shocking that the Aam Aadmi Party does not even fear the Supreme Court," she remarked.Kaur said the BJP had lodged a formal complaint against the alleged high-handedness of the administration with the court-appointed monitoring committee. Following the complaint, observers were sent to the spot, after which opposition candidates were finally allowed to enter the premises, she added.It may be mentioned that the scrutiny of nomination papers was delayed by about three hours by the Returning Officer Inderpal Singh and he was also not allowing the candidates to enter the scrutiny room. The scrutiny of nomination papers must be conducted in the presence of the candidates as per the election rules.Questioning the ruling party's alleged reluctance to allow the opposition candidates to participate freely in the election process, Jai Inder Kaur warned that the BJP would strongly oppose any attempt to intimidate candidates.She further stated that if the government failed to abandon its alleged coercive approach, the BJP would not hesitate to approach the court again to seek intervention.The State Election Commission has transferred the Patiala DSP (city) Sanjeev Singla with immediate effect and posted a 2020-batch PPS officer Guriqbal Singh on this post for smooth conduct of the MC re-elections. The state government gave a panel of three officials out of which Guriqbal Singh's name was selected by the election panel.

headline: Patiala: Woman denied bail in housing scheme scam
content: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has dismissed the anticipatory bail petition of the wife of the main accused in the alleged Rs 7-crore Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) scam involving the Patiala Municipal Corporation.Justice Manisha Batra rejected the pre-arrest bail plea, observing that the allegations against the petitioner were serious and that her custodial interrogation was necessary for a thorough investigation into the alleged misappropriation of public funds.According to the details available, a sum of Rs 3,90,49,375 meant for beneficiaries under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana was allegedly transferred through multiple transactions into a joint bank account of the petitioner and her husband, Amandeep Singh, as well as into the account of her mother-in-law.The FIR in this regard was registered under Sections 316(5), 318(4), 336(2), 336(3), 338 and 340(2) read with Sections 61(2) and 3(5) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, on July 16, 2026, at the Civil Lines police station, Patiala, on the complaint of Surjit Singh Cheema, Secretary of the civic body.The complaint alleged that an instalment of Rs 1.5 lakh meant for a beneficiary, Satta, son of Harphool, of Alipur Araian village, was diverted into another account by forging the signatures of officials on the relevant bills and office orders.The investigation subsequently revealed the alleged involvement of Amandeep Singh, an employee of the MC Accounts Branch, who was arrested in the case.The petitioner Gurvinder Kaur was later nominated as an accused along with her husband and other persons during the course of investigations by the local police.Opposing the bail plea, the counsel for the state submitted that the petitioner and her husband had allegedly acquired valuable immovable properties, including a 500-square-yard plot and a commercial paying-guest accommodation, using the misappropriated funds. The bills relating to the purchase of gold jewellery had also been seized during the investigation.The petitioner’s counsel argued that she had been falsely implicated, was not an MC employee and had no role in preparing or processing the forged documents. It was further contended that merely because money had been transferred into a joint bank account, she could not be held responsible for cheating or forgery. Her counsel also submitted that she had joined the investigation and that her custodial interrogation was not required by the police.However, the state maintained that her interrogation was necessary to establish the source of funds used to acquire properties and gold ornaments and to ascertain the circumstances and manner in which the alleged offences were committed by her husband and family members.Her mother-in-law Amarjit Kaur’s anticipatory bail had also been previously dismissed by the Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Patiala, on August 27 this year.Dismissing the petition, Justice Batra observed that the case was at a nascent stage and that denying custodial interrogation could leave significant gaps in the investigation. The court held that no exceptional or extraordinary circumstances had been made out for granting anticipatory bail.

headline: Footballers Union FIFPRO Slams Bayern Munich Over Comments On Jamal Musiala's Health Condition
content: The global professional footballers union, FIFPRO, has raised serious concerns about German club FC Bayern Munich’s recent statements on its attacking midfielder Jamal Musiala, who has a neurological condition. It came to light when he collapsed twice on the pitch during pre-season friendlies in August 2026. Since then, Musiala’s contract has become the biggest subject of debate around Bayern. When fit, the 23-year-old is one of the best midfielders in the world, full of creative spark and dribbling energy. However, Bayern officials haven’t missed mentioning his contract, valid until June 30, 2030, after an extension last year, is worth close to €25 million (about Rs. 253 crore) a year. Club’s honorary president Uli Hoeneß sparked the controversy by calling the situation a ‘dilemma,’ revealing Musiala’s illness can only be managed with medication and questioning whether his current output justifies his agreed salary. CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen backed Hoeneß’s remarks as ‘sensitive,’ citing the board’s financial responsibility to the club while noting Musiala needs time. Former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge went further, stating Musiala will struggle to regain his past level, claiming no club would buy him, and refusing to rule out negotiating a pay cut. “FIFPRO is deeply concerned by the repeated public statements from FC Bayern Munich’s leadership calling into question the contract of Jamal Musiala as he returns from injury,” the global body said in a statement. “… In FIFPRO’s view, this is a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern’s standing should know better.” “Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala. Across professional football, uncertainty about a player’s future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury. Making Musiala’s health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives,” it added. The world body, comprising of over 77,000 footballers, reminded Bayern to respect the contract it has signed with Musiala as an important principle of the game, saying injuries were no grounds to reopen the negotiations. “FIFPRO stands with Jamal Musiala and with all players who honour their commitments. We expect their employers to do the same.” Bayern’s record revenues The FIFPRO statement came the same day when Bayern Munich announced record revenues of $1.083 billion (approx ₹10,037.30 crore) for the 2025-26 season at their annual general meeting on Saturday, while also becoming the first football club to surpass 500,000 members. The German giants said their membership had doubled over the past 12 years, rising from 250,000 in 2014.

headline: IShowSpeed Completes GTA VI In 52-Hour Marathon With No Sleep; Doctor Explains Health Risks
content: Popular American YouTuber and livestreamer IShowSpeed has turned his Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) playthrough into an endurance test, reportedly spending 40 consecutive hours playing the highly anticipated video game without sleep. The streamer, whose real name is Darren Watkins Jr., reached approximately 82% story completion during the marathon, drawing attention from gaming fans and raising concerns about the health risks of prolonged sleep deprivation. While viewers followed his progress online, doctors have warned that staying awake for extended periods can affect brain function, concentration, memory and even cardiovascular health. Here is what happened during IShowSpeed’s GTA VI livestream and what medical experts say about the dangers of going without sleep. IShowSpeed plays GTA VI for 40 hours without sleep According to NDTV Profit, IShowSpeed began streaming GTA VI on YouTube and Twitch at 9 pm ET on November 18, three hours before the game became available in the United States. What began as a planned gaming session turned into a marathon. By the 40-hour mark, IShowSpeed had reportedly completed around 81–82% of the game’s main story. His in-game progress screen showed the ‘Dirty Work’ mission, and he told viewers that he might need another 12 hours or so to reach the ending. Interestingly, the streamer had previously said that he did not intend to rush through the game. During a November 16 livestream, he had spoken about playing for around 10 to 12 hours a day instead of attempting a continuous marathon. However, the storyline kept him engaged, and he continued playing despite viewers encouraging him to take a break. IShowSpeed’s GTA VI livestream attracts millions of views The marathon also drew considerable attention online. NDTV Profit reported that his first GTA VI broadcast lasted 23 hours and 45 minutes and reached a peak of 392,500 concurrent viewers on YouTube. The recording subsequently crossed 60 million views, according to the report. His playthrough became one of the most talked-about livestreams surrounding the game’s launch, with clips of his progress and reactions circulating across social media. What happens to your body when you stay awake for 40 hours? Prolonged sleep deprivation can affect several functions that the brain and body rely on. Dr Shekhar Patil, Senior Consultant, Adult and Paediatric Neurology, Apollo Hospitals Navi Mumbai, explains that sleep is essential for processing information, consolidating memories and regulating attention and mood. It also supports normal hormonal, metabolic and cardiovascular functions. According to Dr Patil, the effects of sleep deprivation begin well before a person has been awake for two days. Attention, reaction time and judgement can become impaired after a full night without sleep. As wakefulness continues, the risk of microsleeps increases. These are brief, involuntary episodes during which the brain momentarily falls asleep, potentially leaving a person unaware of their surroundings. Dr Patil adds that by around 48 hours without sleep, some people may experience visual distortions, confusion and, in more severe cases, hallucinations. Caffeine and energy drinks may temporarily make someone feel more alert, but they cannot replace the restorative functions of sleep. Don’t trade prolonged gaming for sleep Dr Charu Goel Sachdeva, Chairman and Consultant, Internal Medicine, Manipal Hospital Dwarka, New Delhi, says that staying awake continuously for 52 hours can have serious consequences for the body and brain. She explains that prolonged sleep deprivation can affect concentration, memory, decision-making and reaction time. It may also disturb hormonal balance, increase stress hormone levels, affect blood sugar regulation and place additional strain on the cardiovascular system. Sleep loss can also weaken immune responses and affect emotional well-being. Dr Sachdeva points out that one of the biggest concerns is that people may not recognise how impaired they have become. Even if someone feels capable of continuing an activity, their brain and body may already be functioning below their normal capacity. How much sleep do adults need? Both doctors emphasise that sleep should not be sacrificed for gaming or other prolonged activities. Adults should generally aim for seven to nine hours of sleep every night. Dr Patil advises anyone who has stayed awake for an extreme period to stop gaming, get proper rest and avoid driving or operating machinery until fully alert. Persistent confusion, hallucinations, chest pain or other worrying symptoms require medical attention. While IShowSpeed’s GTA VI marathon has captured the attention of gaming fans, doctors stress that such prolonged periods without sleep should not be treated as a challenge to imitate.

headline: 24 Mutations, 18 Countries: WHO Monitors New COVID Variant PJ.2.1
content: A new COVID-19 variant is drawing attention after the World Health Organization (WHO) classified PJ.2.1 as a Variant Under Monitoring (VUM), following its detection across 18 countries. The lineage has been gaining ground in several regions, particularly in North America, and scientists are examining its genetic changes and how effectively it interacts with human cells. What has caught attention is the number of mutations it carries: PJ.2.1 has 24 amino-acid differences in its spike protein alone compared with its parent lineage. Since the spike protein is the part of the virus that helps it attach to and enter human cells, such changes warrant scientific scrutiny. But a highly mutated virus does not automatically mean a more dangerous one. In its initial risk evaluation published on November 19, 2026, the WHO assessed the additional global public-health risk posed by PJ.2.1 as low, although it emphasised that confidence in the assessment remains low and more evidence is needed. So, what do we know about this new variant, how quickly is it spreading, and should people in India be concerned? What is COVID variant PJ.2.1? PJ.2.1 is a descendant of the JN.1 family of Omicron variants. It evolved from the lineage MC.10.1.7, with the earliest available sequence dating to May 25, 2026. Scientists describe it as a ‘saltation’ variant—a lineage that appears to have accumulated a substantial number of genetic changes over a relatively short evolutionary period. The 24 amino-acid differences in its spike protein have prompted researchers to investigate whether these changes could affect how it binds to human cells, spreads or interacts with existing immunity. The WHO’s classification as a Variant Under Monitoring means that the lineage has characteristics or epidemiological signals that merit closer observation. It is not the same as declaring it a Variant of Concern, nor does the designation indicate that it is causing a more severe disease outbreak. PJ.2.1 has been detected in 18 countries: How fast is it spreading? According to the WHO’s data, 722 sequences of PJ.2.1 had been submitted to GISAID from 18 countries as of November 8, 2026. Its share of available global COVID-19 sequences increased from 1% in epidemiological week 33 to 11.6% in week 41. The increase was particularly noticeable in the Americas, where its proportion rose to 16.6% in week 41. Canada reported that PJ.2.1 accounted for 25.7% of available sequences in the same week, while the US reported 13.8%. The variant has also been detected in Europe and the Western Pacific, with its proportion among available sequences rising in these regions as well. However, the WHO cautions that these numbers must be interpreted carefully. Countries differ in how extensively they sequence COVID-19 samples, and the available data may be affected by reporting delays and uneven sampling. An increase in the proportion of sequences does not, by itself, establish exactly how much more transmissible the variant is. Why are scientists watching its 24 mutations? The spike protein plays an important role in how SARS-CoV-2 attaches to human cells. PJ.2.1’s genetic changes have therefore prompted laboratory studies examining its interaction with the ACE2 receptor, which the virus uses to enter cells. Laboratory evidence reviewed by the WHO indicates that PJ.2.1 has greater human ACE2-binding capability than some contemporary variants, including XFG and NB.1.8.1. This could potentially contribute to its observed growth. However, stronger receptor binding in laboratory experiments is not the same as proof that a virus spreads more easily between people in real-world conditions. Scientists still need epidemiological evidence to establish how much of its growth is attributable to its biological characteristics versus differences in immunity, population behaviour or surveillance. The number of mutations alone is also not a reliable measure of a variant’s severity. Researchers need to understand what those changes actually do. Can PJ.2.1 evade immunity from vaccines or previous infections? This is one of the more reassuring findings so far. The WHO’s assessment found that available laboratory evidence did not demonstrate substantial additional antibody escape by PJ.2.1 compared with the contemporary variants tested. Researchers also found that serum from recipients of LP.8.1- and XFG-adapted vaccines could neutralise the variant in laboratory assays. In one study involving 36 recipients of an LP.8.1-adapted vaccine, PJ.2.1 did not show greater antibody evasion than most of the variants examined. Another study involving 22 participants found that neutralising antibody titres against PJ.2.1 increased following an XFG-adapted mRNA vaccine. These results suggest that vaccine-induced antibodies retain activity against PJ.2.1. However, laboratory neutralisation results should not be confused with real-world vaccine effectiveness. Researchers have not yet established how effectively current vaccines prevent infection specifically caused by PJ.2.1 or how much protection they provide against severe disease from this lineage. Does the new variant cause more severe COVID-19? At present, there is no evidence establishing that PJ.2.1 causes more severe disease than other circulating variants. The WHO has noted that comparative clinical data remain insufficient to determine whether infections caused by this lineage are associated with higher rates of hospitalisation, oxygen requirement, intensive-care admission or death. This is an important distinction. A variant may become more prevalent without necessarily causing more severe illness. Its overall public-health impact depends on several factors, including transmissibility, the population’s existing immunity, the number of infections it causes and the proportion of people who develop severe complications. For now, the severity question remains unanswered—not because the variant has been shown to be more dangerous, but because there is not enough clinical evidence yet. What are the symptoms of PJ.2.1? There is currently no established symptom profile that distinguishes PJ.2.1 from other COVID-19 variants. Symptoms may include: Fever or chills Sore throat Cough Runny or blocked nose Headache Fatigue Muscle aches These symptoms overlap considerably with common colds, influenza and other respiratory infections. Symptoms alone cannot confirm which virus or COVID-19 lineage is responsible. A regular COVID-19 test can identify an infection, while identifying the specific variant generally requires genomic sequencing. Is PJ.2.1 detected in India? The WHO’s November 19 risk assessment documented sequences from 18 countries, with the detections concentrated particularly in Canada and the United States. India was not listed among the countries reporting sequences in the assessment’s country-level data. However, this should not be interpreted as a guarantee that the variant is absent from India. Genomic surveillance and sequencing coverage are not uniform across countries, and the global data may change as additional samples are reported. For India, the important development to watch is whether genomic surveillance identifies the lineage locally and whether it begins increasing in proportion among samples. At present, the WHO’s global assessment does not indicate that PJ.2.1 requires special restrictions or a change in everyday public-health measures. Should you worry about PJ.2.1? The short answer is: there is no reason to panic, but it is worth staying informed. The WHO currently assesses the additional global risk from PJ.2.1 as low, with low confidence. Its increasing presence in several countries, genetic changes and stronger ACE2-binding capability are reasons for continued surveillance, but researchers have not established that it causes more severe illness or substantial additional immune escape. Older adults, people with weakened immune systems and individuals with underlying health conditions should continue to take respiratory infections seriously. Staying up to date with vaccination as advised by a healthcare professional, improving ventilation, practising hand hygiene and avoiding close contact with others when ill remain sensible precautions. If you develop respiratory symptoms, particularly if you are at higher risk of complications, consider testing and seek medical advice when needed. Breathing difficulty, chest pain, confusion or other serious symptoms warrant prompt medical attention. COVID-19 continues to evolve, and new lineages will emerge. The important thing is to distinguish a variant that scientists are monitoring from one that has demonstrated a significant threat to public health. As of November 19, PJ.2.1 falls into the former category.
