headline: HP Vidhan Sabha backs permanent HC Bench at Dharamshala, Seeks centre’s approval
content: After failing to draw the consensus on announcement and formation of new district among Ministers and Own legislators bow Congress Government in Himachal Pradesh has adopted a new lofty promising a High court Regional Bench at Dharmshala, the move considered an attempt to appease people of Kangra and other nearby districts. Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly has unanimously adopted a resolution seeking the establishment of a permanent bench of the Himachal Pradesh High Court at Dharamshala to improve access to justice for people living in Kangra and other lower districts of the state. The resolution urges the Chief Justice of the Himachal Pradesh High Court and the Governor to hold consultations and forward an immediate, formal and comprehensive proposal to the Government of India for setting up the permanent bench. Highlighting the geographical difficulties faced by litigants, advocates and the general public from Kangra and other lower Himachal districts, the resolution observed that travelling to the High Court’s principal seat in Shimla involves considerable distance, difficult terrain and substantial expenditure. These factors often cause hardship, unnecessary delays and financial burdens for people seeking judicial remedies. It argued that a dedicated permanent bench at Dharamshala would ensure accessible, affordable and timely justice to a large section of the state’s population, particularly those residing in Kangra and adjoining districts. Referring to the constitutional and statutory provisions, the resolution cited Article 214 of the Constitution, which provides for a High Court for each state, and Section 51(2) of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956. The latter empowers the President of India, after consultation with the Governor and the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court, to establish a permanent bench at a place other than the principal seat of the High Court.

headline: Himachal Assembly unanimously approves permanent High Court bench in Dharamshala
content: The Himachal Pradesh Assembly has unanimously passed a resolution to establish a permanent High Court bench in Dharamshala, Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu announced on Saturday. He expressed hope that the move would enhance access to justice for residents of Kangra and other remote regions. Speaking at a press conference following the conclusion of the Assembly’s winter session, Sukhu stated that the state government intends to liaise with the Himachal Pradesh High Court and relevant authorities to advance the proposal. The Chief Minister highlighted the difficulties faced by people from distant areas such as Chamba in travelling to Shimla for court proceedings, emphasising that a Dharamshala bench would offer greater convenience. He confirmed that the resolution had been approved by the Assembly and added that he plans to raise the issue with the Chief Justice of India during the latter’s upcoming visit to Himachal Pradesh. Sukhu explained that establishing a bench in Dharamshala would assist litigants from remote areas without significantly impacting the functionality of the High Court in Shimla. The proposal targets improved judicial access for residents in lower Himachal, who currently face challenges attending court hearings over long distances. “We want a bench of the High Court to be established here so that the cases of people from remote areas like Chamba can be heard locally. We have passed a resolution regarding this. The Chief Justice of India is visiting tomorrow, and I will discuss this matter with him so that it receives due consideration. This will not adversely affect Shimla, but a bench should be present here,” he said.

headline: Dharamshala to Get Permanent High Court Bench; Himachal Assembly Passes Resolution Unanimously
content: Dharamshala: The Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly has unanimously passed a resolution seeking the establishment of a permanent bench of the Himachal Pradesh High Court at Dharamshala, paving the way for improved access to justice for people living in Kangra and other districts of lower Himachal. Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu presented the resolution in the House, emphasising that residents of Kangra and neighbouring districts face considerable difficulties in accessing justice due to the geographical distance from the High Court’s principal seat in Shimla. The resolution highlights that difficult terrain, long travel distances and inadequate connectivity in certain areas impose an additional financial burden on litigants, besides causing inconvenience and delays in attending court proceedings. A permanent bench at Dharamshala would help reduce these difficulties and make justice more accessible, affordable and convenient for people in the lower regions of the state. The House also observed that a substantial number of pending cases originate from Kangra and other adjoining districts, strengthening the need for a dedicated High Court bench in Dharamshala. Referring to Article 214 of the Constitution of India, which provides for a High Court for every state, and Section 51(2) of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, the resolution outlines the legal provisions governing the establishment of a permanent bench. Section 51(2) empowers the President of India to establish a permanent bench at a location other than the principal seat of a High Court, in consultation with the Governor of the state and the Chief Justice of the High Court.

headline: Flavoured Hookah Poses Growing Health Threat; Health Department Seeks Ban
content: Shimla: Even as Himachal Pradesh intensifies its ‘Chitta-Free Himachal’ campaign against drug abuse, another emerging health concern is gaining ground across the state, with flavoured hookah smoking posing serious risks to public health, particularly among youngsters and tourists. Unlicensed hookah bars are reportedly operating in major tourist destinations, including Shimla, Solan, Dharamshala and Manali, where hundreds of locals and visitors consume flavoured hookah products daily under the guise of recreation. Despite growing concerns over their health implications, these establishments continue to operate. The Health Department has reportedly submitted a proposal to the state government seeking a ban on such establishments and their closure. However, no concrete action has been taken so far. The concern assumes significance as 11 states and Union Territories, including Punjab and Chandigarh, have reportedly imposed restrictions or bans on hookah bars. Health experts warn that flavoured hookah smoke is far from harmless. It contains several toxic substances, including nicotine, carbon monoxide, tar, heavy metals and cancer-causing chemicals. Contrary to popular belief, the water used in hookahs does not effectively filter out these harmful substances. The charcoal used to heat hookah tobacco is another major source of carbon monoxide, which can reduce the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood and cause serious health complications. Regular consumption can lead to nicotine addiction and increase the risk of cancers affecting the lungs, mouth and oesophagus. It is also associated with reduced lung function, cardiovascular diseases and reproductive health problems. Another concern is the risk of infections arising from the shared use of hookah pipes and mouthpieces, particularly in establishments where hygiene standards may not be adequately maintained.

headline: Sukhu opens advanced MRI facility at Tanda GMC
content: Kullu: Himachal Pradesh chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Friday inaugurated a state-of-the-art 3-Tesla MRI machine at Dr Rajendra Prasad Government Medical College, Tanda, in Kangra district. The machine has been installed at a cost of Rs 23.5 crore.Sukhu said the facility marked another step towards developing Tanda medical college into a centre of excellence for advanced diagnosis, treatment, medical education and patient care.This is the institution’s second MRI machine. Its existing 1.5-Tesla machine has been providing diagnostic services to patients. Sukhu said the new 3-Tesla machine would enhance diagnostic capacity by providing high-resolution images with greater anatomical detail, helping doctors diagnose complex medical conditions more accurately.Interacting with faculty and students, the CM said strengthening the health sector remained the state govt’s top priority and several initiatives had been taken to improve healthcare services at medical colleges.He announced that robotic arms would be provided for advanced surgeries and directed the authorities to eliminate waiting periods for diagnostic services such as MRI, CT scans, ultrasound and X-rays. He also announced a 256-slice CT scan machine for the college.Sukhu said promotions in several categories had already been carried out at the college and the remaining cases would be taken up soon. He said 320 postgraduate seats had been added in medical colleges across the state this year, taking the total from 277 to 597.He also appreciated the college doctors for conducting 28 renal transplants.

headline: Himachal to remain dry till Nov 27, temperatures likely to stay above normal
content: Himachal Pradesh is unlikely to get any respite from the dry spell, with the State Meteorological Centre forecasting dry and clear weather conditions across the state till November 27.According to the centre, dry weather will prevail across the state until next week. During this period, maximum temperatures are very likely to remain above normal in many parts, resulting in warmer-than-usual conditions.Maximum temperatures are expected to range between 8°C and 14°C in the higher reaches, 20°C and 26°C in the middle hills, and 26°C and 30°C in the lower hills and plains throughout the week.Similarly, minimum temperatures are also expected to remain above normal in some parts of the state. They are likely to range between 6°C and 12°C in the plains and low hills, 8°C and 14°C in the middle hills, and minus 4°C and 6°C in the higher reaches.Himachal Pradesh has witnessed largely dry weather this month, with the state recording a 73 per cent rainfall deficit. It has received only 3.1 mm of rainfall so far, against the normal of 11.4 mm.Meanwhile, weather conditions remained mostly dry across the state during the past 24 hours, with most areas witnessing cloudy skies.The maximum temperature in Shimla was recorded at 16.2°C, while Dharamshala recorded 20°C. Manali registered 19°C, Mandi 21.8°C, Solan 21.5°C, Nahan 23.8°C, Kalpa 14°C, Bhuntar 19.6°C, Sundernagar 22.7°C, Keylong 11.1°C, Kangra 23.7°C, Kufri 12.9°C and Bilaspur 24°C.The highest maximum temperature in the state was 26°C, recorded in Una, while the lowest minimum temperature was minus 4.2°C, recorded in Tabo in Lahaul and Spiti.

headline: Eight sports events planned under Khelo Himachal drive
content: In an effort to sensitise young people to the harmful effects of drug abuse, particularly the growing menace of chitta, and encourage them to adopt a healthy lifestyle through sports, eight sporting competitions will be organised in the Padhar subdivision of Mandi district under the ‘Khelo Himachal–Chitta Mukt Campaign’.The eight sporting disciplines included in the campaign are cricket, volleyball, badminton, kabaddi, athletics, wrestling, hockey and tug of war. Both male and female players in the 15-to-30 age group will be eligible to participate.The last date for online registration has been extended to November 30, 2026. Interested players can register through the official portal, https://khelohimachal.hp.gov.in. Participants will also be allowed to register for more than one sporting discipline.According to the proposed schedule, the competitions will be organised in two phases. The first phase will be held from December 25 to 27, 2026, while the second phase is scheduled for January 1 to 8, 2027.The venues identified for the competitions include Government Senior Secondary School, Padhar; Government Senior Secondary School, Siyun; Government College, Narla; and Dianapark Cricket Ground.The campaign also offers substantial cash prizes to encourage participation and promote competitive sporting talent. In kabaddi, volleyball and cricket, winners at the subdivision level will receive Rs 51,000, Rs 41,000 and Rs 31,000 for the first, second and third positions, respectively.At the district level, the prize money has been fixed at Rs 2 lakh for the first position, Rs 1.50 lakh for the second and Rs 1 lakh for the third. At the state level, the respective prize amounts will be Rs 31 lakh, Rs 15 lakh and Rs 10 lakh.SDM Surjeet Singh appealed to educational institutions and the concerned government departments to actively participate in the campaign and ensure maximum involvement of young people. He said participants would also be administered a pledge against drug abuse before every sporting competition.

headline: Haryana: Accused wanted in extortion cases arrested
content: Hisar, Nov 21 (PTI) An accused wanted in multiple extortion cases in Haryana was arrested in Hisar after a police encounter, officials said on Saturday. Pradeep was nabbed by the police after a brief exchange of fire, in which the former sustained a gunshot wound to his leg, police said, adding that an illegal .32-bore pistol and one live cartridge were recovered from his possession. According to an official statement, the accused was in Hisar with the intent of committing a crime. Police received a tip-off about his presence in the area and arrived at the scene to apprehend him. The accused opened fire on the police team, prompting the officers to return fire in self-defence. Investigations revealed that Pradeep was wanted in connection with extortion cases in Rohtak and Karnal. In Rohtak, the accused and his accomplice had last month allegedly demanded a ransom of Rs 5 crore from a man who runs a school, threatening to kill him if the demand was not met. When the ransom was not paid, the accused fired shots at the school’s signage on November 9, according to the police. In Karnal too, he made a similar demand from a village sarpanch. Upon the failure to pay the ransom, they fired shots at the village’s entrance signage.

headline: Bengal to partner Haryana for Gita Mahotsav in Kurukshetra
content: Kolkata: Bengal will participate as the partner state in the International Gita Mahotsav 2026, scheduled to be held in Haryana’s Kurukshetra from Dec 5 to 25, chief minister Suvendu Adhikari announced on social media on Saturday.Calling the participation a matter of “immense pride and joy” for Bengal, Adhikari said minister of state Umesh Rai represented the state at a news conference in Kurukshetra on Saturday and discussed preparations with Haryana CM Nayab Singh Saini.Adhikari said Bengal would join hands with the Haryana govt to take the message and ideals of the Bhagavad Gita to a global audience. headline: Banks in Chamba district of Himachal Pradesh achieve 42.77% of annual credit target
content: Banks in Chamba district have disbursed loans worth Rs 932.44 crore up to September 2026, achieving 42.77 per cent of the Annual Credit Plan target of Rs 2,180.06 crore for the 2026-27 financial year.The progress was reviewed at a meeting of the District Level Review Committee (DLRC), chaired by Assistant Commissioner Manmohan Singh here on Saturday.Expressing concern over the district’s credit-deposit (CD) ratio, Singh directed banks, particularly the State Bank of India, Punjab National Bank and Himachal Pradesh State Cooperative Bank, to analyse their performance at the branch level and hold monthly review meetings to improve credit flow. He also stressed the need for the timely disposal of loan applications received under government-sponsored schemes, including the Rural and Urban Livelihood Missions.Highlighting Chamba’s status as an aspirational district, he asked banks to organise awareness camps to improve their performance on key financial inclusion indicators set by NITI Aayog. These include the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), insurance schemes, Atal Pension Yojana, Aadhaar seeding, Kisan Credit Cards and education loans.He called for enrolling more eligible residents under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana, which provides accident insurance at an annual premium of Rs 20. He also urged banks to publicise the Dr YS Parmar Vidyarthi Rin Yojana to help more students avail themselves of education loans.RBI Lead District Officer Ashish Sangra called for balanced lending across all priority sectors and asked banks to include digital literacy in their monthly awareness camps. He also directed bank branches to reactivate dormant Jan Dhan accounts, complete pending C-KYC and Re-KYC formalities, update nominee details in savings accounts and lockers, and open accounts for adults who remain outside the banking network.NABARD District Development Manager Rakesh Kumar stressed the need for accurate classification of agricultural loans to assess the actual flow of credit to the sector.Lead District Manager DC Chauhan asked banks to complete their assigned camps under the nationwide Financial Inclusion Saturation Campaign, being conducted from October 21 to December 31. He also urged them to educate people about measures to prevent digital fraud.

headline: Himachal winter session: Opposition demands action against Negi, stages walkout | Hindustan Times
content: The fifth day of the ongoing winter session of the Himachal Pradesh assembly on Friday began with an uproar over the revenue minister Jagat Singh Negi’s alleged remarks on Operation Sindoor and armed forces, with the Opposition BJP demanding action against the minister.The Opposition legislators had raised the issue on Thursday as well and demanded that the remarks made by the minister, during Wednesday’s proceedings, be expunged from the record.Raising the issue again on Friday in the House, Leader of Opposition (LoP), Jai Ram Thakur said, “We raised the issue yesterday as well and requested that the remarks made by the minister should not be included in the House proceedings. We feel that the government is protecting the minister’s actions. We want the chief minister to take action and remove the minister from the cabinet.”Speaker Kuldeep Singh Pathania said, “I will peruse the record and take a decision accordingly. If there are any derogatory remarks against the defence forces, they will be expunged.”However, Sukhu accused the BJP legislators of spreading lies. He said, “I have listened to the remarks made by the minister, and there is nothing he said against the armed forces. You should not teach us patriotism. The Speaker has said that he will look into the remarks.” Reacting to Sukhu, the LoP said, “We did not expect the CM to defend the remarks made by the minister.”The LoP urged the Speaker to adjourn the House briefly, listen to the recording of the proceedings and then give his ruling. Pathania said he would personally examine the record and make a decision during the day.Appealing to both sides to ensure the smooth functioning of the House, the Speaker pointed out that the discussion on the adjournment motion under Rule 67 had continued for four days, although the provision envisaged its conclusion within a day.Thakur, however, maintained that the seriousness of the issue warranted the Opposition’s intervention. Accusing the CM of shielding his cabinet colleague, he said the Opposition was left with little option when the head of the government himself chose to defend the minister.Amid continued sloganeering and a war of words between the treasury and Opposition benches, BJP legislators eventually staged a walkout from the House.

headline: Third child no bar to maternity leave, rules Himachal HC
content: Shimla: A govt employee cannot be denied maternity leave merely because she has more than two surviving children, Himachal Pradesh high court has ruled, pointing out that the minimum of 12 weeks is available even for the birth of a third child.A division bench comprising Justice Vivek Singh Thakur and Justice Ranjan Sharma passed the order while allowing a petition filed by teacher Raksha Sawarwat, whose request for maternity leave after the birth of her third child was rejected by state govt.Raksha, appointed in 2002, had delivered her third child on July 24, 2017, and applied for maternity leave from Aug 11, 2017. Her request was rejected on the ground that Rule 43(1) of Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972, restricts maternity leave to women employees having fewer than two surviving children. Rejecting state govt’s stand, the bench observed that Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, provides a statutory minimum entitlement that cannot be curtailed by service rules. Section 5(3) of the Act clearly says that a woman having two or more surviving children is entitled to 12 weeks of maternity benefit.The court noted that the Act overrides any ‘inconsistent law or service conditions’. Even where CCS rules do not provide maternity leave for the birth of a third child, a woman cannot be deprived of the minimum benefit guaranteed under the Act.The high court also referred to Articles 21 and 42 of the Constitution, observing that maternity relief, the right to health, and a child’s entitlement to maternal care are integral to a humane framework of employment. The court also clarified that there was no need to strike down Rule 43(1) or the state’s 2009 office memorandum, as the Maternity Benefit Act itself provides the necessary statutory protection.Directing the authorities to grant the petitioner 12 weeks’ maternity leave and all other admissible benefits, the bench quashed contrary orders and directed the education department to calculate and extend the benefits by Dec 15.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: Urges youth to keep learning new skills, adopt emerging technologies and become self-reliant; highlights dignity of labour and self-employment opportunities
content: CHANDIGARH,21.11.26-The Governor of Punjab and Administrator, U.T. Chandigarh, Shri Gulab Chand Kataria, today felicitated 498 trainees at the 5th Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh 2026 held at Government Industrial Training Institute (GITI), Sector 28-C, Chandigarh. These included 175 trainees from 10 trades of the 2024–26 batch and 323 trainees from 12 trades of the 2025–26 batch. The ceremony was part of the nationwide Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh, addressed virtually by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi from Lucknow. Congratulating the trainees, Shri Kataria said that skill development was essential for building a self-reliant and developed India. Highlighting the institute's achievements, he noted that Government ITI, established in 1962, offers training in 22 trades, has achieved 100 per cent admissions this year and has signed agreements with 20 industries, besides working with 32 other organisations. He also felicitated with award and cash awards to meritorious trainees Sandeep Kumar and Muskan from the COPA trade secured first position with 100 per cent marks and received ₹5,100 each. Abhay Partap Singh secured second position and received ₹3,100, while Radhika and Karan secured third position in Steno English and received ₹2,100 each. Emphasising the value of practical skills, the Administrator said that young people could find work and start their own businesses in many fields, not just traditional technical trades. Skills such as mehndi application, beauty and salon services, cooking and making sweets could also provide good earning opportunities, particularly for women, widows and people from weaker sections. Referring to the Pradhan Mantri Vishwakarma Yojana, he highlighted the importance of traditional artisans and craftspeople. He urged youth to respect every kind of work, overcome hesitation and use their skills to earn a livelihood and create jobs for others. Shri Kataria also encouraged trainees to keep learning and updating their skills to meet changing industry needs. He called for closer cooperation between ITIs and industries through practical training, internships and apprenticeships. Urging young people to adopt new technologies and innovation, he asked them to draw inspiration from Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam and contribute to India's goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047 through hard work and entrepreneurship. Concluding his address, Shri Kataria recalled Guru Nanak Dev Ji's teachings — "Kirat Karo, Naam Japo, Vand Chhako" — which encourage people to earn through honest work, remember the Almighty and share with those in need. He said that these values of hard work, humility and sharing were essential for building a self-reliant and caring society. Ms. Prerna Puri, IAS, Secretary, Technical Education, Chandigarh, Dr. Palika Arora, PCS, Director, Technical Education, Chandigarh, and Dr. Sunita Mehta, Principal, Government ITI, were also present on the occasion.

headline: PGIMER Chandigarh to establish medical college at Sarangpur campus; 125 MBBS seats planned
content: The government has approved the establishment of a new medical college at the Sarangpur campus of the Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), Chandigarh. The project will be developed with an investment of Rs 456 crore and is expected to offer an annual intake of 125 MBBS students.Union Health and Family Welfare Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda announced the approval through a social media post. He said the project would strengthen medical education infrastructure and contribute to the development of a skilled healthcare workforce in the country. The proposed institution will come up across nearly 51 acres at the Sarangpur campus.New medical college to have modern training facilitiesAccording to the minister, the proposed medical college will be equipped with modern laboratories, advanced simulation facilities, clinical training infrastructure and research facilities.The infrastructure is planned to support medical education and practical training, allowing students to gain exposure to clinical practices alongside their academic studies. With an annual intake capacity of 125 MBBS students, the institution will add to the country's medical education capacity.The project is also expected to strengthen PGIMER's presence in Chandigarh by expanding its educational infrastructure at the Sarangpur campus.Project aligned with Centre's medical education expansion plansNadda said the approval represents another step towards fulfilling Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of adding 75,000 medical seats across the country over the next five years.The Centre has been focusing on expanding medical education infrastructure and increasing the availability of trained healthcare professionals. The proposed college is part of this broader effort to improve access to medical education and strengthen the healthcare workforce.The addition of 125 MBBS seats annually will contribute to the country's undergraduate medical education capacity. The proposed laboratories, simulation facilities and research infrastructure are intended to support students' academic learning and clinical skill development.The government has approved the project with a proposed investment of Rs 456 crore. Further details regarding construction timelines, admission commencement and the first batch of students have not been specified in the announcement.Get the latest Education News and Live updates. headline: Chandigarh MC elections: SAD forms manifesto committee | Hindustan Times
content: The Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), Chandigarh unit, has constituted a six-member manifesto committee to prepare the party’s agenda for the upcoming UT municipal corporation elections.Party’s local unit president Charanjit Singh Villy said it would identify key civic issues, assess the concerns of residents and formulate a roadmap for the city’s development. The committee comprises advocate Amarjeet Singh Gujral, Mandeep Singh, inspector Balwinder Singh, Zabarjang Singh, Rajeev Tuli and Ashok Sharma.Villy said the committee would focus on issues concerning civic amenities, infrastructure development, transparency and accountability in municipal governance, and improvement of public services.He added that the party aimed to prepare a people-centric manifesto reflecting the needs and aspirations of Chandigarh residents.

headline: Chandigarh: Bank can’t blame customer for UPI fraud without proof, says consumer commission | Hindustan Times
content: The state consumer disputes redressal commission dismissed an appeal filed by the State Bank of India (SBI) against an order directing it to refund around ₹10,000 to a Chandigarh resident who lost the amount in five unauthorised UPI transactions in July 2021.Upholding the district consumer commission’s order, the state commission observed that the bank could not escape liability merely by alleging that the customer had shared his UPI PIN or failed to maintain its secrecy. The burden of proving customer liability in cases of unauthorised electronic banking transactions rests with the bank, as prescribed under the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) July 6, 2017 circular.The complainant, Sanjeev Kumar Sharma, had told the commission that he received messages on July 21, 2021, regarding five withdrawals of ₹25,060, ₹25,060, ₹25,060, ₹24,560 and ₹200 from his savings account, totalling ₹99,940.He alleged that a day before the transactions, a delivery agent had visited his residence to collect a wrongly delivered parcel and sought his bank details to process a refund. However, when the agent asked for his PIN, Sharma refused to share it. The following day, the unauthorised transactions took place.Sharma maintained that he neither shared his UPI PIN nor authorised the transactions. He claimed to have blocked his bank account and mobile number and informed the bank within two hours of discovering the withdrawals. He also lodged a complaint with the police’s cyber cell in Sector 9.SBI, however, argued that the transactions were carried out through UPI, which requires a six digit secret PIN but not an OTP. The bank contended that the complainant had either undertaken the transactions himself or shared his PIN, and therefore, was not entitled to reimbursement.Rejecting the bank’s contention, the state commission, presided over by justice Raj Shekhar Attri, observed that SBI had failed to produce sufficient evidence establishing the complainant’s liability. It noted that the customer had consistently maintained that the transactions were unauthorised and had promptly reported the fraud to the bank and the police.Referring to the RBI circular on customer protection in unauthorised electronic banking transactions, the commission highlighted that customers are entitled to zero liability in specified circumstances, including third-party breaches reported within three working days. It also noted that banks are required to provisionally credit the disputed amount within 10 working days of receiving notification.The commission further observed that the RBI guidelines place the burden of proving customer liability on the bank.The district commission had, in its November 11, 2025 order, directed SBI to refund ₹99,940 with 9% annual interest from July 21, 2021, till realisation, besides paying ₹10,000 towards mental agony, harassment and litigation expenses.SBI had challenged the order before the state commission, which dismissed the appeal as devoid of merit on October 21. The commission also directed that the ₹1,54,200 deposited by the bank during the appeal proceedings be remitted to the district commission for disbursement to the complainant in accordance with the original order.

headline: Chandigarh MC elections: BJP holds in-house voting to pick candidates for polls | Hindustan Times
content: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) workers voted for their preferred candidates for the upcoming Chandigarh municipal corporation (MC) elections through a secret ballot, as the party begins shortlisting contenders for all 35 wards.While some wards have clear frontrunners, the party is relying on multiple rounds of surveys before finalising its candidates for all the wards.The feedback gathered through secret voting will be assessed alongside inputs from the party’s organisational network and independent surveys to gauge the winnability of potential candidates.The BJP has appointed observers for all 35 wards, who are interacting with booth in-charges, Shakti Kendra pramukhs and other grassroots workers to understand local preferences. The party is also reaching out to influential residents, including doctors, sportspersons, professionals working in multinational companies and other prominent personalities, to assess public sentiment and identify potential candidates.Central agencies are also expected to conduct surveys to independently assess the popularity and electoral prospects of shortlisted contenders. The findings will be used to cross-check the feedback received through the party’s internal exercise.According to a source within the party, the announcement will be made near the nomination date.Ward reservation changes complicate selectionThe change in reservation status of certain wards has emerged as another challenge for the BJP’s candidate-selection exercise. Some wards that were previously unreserved have now become reserved, affecting the prospects of sitting councillors. Consequently, some existing councillors may not be considered for the same wards they currently represent due to anti-incumbency.The party is also keen to field candidates who are residents of the wards they seek to contest from, rather than bringing in candidates from outside.Nabin to visit city on Nov 22, eye on bigger pictureBJP national president Nitin Nabin is scheduled to visit Chandigarh on November 22 to address a workers’ conference. His visit comes as the party’s central leadership closely monitors preparations for the civic polls.The MC elections are also being viewed against the backdrop of the 2027 Punjab assembly elections. AAP’s emergence as the largest party in the 2021 MC elections, with 14 seats, preceded its landslide victory in Punjab in 2022, when it won 92 seats. While the two elections are fought on different issues and electoral dynamics, the Chandigarh contest is likely to be watched for indications of the parties’ organisational strength and voter sentiment ahead of the Punjab assembly battle.Currently, the BJP holds 18 seats in the 35-member elected MC General House.Party intensifies digital outreachBJP leaders on Friday held a ‘Social Media Samvad’ at the party office, Kamalam, to discuss digital outreach and election preparations for the upcoming polls. BJP national social media convenor Deepak Maske and co-convenor Arun Yadav, along with Chandigarh BJP in-charge Mahendra Pandey and state president Jatinder Pal Malhotra, asked party workers to strengthen digital engagement, highlight local civic issues and communicate the party’s development work effectively through social media platforms.Meanwhile, BJP Chandigarh general secretary Ramveer Bhatti said the party would approach voters with a report card of its development work over the past five years rather than making fresh promises. He said the BJP had governed the MC for the past 10 years, barring a one-year period when the AAP was in power, and would present its achievements in roads, sanitation, drinking water, public amenities and urban infrastructure before voters.

headline: Municipal corporation elections: In a first for Chandigarh, webcasting at all polling stations | Hindustan Times
content: A mobile app, ‘Nigam Chunav Chandigarh’ offering real-time waiting at polling stations through queue management system to a QR-code facility for feedback, webcasting at all polling stations enabling monitoring of live proceedings to enhanced closed-circuit television (CCTV) camera coverage at offices of all election officials, the state election commission has rolled out a series of initiatives for 2026 MC elections.State election commissioner Vijay Dev said for the first time in Chandigarh, webcasting will be conducted at all 576 polling stations which will allow officials to monitor live proceedings through their dashboards. He added that voter info slips will provide the coordinates of polling stations to help voters locate them.Videography Further, all critical election events, including the filing of nomination papers, scrutiny, allotment of symbols, preparations and storage of EVMs, important public meetings and processions, will be videographed by the commission. CCTV cameras will be installed at all offices of returning officers, strongrooms and counting centres.Real-time updates on waiting time at polling stationsFor the convenience of voters, the commission has also introduced the ‘Nigam Chunav Chandigarh’ mobile application (to be available on Android and Apple store), which will let voters to search their names in the electoral roll, locate their polling stations on maps, access information about candidates and their affidavits, file complaints and obtain contact details of election officers. The application will also provide access to election results, facilities for assistance to persons with disabilities and voters above 85 years of age, and real-time information on waiting times at polling stations through a queue management system.App for election officials too The commission has also developed a separate ‘SEC Officers Chandigarh’ mobile application to facilitate real-time interaction and sharing of important information and data among election officials. The app is aimed at ensuring timely processing of election-related information and effective coordination among various election functionaries.Single-window systemDistrict election officers, returning officers, assistant returning officers, UT police and officials concerned with the model code of conduct will be able to coordinate through a single-window portal. It has been made available through the commission’s website, chandigarh.gov.in/state-election-commission. The portal will facilitate the grant of permissions to candidates and political parties for organising rallies and using vehicles and loudspeakers, among other election-related activities. An optional facility for filing nomination papers online has also been provided on the website.Feedback through QR codeQR-code-based voter feedback forms will be available at all 576 polling stations. Voters will be able to scan the QR code and share their experience of voting, give feedback on the facilities available at polling premises and offer suggestions for improvement.Facilities at polling stationsOn the infrastructure front, one of the key changes this election is the upgrade of facilities at polling stations from basic minimum facilities to assured minimum facilities. The commission has issued instructions to returning officers and other concerned agencies to ensure that all stations are equipped with essential facilities, including drinking water, sheds and toilets, for the convenience of voters. Special arrangements have also been made for persons with disabilities (PwD) with polling stations located on the ground floor and sturdy ramps to be provided to facilitate access for voters with disabilities.Maximum expenditure limit raised to ₹7.5 lakhThe commission has fixed the maximum election expenditure limit for a candidate contesting from ₹5 lakh per candidate (in 2021 polls) to ₹7.5 lakh this time. Every nominated candidate will be required to maintain an account of election-related expenditure from the date of nomination until withdrawal of candidature, rejection of nomination or declaration of election results, as applicable.Voters more forthcoming in Lok Sabha polls than MCDev said it has been observed that Chandigarh voters come out to vote in Parliamentary elections more than in MC. “MC polls voting has traditionally been around 60 % while in MP elections, the voting percentage is more, we will try to improve this figure in MC polls,” he said.

headline: Chandigarh municipal corporation elections on December 23, results 3 days later | Hindustan Times
content: Residents, mark your calendars. The countdown to picking your next ward councillor has officially begun with the state election commission announcing December 23 as the D-day.The commission released the full poll schedule (see box) at a press conference on Friday, bringing into force the model code of conduct – a set of guidelines issued by the election commission to regulate the behavior of political parties, candidates, and the government to ensure free, fair, and peaceful elections. The poll code will remain in force till the election process is over.State election commissioner Vijay Dev said all political parties, candidates, departments of UT administration, the director general of police, heads of local bodies and autonomous institutions will have to adhere to the poll code.On polling day, 576 booths will be set up across 35 wards, and voting will take place from 7.30 am to 5 pm. Counting of votes will take place on December 26 and the elections shall be completed on December 31.Postal ballot service will be available for all voters above the age of 80. The city has over 4.6 lakh registered voters, including 2.3 lakh male voters, 2.2 lakh female voters and 22 third gender voters. This includes 2,059 first-time voters, and 1,569 persons with disabilities.The five-year term of the current MC House expires on January 7, 2027.

headline: Haryana orders comprehensive audit of all govt portals, digital payment systems
content: Chandigarh: Haryana has ordered a comprehensive audit of all government portals and digital payment systems to plug technical loopholes, prevent financial fraud and secure public funds, with banks and IT experts being roped in to identify vulnerabilities in online transactions and fund-transfer mechanisms.The directions were issued by chief secretary Anurag Rastogi during a meeting with representatives of 25 public and private sector banks, government departments and technology experts on Friday. He directed departments to examine weaknesses in payment processes, bank account transfers and the exchange of transaction-related data between government portals and banking platforms.Rastogi stressed that banks and departments must work in close coordination to prevent unauthorised transactions and diversion of government money. Given the substantial funds disbursed through welfare schemes, development programmes and departmental expenditure, he said, securing digital payment infrastructure was critical. He asked banks to undertake technical scrutiny of payment gateways, application programming interface (API) integrations and other electronic channels used for government transactions. Banks, as custodians of public funds, must ensure that payments reach the intended beneficiaries and designated accounts, Rastogi said.The chief secretary also directed banking and technology experts to examine emerging methods of financial fraud, including the possible misuse of artificial intelligence (AI), and suggest practical safeguards against such threats. Banks and departments have been asked to consult their technical teams and submit concrete recommendations to the Finance Department.Additional chief secretary Sudhir Rajpal called for tighter financial controls at points where government payment systems interface with banking platforms. He emphasised regular transaction monitoring, verification of payment details and timely reconciliation of bank accounts to detect discrepancies and prevent unauthorised transfers. Officials also flagged possible inconsistencies in transaction-data exchange between government portals and banks, underlining the need for stronger verification and reconciliation mechanisms. headline: Chandigarh Carnival kicks off, brings India’s cultural diversity to Leisure Valley
content: Punjab Governor and UT Administrator Gulab Chand Kataria on Friday inaugurated the three-day Chandigarh Carnival 2026 at Leisure Valley, Sector 10. Organised by the UT Department of Tourism, the carnival will continue till November 22, bringing together art, culture, music, entertainment and festive activities. The Tribune is the media partner of the event.The Administrator flagged off the carnival parade, featuring colourful and creatively designed tableaux prepared by students of the Government College of Art. This was followed by a ribbon-cutting ceremony to formally inaugurate the event.He also witnessed performances by local artists showcasing the folk culture and traditions of different states through dance and music. Kataria said the carnival reflected the spirit of “Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat”.Kataria also visited the exhibition, An exhibition, “Darshan Deedar – Guru Nanak Dev Ji: A Journey Through Art and Spirituality”, is being held at the Government Museum and Art Gallery.The ground opposite the Government Museum and Art Gallery in Sector 10 came alive with rows of shopping stalls, amusement rides, prize games and food counters, all illuminated for the evening. Tattoo artists inked designs, face-painting stalls transformed children into tigers and butterflies, while portrait artists sketched visitors who patiently sat for their likenesses."Being surrounded by artists is the best part," said Seema, who runs a handmade crochet and art business from home with her husband, Ajay. The couple visits exhibitions to gain exposure.Nisha Sharma, who runs the Agile Arts stall and travelled from Kalka for the carnival, shared a similar sentiment. "Wherever I look, there are artists, from students to business owners. It makes me feel that I belong here," she said.Rishit and Nivedita, both artists from Mohali, said they had come solely to support fellow artists. "Nivedita wants to turn her painting work into a business, so we came here for inspiration," Rishit said. Akshita, a resident of Sector 19, had a simpler reason for visiting. With her hands full of shopping bags, she said, "The best part was the shopping stalls. The prices were reasonable for the quality."Near the entrance, young artists stole the show. Around 15 cycle-based carts, designed as floats featuring Spider Man, Hulk and other superheroes, were created by students of the Government College of Art. Children giggled as they were taken around on the colourful carts. First-year student Gulshan said around 12 students had spent two weeks building one cart.A stall celebrating Punjabi heritage attracted visitors with phulkari-style embroidered wall hangings, lanterns and wicker seating. Set up by folk singer Sukhi Brar, it also featured a tractor that became a popular backdrop for photographs.

headline: Gurgaon Kannada Sangha to celebrate Kannada Rajyotsava 2026 on Nov 22
content: New Delhi: The Gurgaon Kannada Sangha, in association with Delhi Karnataka Sangha and the Karnataka Border Area Development Authority, will organise Kannada Rajyotsava 2026 in Gurugram on Sunday.Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav will inaugurate the event. Guests of honour include Somanna Bevinamarad, Chairman of the Karnataka Border Area Development Authority; R Renukumar, President of the Delhi Karnataka Sangha; Prakash V Mattihalli, Secretary of the Karnataka Border Area Development Authority; and Umesh G Jadhav, former Member of Parliament from Kalaburagi..Karnataka Rajyotsava celebrated with fervour in Mysuru.The programme will begin at 2 pm at Excelsior American School, Golf Course Road, behind the Dell Building, Block C2, DLF Garden Villas/Sushant Lok Phase 1, Sector 43, Gurugram.Cultural programmes will also form part of the celebrations, according to a statement issued by Shanthkumar Veeranna Nimbal, President of the Gurgaon Kannada Sangha.

headline: Delhi Police nabs 14-year-old Haryana boy trying to sell data of Agniveers on dark web for ₹47,000 | India News
content: A 14-year-old boy from Haryana's Ballabhgarh was held by the Delhi Police on Saturday for allegedly hacking into a website meant for former Agniveers, officials said. He also allegedly attempted to sell the information of around 4,000 personnel on the dark web for $500 (approximately ₹47,000).The teen gained unauthorised access to a test website developed for former Agniveers, news agency PTI reported. The platform was designed to allow personnel who had completed their four-year military service to register and explore employment opportunities in other government departments.He allegedly extracted information from the platform and posted an advertisement on the dark web, claiming to possess details of around 4,000 Agniveers and offering the data for sale. Investigators suspect that AI tools may have been used to access the website.The Delhi Police's Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit has recovered data from the boy's digital devices. The material is being analysed to verify whether it contains genuine information and establish the extent of the suspected breach.Police have also approached the Union ministry of home affairs seeking access to the official Agniveer database to cross-check the recovered information.The teen was questioned in accordance with the law and later handed over to his family following preliminary questioning, officials said.What is the Agniveer scheme?The Agniveer recruitment programme was introduced by the Centre in June 2022, under the Agnipath scheme. It allows young men and women to join the Indian Army, Navy and Air Force for a four-year tenure. Those recruited are called Agniveers and undergo military training before being deployed in their respective services.At the end of their four-year service, up to 25% of each batch can be retained in the regular armed forces, depending on organisational requirements and performance. The remaining personnel are released with a one-time Seva Nidhi package.The programme is also intended to help former Agniveers find employment after completing their military service, including through opportunities in government departments and the private sector.

headline: Panchkula councillor wants permit for ‘dog-sized’ cow in each home. Mayor in favour, not the law
content: Chandigarh: A cow the size of a dog could soon be at the centre of a debate in the Panchkula Municipal Corporation. Ward 4 councillor Bharat Hiteshi has moved a special agenda item, urging the House to allow residents to keep Nadipathy cows, up to two feet tall, as pets. He has modelled the proposal on the Nadipathy Goshala in Andhra Pradesh. The item requests the House to frame rules on space, cleanliness, animal care, animal welfare and public health after consulting the concerned departments, and to grant permission under those conditions. “Hindus worship the cow and keep it at home. Panchkula is a planned city developed largely by the Haryana Shahri Vikas Pradhikaran (HSVP), where keeping milch animals is prohibited,” Hiteshi told ThePrint. A miniature cow, he said, is the size of a dog and can easily be kept in a house. The meeting certainly would be held by the end of the month, Hiteshi added. Strictly speaking, Nadipathy is not a breed. It is the name of a goshala at Lingamparthi village in Andhra Pradesh’s Eluru region, and the brand founded by its founder and Ayurvedic practitioner P. Krishnam Raju. The goshala says its animals grow to just two feet. These miniature cows gained attention after Raju presented them to PM Narendra Modi. The cattle are descended from the Punganur, a dwarf breed from Chittoor district of Andhra Pradesh. Punganur is among the world’s smallest humped cattle breeds, and its milk has a high fat content.

headline: Delhi–Panipat–Karnal Namo Bharat corridor to boost real estate in the region
content: New Delhi: The Delhi–Panipat–Karnal Namo Bharat (RRTS) corridor, which will provide fast, seamless connectivity between Delhi and major cities in Haryana, has now received approval from the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), following clearances from the Centre and the Haryana government.The move will boost the real estate development along the corridor, expert said.“With fast, convenient public transport, the potential for residential, commercial and mixed-use development in these cities will grow. Growth could pick up especially in areas that have so far been unable to realise their full potential for lack of good connectivity. The corridor can play an important role in balanced urban development in Haryana and in the emergence of new real estate hubs,” said Abhay Kumar Mishra, President and CEO of Jindal Realty.Also Read | Tata Power, NCRTC sign pact to shift utilities for 136-km Namo Bharat corridorThe 136.3-km corridor, to be developed by the National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) at a cost of about Rs 33,051 crore, is targeted for completion by 2030. Running parallel to the Delhi–Ambala highway (NH-44), the corridor has received land-use permission from NHAI for pier construction, station development and the shifting of high-tension power lines along the route.“The Namo Bharat corridor will create new opportunities for homebuyers in cities such as Sonipat, Panipat and Karnal. With fast and easy access to Delhi, people will take these cities more seriously as places to live. The impact could be felt especially by families and working professionals looking for affordable, convenient housing with better connectivity. Demand for retail, schools, healthcare and other everyday amenities around the stations will also grow,” said Yashank Vasan, Managing Director of Royal Green Realty.Preliminary work has already begun on a roughly 22-km stretch between Narela and Murthal. Namo Bharat trains on this route, with a maximum design speed of 180 km/h and an operating speed of 160 km/h, will run every 5 to 10 minutes. Haryana will be directly linked to the Namo Bharat network, and through the Delhi–Meerut corridor, to Uttar Pradesh as well.A total of 22 stations are proposed along the route, and most will be elevated, except for Kashmere Gate in Delhi and the stations in Panipat.Also Read | NCRTC to develop urban centres along the Namo Bharat corridorThe mega project will cut travel times sharply. The journey from Delhi to Panipat, which currently takes two to two and a half hours by road or regular train, will come down to one hour, and the three-and-a-half to four-hour trip to Karnal will be reduced to an hour and a half.With the Haryana government including the corridor in its Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) policy, high-rise residential buildings, offices, retail space and commercial complexes are expected to expand rapidly around the stations.“The Namo Bharat project will bring a significant transformation to this belt. This corridor is another important step in that direction. With faster connectivity to Delhi, people can explore residential opportunities in emerging locations such as Sonipat and Panipat. As a developer, we expect improved connectivity to drive demand for both residential and commercial real estate along this belt. With the project targeted for completion by 2030, it has the potential to bring lasting changes to the region’s real estate landscape,” said Vinod Kumar, Director & Founder, Sky Byte Developers.

headline: 14-year-old hacker held for trying to sell private data of 4,000 Agniveers on dark web: Delhi Police
content: New Delhi: A 14-year-old boy from Haryana's Ballabhgarh was apprehended by the Delhi Police Special Cell for allegedly hacking into a website and attempting to sell sensitive data linked to around 4,000 Agniveer personnel on the dark web for USD 500, officials said..According to investigators, the juvenile gained unauthorised access to a test website designed for former Agniveers to register themselves and explore employment opportunities in other government departments..After accessing the website, the boy allegedly extracted the information and posted an advertisement on the dark web, claiming to possess personal data of around 4,000 Agniveers and offering to sell it for USD 500, they said..Investigation has revealed that artificial intelligence tools were allegedly used to access the information, officials said, adding that the exact method employed to breach the website is being examined..The Delhi Police's Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit has recovered data from the juvenile's digital devices. Investigators are now examining the material to ascertain whether it contains genuine information and establish the extent of the suspected breach..Guidelines issued during anti-CEC protest to distinguish journalists from reel-makers, Delhi police tell Supreme Court.The police have also written to the Union Ministry of Home Affairs seeking the official database of Agniveers to match it with the recovered information and verify its authenticity..The juvenile was apprehended and questioned in accordance with the law. Following preliminary questioning, he was handed over to his family, officials said..Further investigation is underway to determine how the website was accessed, whether the information was compromised beyond the data recovered from the boy's devices and if any third party had purchased or accessed the purported database..The incident has brought the security of digital platforms containing information related to Agniveer personnel under scrutiny, even as investigators work to establish the nature and scale of the alleged data breach..The Centre launched the Agnipath recruitment scheme in June 2022 to induct personnel into the Army, Navy and Air Force for a four-year tenure. Those recruited under the scheme, known as Agniveers, undergo military training before being deployed in their respective services.

headline: 14-year-old used AI chatbot to hack Agniveer ‘test’ website, wanted to earn money by selling it on dark web: Delhi police sources
content: New Delhi A 14-year-old boy from Haryana’s Ballabhgarh, who was apprehended for attempting to sell sensitive information linked to around 4,000 Agniveer personnel on the dark web, used artificial intelligence tools to “identify data that could fetch him money and sought the chatbot’s help to hack into a website”, a senior official familiar with the investigation told The Hindu. The boy gained unauthorised access to a test website designed for former Agniveers to register themselves and explore employment opportunities in the Indian Armed Forces. Cyber commandos lead Delhi Police’s digital fight amid protests, bomb hoaxes, crypto frauds Cyber commandos lead Delhi Police’s digital fight amid protests, bomb hoaxes, crypto frauds With just eight commandos, the specialised unit brings advanced technical expertise to decode intricate data and help field officers solve cybercrimes across the National Capital Region Cyber commandos lead Delhi Police’s digital fight amid protests, bomb hoaxes, crypto frauds storyline 1 “Preliminary investigation has revealed that the boy managed to breach only the test website, gaining access to names and addresses. There is no indication so far that information relating to marks, ranks, results or other sensitive personnel records was compromised,” the official said. During preliminary questioning, the boy told investigators that he was motivated by the prospect of making money. “He said he first asked an AI chatbot to identify what kind of data could help him earn money. He then sought its assistance in finding a way to hack into the system and access such information,” the official said. The exact method used to gain access to the website is still being examined. After accessing the website, the boy allegedly extracted the information and advertised it on a dark web marketplace, claiming to possess personal records of around 4,000 Agniveer personnel and sought $500 for the purported database. The Delhi Police’s Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit has recovered data from the juvenile’s digital devices. Investigators are now examining the material to establish its authenticity and determine the extent of the suspected breach. The IFSO unit has also written to the National Informatics Centre (NIC), seeking clarification on the data available on the test website and the information accessed by the boy. The police are awaiting a response to ascertain precisely what information may have been compromised. AI agents gained unauthorised access to Indian organisations, says CERT-In AI agents gained unauthorised access to Indian organisations, says CERT-In The extraordinary disclosure — which does not name the AI providers or Indian organisations involved — comes as a result of proactive disclosures from the agents’ own developers, says CERT-In AI agents gained unauthorised access to Indian organisations, says CERT-In storyline 1 While the NIC provides digital infrastructure and hosts government portals, the ownership and maintenance of Agniveer personnel records rest with the Armed Forces and the concerned ministries, officials said. As the accused is a juvenile, he was counselled and handed over to his parents. The police are consulting the Juvenile Justice Board on the further course of action. Further investigation is underway.

headline: Stubble stops burning when somebody buys it
content: Every winter, stubble burning takes centre stage in India’s air pollution debate. Governments announce measures, farmers are urged to adopt residue-management machinery, and there is no shortage of ideas for putting agricultural waste to productive use. Yet the question underneath it all is rarely asked: who will buy the straw, and can selling it leave the farmer better off than burning it?For a farmer working against the narrow window between two cropping cycles, an alternative to burning must be timely and economical, and most importantly, reliable. So, the challenge is not simply to find ways to remove paddy straw from fields, but to create an ecosystem in which it has a marketable value. This calls for a shift in how we approach the problem: from viewing crop residue as agricultural waste to recognising it as an industrial resource that can support energy generation and create value across the supply chain. Stubble burning, in other words, is an industrial question before it is an agricultural one.The Burning ChallengeThis season, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has deployed flying squads in 34 districts across Punjab and Haryana to monitor and prevent paddy stubble burning. Enforcement has its place, but it cannot by itself change the farmer’s economics. India has also spent almost a decade building the machinery to lift paddy straw off the field, and that investment has paid off. But machinery answers how the straw leaves the field, not where it goes or who pays for it.The next decade of effort has to go into building the market that buys and uses this straw, and that is work industry must lead, with policy as the enabler. This calls for a policy framework that supports reliable straw procurement, encourages long-term offtake arrangements between farmers and industry, and strengthens the collection, aggregation and transportation infrastructure. Crop residue stops being burnt when it acquires a buyer, a price and a collection window that fits the sowing calendar.For years, the crop-residue debate has centred on subsidies for in-situ machinery. Far less attention goes to the ex-situ demand side – who actually buys the straw, at what price, and whether that demand survives a bad year. Ex-situ management means baling the straw after harvest and moving it to where it can be used: biomass power plants, compressed biogas units, bio-ethanol refineries, industrial boilers and others. At SAEL, we see this demand side from the inside. Our eleven agricultural waste to energy plants across Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan process about two million tonnes of agricultural residue a year, and the lesson of operating them is simple: the hard part is less the technology than a supply chain that reaches thousands of farms within a few weeks, every year, at a price that works for both sides.The shift to ex-situ applications is driven by stringent environmental regulations, and the urgent need to tackle winter air pollution across the nation. Consequently, paddy straw has strong potential to transition from an annual agricultural hazard to a dependable industrial raw material. This transition is already gaining ground, with organised efforts demonstrating how paddy straw can be mobilised and channelled into industrial applications at scale. For example, near Sonipat in Haryana, farmers are selling bales of paddy straw to companies for industrial use, including energy generation, instead of burning the residue. This creates an alternative source of income from what was previously treated as agricultural waste.The Three-Week ProblemBut these remain islands. Estimates suggest that India produces 125–140 million tonnes of paddy straw a year, and that 35–40 million tonnes of it is still burnt. Why is more of it not sold?The answer lies in the nature of straw itself. It is plentiful and arrives every year. But because it is bulky, it remains expensive to transport. To compound matters, straw arrives all at once, within the same 15 to 20 days across an entire state, because the next crop is due. A year’s supply has to be collected, baled and stored within this window.These challenges can be met through institutional investment in equipment to bale, store and move millions of tonnes of straw close to where it is grown. Without the necessary residue-management equipment and labour, farmers will have no option but to burn the residual paddy straw.Making the Economics WorkIndustries that consume straw can do far more alongside state governments that are already investing in residue management: longer-term offtake commitments that give farmers and aggregators certainty, shared storage close to the fields, and procurement calendars aligned with the harvest. States want cleaner air in October and November; industry needs reliable feedstock all year; farmers need a buyer who turns up on time. Those interests already point in the same direction.As paddy harvesting gains momentum, Punjab has recorded more stubble fires than last year, a reminder that the gains of Kharif 2025 do not sustain themselves. Between 15 September and 13 October 2026, Punjab witnessed 174 stubble-burning incidents, up from 134 in the same period in 2025.Ultimately, the success of crop-residue management will depend on whether we can make the economics work for the farmer. Enforcement can restrain burning, and technology can make collection easier, but neither can replace the guarantee of a buyer. When residue becomes a commercially valued resource, the interests of farmers, industry and the environment begin to align.The opportunity is to turn a seasonal pollution challenge into a year-round industrial value chain. Stubble will stop burning at scale when the market makes it more valuable to sell it than to burn it.The article is written by Laxit Awla, CEO & Executive Director, SAEL Industries Limited.Note to the Reader: This article is part of Mint's promotional consumer connect initiative and is independently created by the brand. Mint assumes no editorial responsibility for the content.

headline: Haryana CM cracks whip over ‘shoddy’ civic works, sacks XEN in Sirsa dist
content: Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini came down heavily on municipal officials during a grievance redressal meeting in Sirsa on Sunday, ordering the suspension of an executive engineer (XEN), salary cuts and disciplinary action against other officials over alleged irregularities in civic works worth around Rs 30 crore.The action followed complaints by three councillors — Sanjeev Ratusaria of Ward 20, Deepak Bansal of Ward 12 and Rajendra Jangra of Ward 26 — regarding development works in 26 approved colonies.The councillors alleged that the work recorded in measurement books (MBs) exceeded what had actually been completed on the ground.When the XEN presented his inspection report, which showed an incomplete street, Saini lost his temper and asked him to identify the streets where no work had been carried out rather than those where work was only partially complete.“I have the entire report. Why are you showing me this? You were appointed to investigate the complaint. Why are you presenting an incorrect report?” the CM asked.After questioning the officials involved in preparing the report, Saini ordered strict action.An XEN was suspended, while the Deputy Municipal Commissioner (DMC) was ordered to forfeit one month’s salary. Disciplinary action, including suspension and the issuance of chargesheets, was also directed against a Junior Engineer (JE) and a Municipal Engineer (ME).The CM also ordered the registration of a case against the contractor, an inquiry into his properties and his blacklisting if the allegations were substantiated. He said the contractor would have to compensate for the losses caused by substandard work.“We will not tolerate such negligence. Officials must work in the public interest and should not act under anyone’s pressure,” Saini said.On the CDLU land dispute, the CM said his government did not favour builders and that the matter was pending before the High Court.On the shortage of canal water, he said the issue had recently come to his notice and that the officials concerned had been questioned.Saini added that 113 development works worth more than Rs 8.67 crore had been approved for the Sirsa constituency. Of these, 38 had been completed, 50 were underway and work on the remaining 24 was yet to begin.Earlier in the day, Saini flagged off a 5-km marathon in Kalanwali and ran alongside participants as part of the state’s anti-drug campaign.

headline: Haryana’s revenue receipts under pressure as committed spending eats up 56%
content: Chandigarh: Haryana’s finances face mounting pressure from committed expenditure and rising welfare transfers, with interest payments, salaries and pensions together accounting for 56% of the state’s revenue receipts, according to the latest State of State Finances 2026-27 report by PRS Legislative Research.The report points out that more than 85% of Haryana’s total expenditure goes towards revenue items, leaving a relatively smaller share for capital expenditure and asset creation. The high committed expenditure limits the government’s flexibility to redirect resources towards development priorities.The state has budgeted a revenue deficit of 0.9% of its Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) for 2026-27. This means its revenue expenditure will exceed its revenue receipts, requiring borrowings to finance recurring expenditure.Another significant component is welfare transfers. Haryana has earmarked Rs 15,499 crore for identified unconditional cash transfer schemes in 2026-27, equivalent to 11% of its revenue receipts. Of this, Rs 6,500 crore is allocated for women, Rs 8,629 crore for social security pension beneficiaries and Rs 370 crore for youth. The allocation places Haryana among nine states spending more than 10% of their revenue receipts on such transfers.On the revenue mobilisation front, Haryana’s own-tax revenue is estimated at 6.9% of GSDP, marginally below the national state average of 7%. Maharashtra (7.7%) and Punjab (7.2%) have higher ratios.However, Haryana has recorded a strong performance in GST collections. Its SGST revenue grew 23% in 2025-26, with the SGST-to-GSDP ratio rising from 3.1% to 3.4%, even as several states witnessed a decline.The report also highlights the growing dependence of states on revenue expenditure. Nationally, the combined revenue deficit rose from 0.23% of GDP in 2022-23 to 0.71% in 2025-26, reflecting the widening gap between recurring expenditure and receipts.The findings underline the challenge before Haryana: sustaining welfare commitments while maintaining fiscal space for infrastructure, investment and long-term development.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news.
