headline: Haryana government tells education department to avoid scheduling major exams before March 1 | Hindustan Times
content: The Haryana government has directed the state education authorities not to schedule any major examinations before March 1, 2027 in view of the deployment of teachers for the upcoming Census 2027 exercise.In an official communication issued by the school education department on November 17, the principal secretary’s office directed the secretary of the Board of School Education Haryana and all district education officers (DEOs) and district elementary education officers (DEEOs) to ensure that no major examinations are to be scheduled before the stipulated date.The directive comes against the backdrop of the second phase of Census 2027, involving house-to-house field enumeration, which is scheduled to begin in January 2027 and will be completed by March 1, 2027.Citing information received from the registrar general and census commissioner, Haryana the department said the Census exercise was underway and, like previous exercises, it would be conducted in two phases. The first phase, involving house-listing and housing census had already been completed in all states and Union territories except Manipur, according to the communication.The order highlighted that a majority of these personnel are to be drawn from the pool of primary and middle school teachers, while a significant number of secondary school teachers will also be deployed for census-related duties.Considering the involvement of a large number of teachers in the exercise, the education department has asked the concerned authorities to plan the examination schedule accordingly to avoid any disruption.

headline: Haryana orders audit of government portals, digital payment systems | Hindustan Times
content: The Haryana government on Friday directed departments to conduct a comprehensive audit of their online portals and digital payment systems to identify technical vulnerabilities for preventing financial fraud and safeguarding public funds. The audit will examine weaknesses in payment processes, fund transfers between bank accounts and the exchange of transaction related data between government portals and banking platforms.Chief secretary Anurag Rastogi who chaired a high level meeting attended by representatives of 25 public and private sector banks, government departments and information technology experts said banks and government departments must work together to prevent unauthorised transactions involving public money and its transfer to other accounts. The chief secretary said the state government makes substantial payments under various welfare schemes, development projects and departmental expenditure, making it essential to ensure the technical security of digital payment systems.He asked banks to work closely with the departments concerned to conduct technical examinations of payment gateways, application programming interface (API) integrations and other electronic channels used for transferring government funds.Rastogi said banks, as custodians of public funds, had a responsibility to ensure that payments reached the intended beneficiaries and designated accounts. He emphasised the need for stronger preventive safeguards and accountability in handling public money.The chief secretary asked banking and technology experts to examine different methods of financial fraud, including the potential misuse of artificial intelligence (AI), and recommend practical measures to prevent such activities.He directed banks and government departments to continue consultations with their technical teams and submit concrete recommendations to the finance department.Additional chief secretary, finance, Sudhir Rajpal said financial controls at sensitive points where government payment systems interface with banking platforms should be strengthenedHe said regular monitoring of transactions, verification of payment details and timely reconciliation of bank accounts must be ensured. Recommendations received from banks and technology experts would be examined in consultation with the departments concerned before necessary corrective measures were taken.Officials also raised the issue of potential discrepancies in the exchange of transaction-related data between government portals and banking platforms. They stressed the need to strengthen payment verification procedures and regular account reconciliation to maintain the accuracy of financial records.

headline: Rights panel seeks reports on sexual abuse of 5-yr-old Panipat girl
content: Panipat: Taking note of the alleged sexual abuse of a five-year-old girl by a school van driver in Panipat, the Haryana Human Rights Commission (HHRC) has sought detailed reports from the deputy commissioner, the superintendent of police, the district education officer, and the school management.The commission took suo motu cognisance of a newspaper report highlighting serious concerns over children’s safety during school transportation.A full commission bench comprising chairperson Justice Lalit Batra, judicial member Kuldip Jain and member Deep Bhatia observed that ensuring children’s safety is a paramount responsibility of educational institutions, extending beyond school premises to transportation arrangements.According to the report, the school van driver allegedly touched the KG student inappropriately and threatened her against disclosing the incident. The child reportedly experienced difficulty walking and using the toilet before revealing the incident to her mother.Following a complaint by her father, a case was registered at the women police station in Panipat under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and other relevant provisions.The child’s medical examination was conducted, and her statement was recorded before a court. The Child Welfare Committee also reportedly counselled her.The commission particularly noted allegations that the driver made the child sit on the front seat of the van while the woman attendant remained occupied with her mobile phone. It also noted that the school’s head teacher had denied the occurrence of such an incident. However, the Commission clarified that the allegations were yet to be established through an impartial investigation.Highlighting the accountability of school management, the Commission said institutions must ensure proper background verification of drivers and attendants, effective supervision during transportation and adequate safeguards against any form of abuse. It emphasised that attendants must remain vigilant throughout the journey and respond promptly to any indication of harm to a child.The commission also directed the district education officer (DEO) to examine compliance with Haryana’s Surakshit School Vahan Policy, particularly the installation and functioning of CCTV cameras in the school van on the date of the alleged incident.The availability and preservation of CCTV footage, along with details of the person responsible for maintaining the recordings, must also be verified. Any available footage must be secured immediately for examination by the investigating agency.The Commission stressed that CCTV surveillance must cover the entire vehicle while ensuring the privacy and dignity of children.The Panipat DC has been directed to examine the matter and coordinate action among the concerned departments. The DEO must report on the school’s recognition, transport safety compliance, background verification of the driver and attendant, supervision arrangements and child-protection mechanisms.The SP has been asked to provide details of the FIR, investigation, evidence collection, medical examination, the child’s statement and measures taken to ensure her safety.The school management must explain its transport arrangements, staff responsibilities and corrective measures, while the district programme officer of the women and child development department must report on the Child Welfare Committee’s intervention and assistance provided to the child.Referring to the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child; the POCSO Act, 2012; and the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, the Commission emphasised that the child’s best interests, dignity and confidentiality must remain paramount throughout the proceedings.Puneet Arora, assistant registrar of the State Human Rights Commission, said all authorities had been directed to specify measures to prevent recurrence of such incidents, strengthen supervision and fix accountability wherever negligence was established.The matter has been adjourned to Jan 28, 2027. All concerned authorities and the school management have been directed to submit their detailed reports at least one week before the next hearing.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: Chandigarh: 18 live rounds seized from Sector-39 house, Delhi man booked | Hindustan Times
content: A 24-year-old Delhi man was booked under the Arms Act after 18 live ammunition rounds were recovered from his rented accommodation in Sector 39-B, police said on Friday.The recovery was made by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), Chandigarh Regional Unit, during a search of house number 1036 on Thursday. The accused, Joy Prem, a resident of Dilshad Colony in East Delhi, had shifted to the premises a few days before the search.According to the complaint lodged by DRI officer Lakshyarth Sihag, the ammunition was handed over to the Sector 39 police, following which an FIR under relevant provisions of the Arms Act was registered.Prem is currently in DRI custody in connection with an investigation into a suspected contraband consignment traced at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport. Chandigarh Police are expected to seek his custody on a production warrant for further questioning.The police are investigating the source of the ammunition. The property’s owner is reportedly in Australia.

headline: Delhi Health Minister Urges US Healthcare Companies To Bring Affordable Technologies To India
content: Delhi Health Minister Dr Pankaj Kumar Singh on 19 November 2026, invited US healthcare and pharmaceutical companies to bring advanced technologies to India at affordable prices, calling for stronger bilateral partnerships to improve healthcare access and strengthen the country's medical infrastructure. Addressing the 23rd Indo-US Economic Summit organised by the Indo-American Chamber of Commerce (IACC) in New Delhi, he highlighted the potential of combining India's pharmaceutical manufacturing capabilities and healthcare workforce with US expertise in biomedical research, technology and regulatory systems. "Indian doctors and the pharmaceutical industry have made a name for themselves across the world. I would urge the US representatives present here today and the pharmaceutical companies to come to India with your technology at affordable prices. We welcome you, and together we can work towards strengthening the healthcare sector and providing affordable facilities to our people," Dr Singh said. The discussions focused on strengthening cooperation across medicine supply chains, disease surveillance, cancer research, medical technology and patient access. Strengthening Pharmaceutical PartnershipsAddressing the session on Healthcare, Pharma and Life Sciences, Genessa Giorgi, Health Attaché and Regional Representative for South Asia at the US Embassy, highlighted the importance of strengthening pharmaceutical supply chains as a shared priority for both countries. "India plays an integral role in the global pharmaceutical supply chain and is the world's largest provider of generic medicines," Giorgi said, noting that India supplies more than 40 per cent of the generic medicines consumed in the US.She highlighted the contribution of bilateral pharmaceutical trade to access to essential medicines for chronic conditions, including diabetes, heart disease and cancer, as well as antibiotics and cancer treatments. Referring to the India-US Initiative on Critical and Emerging Technology (iCET), Giorgi said both countries were working towards strengthening supply chains and improving their resilience against future disruptions. She also highlighted the SelectUSA initiative and referred to USD 20.2 billion in investments announced by the US in May, of which USD 19.1 billion was in Indian pharmaceuticals and other sectors. Innovation, Investment And RegulationThe session also examined the role of innovation and investment in expanding healthcare capabilities. Henna Dhawan, Country Head, Public Affairs, Novartis India, said innovative medicines should be recognised for the breakthroughs they deliver rather than being assessed primarily through their costs."Healthcare is not a cost but an investment," Dhawan said.

headline: Delhi Jal Board To Monetise Karol Bagh Headquarters And Other Prime Properties Amid Mounting Financial Pressure: Report
content: The Delhi Jal Board (DJB) has reportedly approved a proposal to monetise its land and buildings to private companies in a bid to generate revenue, with officials announcing the plan today (20 November). The water utility, which serves around 27 lakh connections across the capital, will begin with its six-floor headquarters Varunalaya in Karol Bagh, followed by other prime properties. The board plans to hire a Department of Economic Affairs-empanelled financial adviser to carry out a comprehensive assessment and submit a detailed report. Initial properties identified for monetisation include the Jhandewalan office, Haiderpur Water Treatment Plant residential housing complex Varun Niketan, and Jal Vihar in Lajpat Nagar. The monetisation drive comes as the utility grapples with mounting financial pressure, with loans and interest surpassing Rs 73,000 crore. Officials pointed out that water tariffs have remained unchanged since 2018, significantly affecting the board's financial health and ability to service debt. Located in the busy commercial area of Karol Bagh, Varunalaya houses the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Engineers and board members across its three phases. Officials confirmed plans to identify additional assets for commercialisation following the initial phase. The Lajpat Nagar site includes residential properties for officers and an old pump house. headline: UGC flags 32 fake universities across India: Delhi accounts for 12, Uttar Pradesh four | Check full list
content: The University Grants Commission (UGC) has issued a fresh warning to students and parents against seeking admission to unrecognised universities, flagging 32 institutions across India that do not have the authority to award degrees. Delhi accounts for the largest share, with 12 institutions on the list, followed by Uttar Pradesh with four.The latest advisory, issued on November 17, highlights the risks of enrolling in institutions that are not recognised by India's higher education regulator. A comparison of the UGC's March 2023 and February 2026 lists shows that 18 of the 20 institutions identified in 2023 continue to feature on the latest list.The UGC's warning is particularly relevant for students preparing for university admissions, as degrees awarded by institutions without the requisite legal authority may not be recognised for higher education, government recruitment or professional purposes.Why has the UGC issued a fresh warning?The latest advisory follows directions from the Supreme Court, which asked the UGC and other regulatory bodies to publicly caution students against enrolling in unauthorised educational institutions. The court's intervention came after reports of an alleged fake medical college operating from a farmhouse in Etah, Uttar Pradesh.In its October 9 order, the Supreme Court directed the concerned authorities to issue public warnings to ensure that prospective students do not fall prey to institutions making misleading claims about their recognition status and degrees.The UGC had earlier written to state education authorities in April 2023, seeking action against institutions allegedly violating provisions of the UGC Act, 1956. Follow-up communications were sent in July, while another letter in September asked the institutions concerned to submit compliance reports within 15 days.The Education Ministry also informed Parliament in August 2026 that state governments had been asked to register FIRs and take steps to shut down unauthorised institutions.However, the presence of an institution on the latest UGC list does not, by itself, establish that it is still operating. It also does not indicate that enforcement action has not been initiated against it.UGC fake university list 2026: State-wise names of all 32 institutionsThe UGC has identified 32 institutions across 12 states and Union Territories. Delhi accounts for more than one-third of the total, with 12 institutions. Here is the complete state-wise list flagged by the commission.Delhi: 12 institutionsMountain Institute of Management & TechnologyWorld Peace of United Nations University (WPUNU)Institute of Management and EngineeringNational Institute of Management SolutionAll India Institute of Public & Physical Health Sciences (AIIPHS) State Government UniversityCommercial University LtdUnited Nations UniversityVocational UniversityADR-Centric Juridical UniversityIndian Institute of Science and EngineeringViswakarma Open University for Self-EmploymentAdhyatmik Vishwavidyalaya (Spiritual University)Uttar Pradesh: 4 institutionsGandhi Hindi Vidyapith, Prayag, AllahabadNetaji Subhash Chandra Bose University (Open University)Bhartiya Shiksha ParishadMahamaya Technical UniversityAndhra Pradesh: 2 institutionsChrist New Testament Deemed UniversityBible Open University of IndiaKarnataka: 2 institutionsGlobal Human Peace UniversitySarva Bharatiya Shiksha PeethKerala: 2 institutionsInternational Islamic University of Prophetic Medicine (IIUPM)St. John's University, Kishanattam, KeralaMaharashtra: 2 institutionsRaja Arabic University, NagpurNational Backward Krushi VidyapeethPuducherry: 2 institutionsUsha Latchumanan College of EducationSree Bodhi Academy of Higher EducationWest Bengal: 2 institutionsIndian Institute of Alternative MedicineInstitute of Alternative Medicine and ResearchRajasthan: 1 institutionRajeev Gandhi Institute of Technology & ManagementArunachal Pradesh: 1 institutionIndian Institute of Alternative MedicineHaryana: 1 institutionMagic & Art University, 308A, Dashmesh PlazaJharkhand: 1 institutionDaksha University (Vocational and Life Skill Education)Delhi accounts for the highest number of institutions on the listDelhi has 12 of the 32 institutions identified by the UGC. This is an increase from the eight institutions listed in the national capital in March 2023. All eight institutions named in the earlier list continue to feature in the latest one, while four additional institutions have been included.Uttar Pradesh ranks second, with four institutions. Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, Puducherry and West Bengal have two institutions each. Rajasthan, Arunachal Pradesh, Haryana and Jharkhand have one institution each.How can students check whether a university is recognised by the UGC?Students should verify an institution's recognition status before applying for admission or paying any fees. A university's website, advertisements, brochures or social media pages should not be treated as proof of its legitimacy.The UGC has advised students and parents to independently verify the following:UGC recognition: Check whether the university is recognised by the commission and legally authorised to award degrees.Course approval: Confirm whether the specific course or programme has the necessary regulatory approvals.Online and distance education: Students applying for online or distance-learning courses should verify that the institution has permission to offer the programme.Off-campus centres: Check whether the university is authorised to operate the particular off-campus centre from which the course is being offered.Official records: Cross-check the institution's details through the UGC and relevant regulatory authorities' official websites.Students can access the UGC's official university information and category-wise lists through its website.What happens if a student enrols in a fake university?A degree awarded by an institution that does not have the legal authority to grant recognised qualifications may not be accepted for higher education, government recruitment or other professional purposes.Students who enrol in such institutions risk losing years of study and substantial amounts paid as fees. They may also face difficulties when applying for jobs, competitive examinations or further education.The UGC's latest advisory underlines the importance of checking an institution's recognition status and the approvals applicable to a specific course before taking admission or making any payment.

headline: Delhi Jal Board plans to monetise land and buildings for revenue generation
content: In an attempt to generate revenue, the Delhi Jal Board plans to monetise its land and buildings to private companies, starting with 'Varunalay', its headquarters situated in Karol Bagh, officials said on Saturday.Delhi Jal Board (DJB) has around 27 lakh water connections across the city , however the water utility has been reeling under financial losses for the past several years."In a recent board meeting the proposal to monetise its properties including land and buildings has been approved. We plan to hire a Department of Economic Affairs-empanelled financial advisor to carry out an assessment and submit a report," an official said.To begin with, the Delhi Jal Board's land and building assets for the Jhandewalan office -- Varunalaya, Haiderpur WTP Residential housing -- Varun Niketan and Jal Vihar situated in Lajpat Nagar, will be monetised."Following this we plan to identify other assets that can also be commercialised," an official said.Located in busy commercial area of Karol Bagh the 'Varunalaya' has six floors, divided into three phases, where the DJB Chief Executive Officer, other Chief Engineers and DJB board members operate. In Lajpat Nagar, the DJB mostly has residential properties for its officers and an old pump house.Officials added that water tariffs have not been increased since 2018, which is affecting the financial health of the DJB, as loans and interest of the board have surpassed Rs 73,000 crore.

headline: Proposed Dwarka-Gurugram Metro can boost NCR connectivity, realty prospects
content: The proposed Metro corridor connecting Yashobhoomi in Dwarka Sector 25 with Rajiv Chowk in Gurugram could add a new dimension to the Delhi-NCR's urban transport network, potentially improving connectivity between two major residential and commercial centres. The corridor is among the routes proposed under the Delhi Metro's Phase V(B) expansion. Its implementation, however, remains subject to the necessary government approvals. Improved connectivity The proposed link is particularly relevant for commuters travelling between Dwarka, the Dwarka Expressway belt, and Gurugram's commercial districts. Better integration with the Metro network could offer an alternative to road-based commuting and improve access to employment centres, business districts, and social infrastructure. For the real estate sector, the proposed connectivity could influence homebuyer preferences, particularly in locations where accessibility to workplaces and established urban infrastructure is an important consideration. However, the extent of its impact will depend on the final alignment, project approvals, and implementation timeline.Also Read: Delhi Metro Pink Line commuters can check crowd levels in coaches before boarding Santosh Agarwal, Executive Director and CFO, Alpha Corp Development Limited, said infrastructure investment often plays an important role in shaping the growth of urban property markets. "Improved connectivity between Dwarka and Gurugram could strengthen the appeal of established residential locations by making daily commuting more convenient. In a mature market such as Sector 15 in Gurugram, better transport links could complement existing locational advantages and further influence homebuyer interest," he said. Dwarka Expressway region’s strategic location Ashish Tandon, Chief Business Officer, Origen Realty, said the proposed corridor could also strengthen the Dwarka Expressway micro-market's integration with the wider NCR transport network.Also Read: Delhi Metro celebrates 23 years with special run of its first train "With its strategic location between Delhi and Gurugram, the Dwarka Expressway region has seen growing infrastructure development and residential activity. Improved urban mobility, alongside planned infrastructure investments, could support the area's next phase of real estate development and make it more accessible to homebuyers," he said. Other planned Metro expansions The proposal comes against the backdrop of other planned Metro expansions across the capital. Phase V(B) includes additional corridors aimed at extending connectivity to several emerging residential and commercial areas. A draft detailed project report for the Yashobhoomi–Rajiv Chowk link was earlier reported to have outlined a proposed 20-km underground corridor with five stations. The alignment included locations such as Bijwasan, Kapashera, Udyog Vihar, and IFFCO Chowk. These details remain subject to the final project plan and approvals.Also Read: Delhi Metro to keep 10.9 lakh vehicles off roads daily by 2031: TERI study For now, the proposed corridor represents a potential addition to NCR's transport infrastructure rather than an operational Metro connection. Its eventual impact on property markets will depend on how quickly the proposal progresses from planning to execution.

headline: Global City roads to link Dwarka Expressway, Delhi-Gurgaon eway, Pataudi Road; min asks HSIIDC to work ou
content: Gurgaon: Haryana’s ambitious Global City project is set to get a third major access route. The state govt is planning to connect it directly to Delhi-Jaipur highway (NH-48) near Kherki Daula cloverleaf. The proposed link will add to the planned connectivity with Dwarka Expressway and the existing access from Pataudi Road, giving the 1,000-acre mixed-use development access to three major arterial roads and strengthening its links with Delhi, Manesar and the wider NCR.Global City — being developed around sectors 36B, 37A and 37B — is envisioned as a large integrated business and urban hub, with commercial, residential, retail and social infrastructure. The project is expected to attract large corporate establishments and investments, making external connectivity crucial to its development.Cabinet minister Rao Narbir Singh has directed Haryana State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation (HSIIDC) officials to work out the route alignment and address the hurdles in connecting Global City to NH-8. The proposed access point is located around 200 metres before the cloverleaf, where a right of way (RoW) is available. However, certain legal issues need to be resolved before work can begin, the minister said.“Global City will also be connected to the Delhi-Jaipur highway. Officials are preparing the route map for this. The process for connectivity with Dwarka Expressway has been completed and work will begin in Dec. Once the first phase is completed, the process of land allotment will also begin,” Singh said.Officials have been asked to assess the technical requirements and any land-related or other formalities involved in developing the link and submit a report. Once in place, the connection will allow traffic from Delhi-Jaipur highway to reach Global City without having to negotiate congested stretches of the city’s internal road network.Kherki Daula cloverleaf is a key interchange connecting Dwarka Expressway and Southern Peripheral Road (SPR). A direct link from NH-8 would also improve access for businesses, investors and visitors travelling from Delhi, Manesar, Rewari and Jaipur. The move comes as HSIIDC works on establishing the project’s connectivity with Dwarka Expressway. For this, a tunnel will be constructed beneath the expressway to provide direct access to Global City. The plan has been finalised and HSIIDC will make the required payment to National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) for the work. Construction is scheduled to begin in Dec, Singh said.While Pataudi Road currently provides access to the project, the Dwarka Expressway link is expected to offer a faster route towards Delhi and IGI airport. The proposed NH-8 connection will provide another important entry point from the national highway network, improving access for both passenger and commercial traffic.The focus is also on completing the internal infrastructure before the project is opened up for development by investors. Singh said around 70% of the first phase of infrastructure work had been completed. HSIIDC is spending around Rs 900 crore on this phase, which includes internal roads, water and electricity networks and underground utility infrastructure. Govt plans to take up the project in two phases. With the first phase nearing completion, the process of allotting land to investors is also expected to begin once the infrastructure work is completed, Singh said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news. headline: Delhi–Panipat–Karnal Namo Bharat corridor may reshape Haryana real estate
content: The Delhi–Panipat–Karnal Namo Bharat corridor is set to improve regional connectivity between Delhi and cities in Haryana, while potentially changing development patterns in Sonipat, Panipat and Karnal. The 136.3-km project has received land-use permission from the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) for pier construction, station development and the shifting of high-tension power lines, according to an Economic Times report. The corridor is being developed by the National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) at an estimated cost of about Rs 33,051 crore. It is targeted for completion by 2030 and will run broadly parallel to the Delhi–Ambala highway, or NH-44. Preliminary work has begun on an approximately 22-km stretch between Narela and Murthal. The project proposes 22 stations. Most are planned as elevated stations, while Kashmere Gate in Delhi and the stations in Panipat are expected to be at ground level, the report said. Trains will have a maximum design speed of 180 kmph and an operating speed of 160 kmph, with services planned at intervals of five to 10 minutes. The corridor is expected to reduce the journey from Delhi to Panipat to about one hour, compared with the current two to two-and-a-half hours by road or regular train. The journey to Karnal, currently reported to take three-and-a-half to four hours, is expected to fall to about one-and-a-half hours. These travel-time reductions could make locations outside Delhi more attractive to households seeking lower-cost housing with access to the National Capital Region. Abhay Kumar Mishra, president and chief executive of Jindal Realty, said faster public transport could support residential, commercial and mixed-use development in areas that have not reached their potential because of weak connectivity. Yashank Vasan, managing director of Royal Green Realty, said demand could increase not only for housing but also for retail, schools, healthcare and other everyday services near stations. Vinod Kumar, director and founder of Sky Byte Developers, similarly linked improved connectivity with potential demand for residential and commercial property in emerging locations such as Sonipat and Panipat.

headline: Delhi To Karnal In 90 Minutes: How Rs 33,051-Crore Namo Bharat Corridor Will Transform Connectivity
content: Delhi-NCR's connectivity with Haryana is set for a major upgrade, with the proposed Delhi-Panipat-Karnal Namo Bharat corridor receiving approval from the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI). The development brings the 136.3-km rapid rail project a step closer to reality and could change how thousands of people travel, work and choose their homes across the region. The corridor, which will be developed by the National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) at an estimated cost of Rs 33,051 crore, is targeted for completion by 2030. It will run parallel to the Delhi-Ambala highway (NH-44), connecting the national capital with important urban and industrial centres in Haryana. The project has already received clearances from the Centre and the Haryana government. NHAI has now granted land-use permission for pier construction, station development and the shifting of high-tension power lines along the route. Preliminary work has also started on an approximately 22-km stretch between Narela and Murthal. For commuters, the biggest attraction will be the reduction in travel time. A road or regular train journey from Delhi to Panipat currently takes around two to two-and-a-half hours. The Namo Bharat corridor is expected to bring this down to nearly one hour. The journey to Karnal, which can currently take three-and-a-half to four hours, is expected to fall to around 90 minutes.

headline: Haryana: 4 Officers Assigned; A Mona Sreenivas Gets Additional Charge of Rohtak
content: Haryana Transfers 3 IAS and 1 HCS Officer; A Mona Sreenivas Gets Additional Charge of Rohtak The Haryana government has ordered a minor administrative reshuffle involving three IAS officers and one HCS officer. Senior IAS officer A Mona Sreenivas has been assigned additional charge of Rohtak district, while Mukul Kumar has received an additional responsibility in the Haryana Backward Classes Commission. The Additional Deputy Commissioners of Panipat and Jhajjar have also been transferred in an exchange of postings. The Haryana government has reassigned three Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officers and one Haryana Civil Service (HCS) officer, bringing changes to district administration and key departmental responsibilities. The latest transfer orders involve additional charges for two senior IAS officers and the transfer of the Additional Deputy Commissioners (ADCs) of Panipat and Jhajjar. A Mona Sreenivas, a 2006-batch IAS officer of the Haryana cadre, has been given additional responsibility for looking after Rohtak district. She is currently serving as Resident Commissioner, Haryana Bhawan, New Delhi; Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Sonepat Metropolitan Development Authority; and Chief Administrator of the Trade Fair Authority of Haryana, New Delhi.

headline: Haryana: Couple, 22-year-old son killed as car rams into parked truck | Hindustan Times
content: Blurb: Family was travelling to Punjab for niece’s birthday; driver booked under sections of BNSA couple and their 22-year-old son from Madhya Pradesh’s Ratlam district were killed after their car rammed into a stationary truck on the Jammu-Katra Expressway near Ghilod village in Rohtak district on Friday morning.According to the police, the deceased have been identified as Karamjit Singh, 48, who was driving the car, his wife Pawandeep Kaur and their son Amarendra Singh, 22.According to preliminary information from the police, the car crashed into a truck parked in a no-parking zone on the expressway. The impact was so severe that the car got wedged underneath the truck. The police said the truck driver, identified as Gurmel Singh has been booked under relevant sections of BNS.They were rushed by ambulance to the trauma centre of the Post Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences (PGIMS), Rohtak, where doctors declared them dead.The bodies have been sent for post-mortem examination, and an investigation into the accident is underway.Ramjot Singh, a cousin of Pawandeep Kaur, said the family had been living in Ratlam for several years and was travelling to Punjab for the birthday celebrations. The couple’s younger son had stayed back in Ratlam with his grandparents.Other family members have left Ratlam for Rohtak after receiving news of the tragedy, the police said.

headline: Haryana: Farmers to start indefinite sit-in outside agriculture minister’s house | Hindustan Times
content: As farmers up the ante over their demand to raise sugarcane prices to ₹600 per quintal, the Bharatiya Kisan Union (Tikait) will begin a permanent dharna (sit-in) in front of the residence of Haryana agriculture and farmers welfare minister Shyam Singh Rana in Radaur town of Yamunanagar district from Saturday.Yamunanagar president of BKU (Tikait), Subhash Gurjar, said that the farmers would gather in Radaur town and then march toward the minister’s residence.“We will begin a permanent day-and-night dharna after erecting a tent, demanding an increase in sugarcane prices. By raising the prices of the crop by only ₹15 per kg, the government has played a cruel joke with the farmers,” he said.Union’s state president Rattan Mann said the Sanyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM) has been continuously protesting at sugar mills in every district across the state, as part of which a large gathering will be held in Jind.Mann said the morcha along with several other farmer unions who have joined hands, will gherao the chief minister’s residence in Kurukshetra on December 2 if the demands are not met.Another group of BKU, representing Charuni faction is already on a sit-in outside the Saraswati Sugar Mills in Yamunanagar since November 15.Faction’s head Gurnam Singh Charuni participated at a protest site in Ambala’s Naraingarh. He claimed that the farmers will hamper mill operations, scheduled to start from November 23 and stop harvesting.“At a government secret meeting to decide on sugarcane prices, it came to light that the farmers spend ₹455 as expenses incurred on per quintal of crop and we are being paid ₹430. We are just demanding ₹600, nothing below that,” the farmer leader said.A day after Mann’s request to join the protest, Charuni also showed interest and said the doors are open for any deliberations where five members each from both groups can meet.

headline: Soch Partners with OneConsent to Implement DPDPA Compliance and Data Privacy
content: VMPLGurugram (Haryana) [India], November 20: Soch Apparels Pvt. Ltd., a renowned Indian ethnic wear brand, has partnered with OneConsent, an AI-powered DPDP-compliant Consent Management Platform, to manage consent across its business operations. Under the collaboration, OneConsent will provide Soch with a centralized record of permissions granted by Data Principals, including customers, employees, vendors, business partners and other individuals whose personal data it processes, track each permission against its purpose, and manage updates and withdrawals as they happen.Soch interacts with different categories of Data Principals across multiple touchpoints, often involving separate permissions captured in different systems. With OneConsent, these permissions can be brought into one place, ensuring that consent is recorded against its specified purpose and that updates are reflected across channels. Every change to a Data Principal's consent will be time-stamped and logged, giving Soch a verifiable history it can rely on for internal governance and regulatory review.As part of the engagement, OneConsent will support Soch across key stages of its DPDP compliance journey, including discovery and assessment, remediation planning, integration and configuration, testing and validation, and ongoing audits and improvements.The move comes as businesses in India prepare for the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023. The DPDP Rules, 2025, notified by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) on 13 November 2025, set out a phased timeline. The latest milestone arrived on 13 November 2026, when the Data Protection Board of India (DPBI) portal launched, marking an important step toward operationalising the country's data protection framework and enabling the registration of Consent Managers. The core obligations on Consent Notices, Data Principal Rights and Breach Reporting follow on 13 May 2027, and the Act allows penalties of up to ₹250 crore for certain violations.Under the DPDPA Act, consent must be tied to a specified purpose, and managing consent must be as easy as giving it. For businesses, meeting that standard is less about the consent form and more about the systems behind it: knowing, at any given moment, what each Data Principal has agreed to, for which purpose, and whether that permission still applies.Speaking on the partnership, Soumya Chatterjee, CEO & Co-Founder, OneConsent, said, "Soch has been an integral part of Zence CRM ecosystem, enabling connected customer experiences. With OneConsent, we are extending this partnership by bringing consent compliance into the broader business ecosystem, helping Soch maintain consent continuity across applicable touchpoints while strengthening transparency, privacy, and trust. Together, we are building a more connected and responsible data management ecosystem."The partnership echoes a wider shift among Indian brands toward building consent management into everyday data operations, well ahead of the DPDP Act's compliance deadlines.About OneConsentOneConsent is an AI-powered Consent Management Platform designed to support businesses in meeting DPDPA requirements. It enables organizations to manage the consent lifecycle, including collection, tracking and withdrawal, while maintaining auditable records. The platform helps businesses translate data protection obligations into accountable operational practices.For more information, visit https://oneconsent.ai/About Soch Apparels Pvt LtdSoch Apparels Pvt Ltd represents a harmonious fusion of tradition and contemporary artistry in ethnic fashion. Founded in 2005 with its first exclusive store in Bengaluru, Soch today operates over 175 stores across 60+ cities in India. The brand offers a wide range of intricately crafted women's ethnic wear, blending traditional craftsmanship with modern aesthetics. With a dedicated team of over 1,400 members, Soch continues to deliver quality, innovation, and exceptional customer experience across its growing retail footprint.(ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by VMPL. ANI will not be responsible in any way for the content of the same.)

headline: HP High Court restricts section 118 land purchase permissions in Solan without its approval
source: Achievements of Atal Medical and Research University
content: Himachal Pradesh High Court has directed the state government not to grant any permission to purchase land under section 118 of Himachal Pradesh Land Tenancy Act-1972 to non- agriculturists in Solan district of Himachal Pradesh without the permission of the High Court. In a sue -motu order considering the matter as Public Interest Litigation (PIL) a double bench of HP High court comprising Justice Gurmeet Singh Sandhwalia and Justice Bipin Chander Negi passed these orders directing the state government to present reasons for granting such permissions. The High Court has also directed the state government to give details of all permissions given to purchase land during the last ten years in the district under section 118 of HP Land Tenancy Act-1972. The court has also asked the state government to submit details of such permissions granted in the state during the last 10 years including amended list of Shimla, Kangra, Kullu, Sirmaur and remaining areas and also submit reasons for rejecting permission under the Act. The Court observed that the spirit of the Act has been diluted during the last few years weakening the protection given to farmers of the state under the Act. The court also directed the state government to impleadment of three builders of Kasauli and town planner for violation in purchase of the land and in carrying construction of a large number of flats.

headline: Prolonged restraint violates liberty: Delhi court grants bail to man held for over 24 hours before arrest
content: New Delhi: A Delhi court has granted bail to a man accused of smuggling drone components, saying that restraining a person for more than 24 hours before a formal arrest violates the fundamental right to personal liberty and constitutional safeguards on arrest..Additional Sessions Judge Saurabh Partap Singh Laler, in an order dated November 18, granted bail to accused Shoaib Nawab Khan, who had been in judicial custody since September 27..In its order, the court said that Khan "remained under the control and restraint of the customs authorities for a period exceeding 24 hours" before his formal arrest..Supreme Court refuses to interfere with Azam Khan’s interim bail in ED case."Apprehension and brief detention for the purpose of checking baggage and completing necessary formalities immediately after landing is permissible,” the court said.."However, keeping a person under restraint from the night of arrival on the 25th till the morning of the 27th, thereby postponing the formal arrest and the consequential constitutional safeguards, is not sanctioned by law,” it added..Referring to Article 22(2) of the Constitution, which requires an arrested person to be produced before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours, the court said that the protection "attaches from the moment liberty is curtailed by restraint, and not merely from the artificial recording of formal arrest.".It further said, "The practice of detaining a person for prolonged periods under the colour of investigation or for 'rest' at the office premises, and thereafter recording formal arrest only when convenient, has the effect of circumventing the 24-hour mandate.".The court said the applicant was effectively apprehended after crossing the immigration channel on the night of September 25 but was produced before the magistrate only after formal arrest on September 27.."The delay is far in excess of what is permissible," it said..The court said that if the department was not in a position to form the requisite satisfaction under Customs Act provisions for effecting arrest after the initial interception and examination, "the proper course was to release the applicant (accused Khan) and to effect arrest subsequently, if and when the investigation so warranted."."Prolonged detention without formal arrest, while continuing to restrain liberty, is violative of the basic principle of personal liberty enshrined in Article 21 of the Constitution and of the specific safeguards under Article 22," it said..The court also rejected the customs department's argument that Khan had not been in continuous illegal custody, as he had himself submitted a written request to "rest" at the customs office and join proceedings the next morning..Noting that the request letter was a typed one merely signed by Khan, the court said, Even assuming its existence, such a request cannot legitimise the continued restraint of personal liberty for the entire night of September 25, the whole (day) of September 26 and the night of September 26 without effecting formal arrest.".Pannun murder conspiracy case: US court sentences Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months in jail.It said that the letter, "even if signed, cannot be treated as a voluntary waiver of these fundamental rights so as to permit the authorities to keep the person in de facto custody for such an extended period.".The court said that the prolonged detention without formal arrest and the delayed production before the magistrate "constitute a clear violation of Articles 21 (protection of life and personal liberty) and 22 (safeguards on arrest and detention) of the Constitution.".The customs department alleged that Khan and two others travelled from Hong Kong to Delhi via Vietnam, landing at Terminal-3 of the IGI Airport at around 11 pm on September 25..Ten Autel Robotics drones, along with remote controllers, adaptors, cables and other parts and an iPhone, were allegedly seized, with an aggregate value of over Rs 1 crore, it alleged..The prosecution alleged that from Khan's checked-in baggage, four remote controllers, ten adaptors, ten power cables and one iPhone were allegedly recovered, while the drone bodies were carried by another passenger..The prosecution claimed that the drones are military-grade UAVs whose import is prohibited..Khan's first bail plea was dismissed by a magistrate court on October 27..The court granted him bail on a personal bond of Rs one lakh along with one surety of the same amount..It clarified that its observations are "tentative and confined to the present bail application."

headline: Breaking: Amritsar School of Eminence Principal suspended
content: Amritsar (Punjab), November 21, 2026: The Punjab Education Department has suspended Jaspreet Singh, principal of the School of Eminence at Warpal in Amritsar district, over multiple allegations, including alleged irregularities in government grants and other serious charges. According to the suspension order issued by the department, the action follows allegations of financial irregularities involving school grants, financial losses reportedly caused by the cutting of trees, incidents of alleged molestation involving students and issues related to the mid-day meal scheme. The department has taken action against the principal on the basis of these allegations. Further details of the charges and the inquiry proceedings were not immediately available.

headline: Preventing meeting with Youth Congress leaders in Patiala Jail is a glaring example of Mann government's dictatorship: Pargat Singh
content: Patiala/Chandigarh, November 21, 2026: Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee President Pargat Singh strongly condemned the Bhagwant Mann government for preventing him from meeting Youth Congress leaders lodged in Patiala Central Jail, calling it a glaring example of dictatorship and blatant misuse of power. He said the Aam Aadmi Party government in Punjab has completely abandoned democratic values and has no regard for people's rights. The situation has reached a point where elected representatives of the opposition are being denied even the right to meet young political workers lodged in jail. The police and prison administration are being turned into instruments of political vendetta. Pargat Singh said he simply wanted to meet the detained youth, but the government stopped him, exposing its intolerance towards questions and dissent. Pargat Singh asked whether demanding an impartial investigation into alleged irregularities in the PCS recruitment examination was a crime. He said Youth Congress leaders were fighting for the future of hardworking young people in Punjab, but instead of answering their legitimate questions, the Mann government chose to put them behind bars. He pointed out that apart from alleged irregularities in PCS recruitment, allegations of a Rs 10,000-crore scam in GMADA and even bigger scams at Baba Farid University had also surfaced. Who will take responsibility for these scandals? Addressing Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, he said, "Listen carefully, you cannot silence the voice of Punjab's youth with police batons and prison bars. Those who have played with the future of young people through irregularities in recruitment processes will have to answer. When Congress forms the government, every layer of every scam will be exposed and nobody involved will be spared." Questioning the double standards of the AAP government, Pargat Singh said that when the ED conducted a raid in connection with the GMADA matter, AAP workers had allegedly entered the ED office and vandalised the premises. "Where was the police then? Why was no action taken against those who damaged government property? Where was Punjab's Home Minister at that time? Is the law meant only to intimidate the opposition and young people? When ruling party workers indulge in such acts, everything is forgiven, but when young people raise their voices for their rights, criminal cases are slapped against them. What kind of law and justice is this?" he asked. He said the government's conduct showed that instead of answering questions about alleged scams, it was trying to silence those raising them. Issuing a direct challenge to Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, Pargat Singh said, "Bhagwant Mann ji, register even a hundred cases against us, we are not going to be intimidated. Fighting for the rights of Punjab's youth is not a crime. If the opposition does not stand by the youth and become their voice, then what is the point of having an opposition? Your prisons and your cases cannot frighten us. We will ensure that everyone who has played with the future of Punjab's youth is held accountable." He asserted that the Congress party would continue this fight with full force, from the streets to the Assembly. The Bhagwant Mann government must stop using police intimidation and immediately release all arrested Youth Congress leaders. An impartial investigation must be conducted into the allegations of irregularities and scams involving PCS recruitment, Baba Farid University and other recruitment processes. Punjab's youth deserve justice, not prison cells and police batons. The government must remember that power is never permanent, but those who commit injustice against the people are always held accountable. MP Dr. Dharamvir Gandhi, former MLA Kuljit Singh Nagra, former minister Sadhu Singh Dharamsot, former Youth Congress President Mohit Mahindra and other Congress leaders were also present on the occasion. headline: Amritpal Singh flown to Punjab's Amritsar for grandmother's cremation, meets family members
content: Amritsar: Punjab MP and Akali Dal Waris Punjab De chief Amritpal Singh on Saturday arrived at his residence in Jallupur Khera village where he met his family members after he was flown to Amritsar from New Delhi under tight security arrangements..A court in Amritsar has granted him permission to attend his grandmother's cremation at his native village, Jallupur Khera, in Amritsar. On Friday, the MP was brought from Assam's Dibrugarh jail to Delhi..Videos and pictures appeared on social media showing the Khadoor Sahib MP entering his residence with folded hands. In a video, Singh could be seen embracing one of his relatives..Only select family members were allowed to meet Singh who was brought from the Amritsar airport to his village, Jallupur Khera, in a convoy of police vehicles. Police personnel have been deployed at his residence..Later, Singh took part in a funeral procession from the residence in a tractor trolley for the final rites of his grandmother. He was accompanied by his family members and Waris Punjab De leaders..Jailed MP Amritpal Singh to attend grandmother's cremation under tight security on Nov 21.A five-member Punjab Police team on Friday took custody of the 33-year-old MP. Singh returns to Punjab after more than three and a half years, which he has spent in a Dibrugarh jail in connection with an attack on a police station..The court on Tuesday granted Singh permission to attend the cremation for three hours on November 21. It directed the Punjab government to ensure Singh's physical presence at Jallupur Khera village from 12 noon to 3 pm on Saturday, subject to conditions laid down in its November 13 order..Punjab Police have made elaborate security arrangements in and around Jallupur Khera village. Sufficient force has been deployed to maintain law and order, a senior police officer said..Earlier, Akali Dal Waris Punjab De chief spokesperson Shamsher Singh Padhri said Singh will first be taken to his residence and from there he will be brought to the cremation ground..Arrangements have been made on eight acres of land to accommodate a large number of attendees at the cremation. Parking space has been created at four locations, besides arrangements for 'langar' for the gathering..Barricades have been erected around the cremation site to regulate the movement of people..Singh's grandmother, Charan Kaur (84), died on November 8 following prolonged illness. The Khadoor Sahib MP was granted a three-hour permission on November 14, but could not be brought to Punjab as authorities expressed their inability to make arrangements at such short notice. His legal team subsequently moved a fresh plea..Kaur's remains have been kept in Jallupur Khera village, with the family deferring the cremation until Singh could attend the last rites..The family has scheduled the cremation for November 21, the collection of ashes for November 22 and the 'bhog' ceremony for November 23..Singh has been in jail since 2023 in connection with a police station attack case..On February 23, 2023, Singh and his supporters, some of them brandishing swords and guns, stormed Ajnala police station on the outskirts of Amritsar and clashed with police while trying to secure the release of his aides detained there..He was arrested on April 23, 2023, following a month-long manhunt and subsequently detained under the National Security Act (NSA)..After his detention under the NSA ended on April 22 this year, he was arrested again on April 23 and lodged in the Dibrugarh jail..Singh contested the 2024 Lok Sabha elections as an independent candidate and won from Khadoor Sahib.

headline: Punjab Government's ₹3,200 Crore Canal Water Supply Project at Risk of Going Waste Without Proper Planning: Parveen Bansal
content: Ludhiana, November 21, 2026: BJP leader Parveen Bansal has raised serious questions over the functioning of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab regarding the ongoing project to supply canal water to Ludhiana city. He said the Central Government had provided funds amounting to approximately ₹3,200 crore for Ludhiana to promote the use of canal water and raise the groundwater level. While the Mayor has been claiming that more than 50 per cent of the project work has been completed, the ground reality appears to be quite different from these claims. Parveen Bansal said that large water storage tanks were being constructed across the city, but the essential infrastructure and pipeline network required for proper water distribution were still incomplete. More concerningly, the tanks were also being constructed without a concrete plan or proper assessment of actual requirements. Citing an example, he said that six water storage tanks were being constructed within a radius of approximately 100 metres near Salem Tabri. The question is how water will reach distant wards of the city when so many tanks are being constructed in the same area. Have the authorities conducted any technical survey taking into account water pressure, pipeline capacity and the requirements of different localities? He said that this was not a particularly complicated issue. Even an ordinary person could understand that the location and capacity of water tanks, along with the pipeline network, must be planned according to the requirements of the entire city to ensure proper water distribution. Unfortunately, under political pressure, officials appear to be prioritising agreement with political leaders rather than offering their independent technical opinions. Expressing concern, Parveen Bansal said that just as people had failed to get the expected results despite an expenditure of approximately ₹650 crore in the name of cleaning and beautifying the Buddha Nullah, the important ₹3,200 crore canal water supply project also faces the risk of going waste in the absence of proper planning. He said that taxpayers' hard-earned money and public funds should not be spent under political pressure, for private interests or on the basis of incomplete understanding. Instead, expenditure must be guided by expert advice and comprehensive planning. He further said that the Central Government was continuously providing new schemes and funds for the development of Punjab. However, due to what he described as the irresponsible functioning of the present AAP government in the state, the full benefits of these schemes were not reaching the people of Punjab. Parveen Bansal demanded that: • A technical assessment should be conducted of the locations and actual requirements of all water storage tanks being constructed in Ludhiana. • The master plan for the city's entire water supply system should be made public. • The pipeline network, water pressure and capacity to supply water to distant wards should be thoroughly examined. • Complete details of the project's current progress and expenditure should be presented before the public. • Necessary modifications should be made on the advice of experts before any further wastage of public funds takes place. He appealed to the residents of Ludhiana to unite and demand accountability from the government to protect the interests of the city and Punjab. He said that Punjab's money should be spent on the development of the state rather than being wasted due to wrong decisions. He said, "Let us come together to safeguard the interests of Punjab and build a new, prosperous and developed Punjab." headline: KLK Ventures secures 500 kW solar project in Himachal Pradesh
content: Himachal Pradesh Energy Development Agency (HIMURJA) has awarded KLK Ventures, a contract for a 500-kW ground-mounted solar power project at Pargod (Shahpur) in Kangra district, Himachal Pradesh. The contract covers design, engineering, manufacturing, supply, installation, and commissioning of the project. KLK Ventures will hand over the facility to HIMURJA following completion of all work and achievement of the Commercial Operation Date (COD). The agreement includes a comprehensive five-year warranty period. CEO Akshat Jain said the company will focus on engineering, timely delivery, and operational efficiency while contributing to Himachal Pradesh's renewable energy objectives .

headline: Bulldozers, chainsaws and ‘parkification’: What’s happening to Delhi’s Central Ridge
content: It's almost a miracle that a sprawling forest exists in the heart of Delhi. Often called the “green lungs of Delhi”, the Central Ridge is an important source of biodiversity in a city increasingly swallowed by urbanisation and smoke. But this forest, tucked away behind Rashtrapati Bhawan, now faces a different kind of threat. According to environmentalist and filmmaker Pradip Krishen, it comes from the government's own intervention. Newslaundry met the author of Trees of Delhi: A Field Guide a week before Diwali to understand what is happening to the forest. The sound of a chainsaw accompanied our conversation for nearly two hours. As we began our morning walk through Budh Jayanti Park, we spotted a JCB standing idle. By the end of our interview, it was at work. Its driver and assistants told us they had been tasked with removing two invasive species: Vilayati Keekar and Subabul. Both grow rapidly and inhibit the growth of other species. The government’s stated aim, then, is forest restoration. But for Krishen, the concern is less about what the forest department is removing than how it is going about it. Instead of being removed individually, the trees are being cleared with a bulldozer. The one we saw in action drove over the forest floor, tearing out not just invasive trees but also other vegetation in its path. The government is also attempting what Krishen calls “parkification” of the Ridge. Watch our interview to understand what this means for Delhi’s forests.
